title: विशाखापत्तनम में ब्रिक्स के युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक संपन्न; संयुक्त वक्तव्य अपनाया गया
content:
युवा कार्यक्रम एवं खेल मंत्रालय 
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    विशाखापत्तनम में ब्रिक्स के युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक संपन्न; संयुक्त वक्तव्य अपनाया गया
                              
                              
                                    
ब्रिक्स के युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक में भारतीय प्रतिनिधिमंडल का नेतृत्व डॉ.मनसुख मांडविया और श्रीमती रक्षा निखिल खडसे ने किया
ब्रिक्स देशों के युवा कार्य मंत्रियों ने विकास कार्यों में युवाओं के  सहयोग और भागीदारी को मजबूत करने के संयुक्त वक्तव्य को अपनाया
बैठक गांधीनगर में आयोजित ब्रिक्स युवा शिखर सम्मेलन और ब्रिक्स युवा परिषद की बैठक के परिणामों पर आधारित
प्रतिनिधियों ने 'एक पेड़ मां के नाम' वृक्षारोपण अभियान में भाग लिया और ऐतिहासिक तोतलाकोंडा बौद्ध मठ का दौरा किया
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        भारत सरकार के युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल मंत्रालय के युवा कार्य विभाग द्वारा आयोजित ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक शनिवार, 22 अगस्त, 2026 को विशाखापत्तनम में सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न हुई।
इस बैठक की अध्यक्षता माननीय केंद्रीय युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल मंत्री डॉ. मनसुख मांडविया ने की। उनके साथ माननीय युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल राज्य मंत्री श्रीमती रक्षा निखिल खडसे और युवा कार्यक्रम विभाग के सचिव श्री सुनील पालीवाल भी उपस्थित थे।
मंत्रियों की बैठक में हुई चर्चाएं ब्रिक्स युवा शिखर सम्मेलन और ब्रिक्स युवा परिषद की बैठक के परिणामों पर आधारित थीं। इन आयोजनों में प्राप्त हुई सिफारिशों और विचारों से युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की चर्चा के लिए महत्वपूर्ण आधार तैयार हुआ।
माननीय केंद्रीय युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल मंत्री डॉ. मनसुख मांडविया ने प्रतिनिधियों को संबोधित करते हुए कहा, "माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में, हमने 2047 के लिए एक विज़न डॉक्यूमेंट तैयार किया है, जब भारत अपनी आज़ादी के 100 वर्ष पूरे करेगा। प्रधानमंत्री ने इस विज़न को साकार करने की दिशा में देश का नेतृत्व करने के लिए बिना किसी राजनीतिक पृष्ठभूमि वाले 1,00,000 युवा नेता तैयार करने का आह्वान किया है।"
डॉ. मांडविया ने कहा, "इसलिए, हमने इसी भावना के साथ कई पहल शुरू की हैं। हमने स्वयंसेवा, सीखने, नेतृत्व और नागरिक भागीदारी के लिए ‘माय भारत’ नाम का एक वन-स्टॉप प्लेटफॉर्म बनाया है। इस समय 25 मिलियन से अधिक युवा इस प्लेटफॉर्म पर पंजीकरण करा चुके हैं और इसमें सक्रिय रूप से भागीदारी कर रहे हैं।"
इन कार्यक्रमों में ब्रिक्स के सदस्य और सहयोगी देशों के युवा प्रतिनिधि, युवा नेता, नीति-निर्माता और वरिष्ठ अधिकारी एक जुट हुए। इससे युवाओं के आवश्यक मुद्दों पर बातचीत करने, अनुभव साझा करने और मिलकर काम करने के लिए मंच उपलब्ध हुआ।
माननीय युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल मंत्री ने बेहतर भविष्य बनाने के लिए युवाओं के साथ मिलकर काम करने की ज़रूरत पर ज़ोर दिया। उन्होंने कहा, "भारत की ब्रिक्स अध्यक्षता के दौरान हमारा दृष्टिकोण स्पष्ट रहा है कि युवाओं को केवल लाभ पाने वाले के तौर पर नहीं, बल्कि हमारे साझा भविष्य को बनाने में सक्रिय साझेदार के रूप में देखा जाना चाहिए। आइए, हम युवाओं की भागीदारी से आगे बढ़कर युवाओं के साथ साझेदारी की ओर बढ़ें,विचार-विमर्श से आगे बढ़कर मिलकर कुछ नया बनाने की ओर, युवाओं के लिए कार्यक्रम बनाने से आगे बढ़कर युवाओं के साथ मिलकर मंच तैयार करने की ओर बढ़े। आइए, हम सब मिलकर एक ऐसा ब्रिक्स बनाएं, जहां युवा केवल भविष्य की तैयारी न कर रहे हों, बल्कि उसे सक्रिय रूप से आकार दे रहे हों।"
ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक के अवसर पर ब्रिक्स के सदस्य देशों के प्रतिनिधियों ने 'एक पेड़ मां के नाम' नामक एक विशेष वृक्षारोपण कार्यक्रम में भाग लिया, जिसमें प्रत्येक प्रतिनिधि ने अपनी-अपनी माताओं के सम्मान में एक पौधा लगाया। इस भाव को व्यापक रूप से सराहा गया और इसे कृतज्ञता की एक प्रतीकात्मक और हार्दिक अभिव्यक्ति माना गया।
प्रतिनिधियों ने विशाखापत्तनम के आस-पास के महत्वपूर्ण धरोहर स्थलों में से एक, ऐतिहासिक तोतलाकोंडा बौद्ध मठ का भी दौरा किया। इस दौरे से प्रतिनिधियों को भारत की समृद्ध सभ्यतागत विरासत और शांति, सद्भाव और सांस्कृतिक आदान-प्रदान की पुरानी परंपराओं के बारे में विशेष जानकारी मिली। मेहमानों ने इसे बहुत पसंद किया। इसने पूरे कार्यक्रम में एक समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक पहलू जोड़ा और ब्रिक्स देशों के युवाओं के बीच मित्रता और आपसी समझ के रिश्तों को और मज़बूत किया।
19 और 20 अगस्त, 2026 को गुजरात के गांधीनगर में आयोजित ब्रिक्स युवा शिखर सम्मेलन और ब्रिक्स युवा परिषद की बैठक के बाद, ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक युवाओं से जुड़ी गतिविधियों का समापन कार्यक्रम थी। इस बैठक में ब्रिक्स के सदस्य देशों के युवा कार्य के लिए उत्तरदायी मंत्री और वरिष्ठ अधिकारी शामिल हुए। उन्होंने युवाओं के बीच सहयोग में हुई प्रगति की समीक्षा की, नीतिगत दृष्टिकोणों का आदान-प्रदान किया और टिकाऊ व समावेशी विकास में युवाओं की भूमिका को और बढ़ाने की प्राथमिकताओं पर चर्चा की।
ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक का एक मुख्य परिणाम संयुक्त वक्तव्य को अपनाना था। यह वक्तव्य युवाओं के बीच सहयोग को मजबूत करने और विकास प्रक्रियाओं में युवाओं की सार्थक भागीदारी को बढ़ावा देने के प्रति ब्रिक्स देशों की साझा प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाता है। संयुक्त वक्तव्य  में शिक्षा, प्रशिक्षण और कौशल, युवा उद्यमिता, विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी और नवाचार, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक भागीदारी, समाज सेवा और स्वयंसेवा,विकास, गरीबी, भुखमरी और असमानताओं से निपटना,स्वास्थ्य, युवा और खेल, युवा, पर्यावरण और स्थिरता, अंतर-धार्मिक युवा संवाद,युवा आदान-प्रदान और इनमें युवाओं को शामिल करने के महत्व के बारे में बताया गया है।
मंत्रियों की बैठक में चर्चा के मुख्य विषयों में से एक था युवाओं के लिए ऐसा माहौल बनाना जिससे वे अपनी क्षमताएं विकसित कर सकें, निर्णय लेने की प्रक्रिया में सार्थक रूप से शामिल हो सकें और युवाओं से जुड़े मौजूदा मुद्दों का समाधान करने में योगदान दे सकें। उन्होंने युवाओं के नेतृत्व वाली पहलों को मज़बूत करने, नवाचार और उद्यमिता को बढ़ावा देने तथा साझा हितों के मुद्दों पर विचार-विमर्श के ज़रिए युवाओं के बीच सीमा-पार सहयोग के अवसर बढ़ाने के महत्व पर भी ज़ोर दिया।
ब्रिक्स  युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक का सफल समापन और ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों के संयुक्त वक्तव्य को अपनाना, ब्रिक्स  देशों के बीच युवा सहयोग को आगे बढ़ाने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि है।
ब्रिक्स युवा कार्यक्रमों से साझेदारियों सुदृढ़ हुई हैं, आपसी समझ बढ़ी है और ब्रिक्स  के युवाओं और संस्थानों के बीच निरंतर सहयोग के मार्ग खुले हैं।
भारत की 2026 की ब्रिक्स अध्यक्षता के तहत, युवाओं से जुड़े कार्यक्रमों का उदे्श्य युवाओं के बीच सहयोग को मज़बूत करना रहा है। इसमें बेहतर तौर-तरीकों के आदान-प्रदान, राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकताओं और मिलकर काम करने पर ज़ोर दिया गया है। यह सब भारत की 2026 की ब्रिक्स अध्यक्षता की मुख्य थीम – "लचीलेपन, नवाचार, सहयोग और स्थिरता के लिए निर्माण"  के अनुरूप है।
भारत की 2026 की ब्रिक्स अध्यक्षता के दौरान ब्रिक्स युवा गतिविधियों के कैलेंडर के तहत ब्रिक्स युवा शिखर सम्मेलन, ब्रिक्स युवा परिषद की बैठक और ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक आयोजित की गई थी।  इसी क्रम में  22 अगस्त, 2026 को आंध्र प्रदेश के विशाखापत्तनम में ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न हुई।
जैसे-जैसे भारत की ब्रिक्स अध्यक्षता अपनी समाप्ति की ओर बढ़ रही है, इन वार्ताओं के परिणाम निरंतर सहयोग के लिए एक मजबूत आधार प्रदान करते हैं और एक अधिक लचीला, नवाचार, समावेशी और टिकाऊ भविष्य के निर्माण में युवाओं की क्षमता का उपयोग करने के लिए ब्रिक्स देशों की साझा प्रतिबद्धता की पुष्टि करते हैं।
ब्रिक्स युवा कार्य मंत्रियों की बैठक के अवसर पर डॉ. मनसुख मांडविया ने दक्षिण अफ्रीका और संयुक्त अरब अमीरात के अपने समकक्षों के साथ द्विपक्षीय बैठकें भी कीं। चर्चाओं में युवा कार्यक्रम और खेल के क्षेत्र में द्विपक्षीय सहयोग सुदृढ़ करने पर ध्यान दिया गया, जिसमें कौशल विकास, युवा उद्यमिता और युवा सहभागिता के लिए डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म जैसे मुद्दों पर जोर दिया गया।
सभी पक्षों ने युवा और खेल के क्षेत्रों में भारत और संबंधित देशों के बीच संबंधों को और मज़बूत करने के लिए आदान-प्रदान कार्यक्रम, क्षमता-निर्माण की पहल और संस्थागत ढांचे के ज़रिए घनिष्ठ  सहयोग के तरीकों पर विचार–विमर्श किया।

title: Walmart to roll out Apple Pay, other contactless payment options, at all US stores from Aug 24
content:
Ending a long-standing holdout, Walmart announced on Friday that it will roll out widespread contactless payment options—most notably Apple Pay—across its operations.
This rollout is part of the world's largest retailer's initiative to streamline the shopping experience and increase convenience for consumers, Bloomberg reported.
The new payment methods will be integrated across all of Walmart's physical stores by the end of the year, as well as on its websites and mobile applications.
For years, Walmart has been one of the most prominent retail holdouts resisting third-party contactless payments.
Previously, the only way shoppers could use contactless checkout at Walmart was through the retailer's own proprietary system, Walmart Pay, which required using the Walmart app.
As “tap-to-pay” via phones or enabled credit cards became ubiquitous across the retail landscape, Walmart's refusal to accept Apple Pay caused noticeable frustration among its customers.
By allowing customers to tap their devices or cards at electronic terminals, Walmart aims to significantly reduce checkout times.
Bloomberg said the integration of the new payment systems will happen in phases. The initial rollout will begin at select Walmart and Sam’s Club locations on Monday, August 24.
The new contactless payment options, including Apple Pay, will be available at all stores by the end of the year and at gas stations by mid next year.
By mid-next year, Bloomberg said, the payment options will expand to include Walmart-operated gas stations.
The announcement arrives on the heels of a challenging quarter for the Bentonville, Arkansas-based retailer.
On Thursday, Walmart reported a rare earnings miss, marking its slowest US comparable sales growth in over six years. The company attributed this sluggish performance primarily to pricing pressures within its pharmacy division.
In response to changing consumer habits, Walmart has spent recent years heavily expanding its e-commerce footprint and investing in faster delivery networks to remain competitive and appeal to shoppers prioritising convenience.
Walmart’s head of communications is stepping down early next year, Bloomberg said, adding that the retailer will look for a replacement externally.
Chief Communications Officer Allyson Park, who has been at Walmart for more than three years, will transition to an advisory role starting 1 September, according to a memo viewed by Bloomberg News. She’ll depart the company on 1 February.
Park, who has also worked at Yum! Brands Inc. and Mars Inc, integrated the communications department more effectively with other divisions, according to the memo.
During her tenure, Walmart has invested in new hires for the team and applied AI more frequently. She also led the company’s communications strategy during last year’s transition of the chief executive officer, when John Furner replaced Doug McMillon.

title: Trump's 50% Canada tariffs kick in: Whisky, alcohol, dairy, motorcycles and more affected | Check list
content:
The Trump administration has slapped new tariffs on some popular Canadian goods, effective from Saturday, marking the latest salvo in his trade war with America's northern neighbour as his feud with Prime Minister Mark Carney expands. US President Donald Trump had announced the latest round of tariffs last month, saying they were intended to "offset Canadian discrimination" against American cars, dairy products and alcohol. US and Canadian officials had spent days negotiating an agreement aimed at preventing the tariffs from taking effect. Earlier in the week, Trump said in a Truth Social post that the two sides were close to reaching a deal. The latest US tariffs came into force at 12:01 am on Saturday, covering a broad range of Canadian products. The affected goods include alcoholic drinks, dairy products and hockey equipment, among several other items, according to a Business Insider report. Here are some of the well-known Canadian products that could become more expensive in the US. Beer, wine and spirits are among the products covered by the tariffs, including Canadian whisky, one of the most popular alcoholic drinks imported by the US from Canada. Popular Canadian whisky brands such as Crown Royal, Canadian Club and Black Velvet could be affected by the new duties. Crystal Head Vodka, known for its distinctive skull-shaped bottle, is also produced in Canada and could face the tariffs. Fireball Cinnamon Whisky is an American product but uses Canadian whisky, meaning it could potentially be affected indirectly. The dispute over alcohol between the two countries intensified last year after Trump introduced his first round of tariffs. In response, several Canadian provinces removed US-made alcoholic drinks from their shelves. Hockey equipment, including sticks and gloves, is also included in the list of products covered by the tariffs. Canadian-based brands such as Bauer Hockey, CCM Hockey and Sherwood are among the major names in the industry. However, products made by these companies will not necessarily be subject to the new duties. Some Canadian hockey brands manufacture their equipment in countries such as China and Vietnam, meaning those products may not fall under the tariffs. Sherwood, for instance, says some of its wooden hockey sticks are manufactured in Canada. Those products could therefore be affected. The tariffs also cover several dairy items, including milk, cream and powdered dairy products. Cheese, however, does not appear on the affected list. This is despite Trump citing Canada's treatment of US-made cheese as one of the reasons for imposing the tariffs. The tariffs extend well beyond food and sports equipment. The long list of affected Canadian goods also includes motorcycles, honey, clothing, plants, essential oils and dog leashes. Construction materials, paper, smartphones and a range of other products are also included, meaning the impact could extend to several areas of everyday consumption. Meanwhile, Carney said Canada will apply dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on US imports on September 8. “We take this step reluctantly,” Carney said Saturday, “because we recognize that it will raise costs and reduce choice for Canadians,” that it will hit innocent US companies and states, and prevent the two countries from working together. Carney, in a statement, said Canada would respond with tariffs on US goods "dollar for dollar" to protect Canadian workers and businesses. He said the retaliatory import taxes will be concentrated on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, with more details to be published in the coming days. title: Panama-flagged cargo ship with mostly Chinese crew sinks off Odisha's Paradip coast
content:
A Panama-flagged cargo vessel carrying iron ore from Odisha to Singapore sank in the Bay of Bengal on Saturday, around 240 nautical miles off the Paradip coast, officials told news agency PTI.
Cargo ship sinks in Bay of Bengal; search on for missing crew
The ship, identified as MV Ocean Winner, had 24 crew members on board. Two have been rescued so far, while search teams are looking for the remaining 22.
"The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy have launched a rescue operation. So far, two persons have been rescued from the waters," a senior IPS officer told PTI.
The vessel had left the Odisha coast on Friday and was headed for Singapore with a consignment of iron ore. It lost communication with its base before sinking, triggering a major search and rescue operation involving the Indian Coast Guard and the Indian Navy.
The Coast Guard said the crew comprised 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.
The ship went down far from the coast. Other vessels in the area have been alerted and asked to help with the search.
Officials are now trying to locate the missing crew members and establish their positions. But the circumstances that led to the vessel losing communication and sinking are still unclear.
There has been no immediate word on what went wrong aboard MV Ocean Winner. Authorities have not said whether the vessel sent out a distress signal before contact was lost. The search operation is continuing in the Bay of Bengal.
PTI also cited an unnamed police officer as saying that “authorities were initially unsure how many crew members had been rescued”. Officials later confirmed that two people had been pulled from the waters.
No further details about their condition were immediately available.
The incident has brought together the Coast Guard and Navy for what is likely to be a difficult search, given the vessel's distance from the shore. Ships operating nearby have also been asked to remain alert and assist if required.
The priority, for now, is finding the 22 crew members who remain missing. The cause of the sinking has not yet been established, and more details are expected as the rescue operation continues.

title: Canada to impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods from September 8; Carney vows 'dollar-for-dollar' response
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Saturday said Canada will impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods from September 8, after trade talks aimed at averting new punitive US tariffs collapsed on Friday. Details of the measures will be announced in the coming days, Carney said, Reuters reported. "In the coming days, we'll release details of these new tariff measures, measures which will come into force the Tuesday after Labor Day," Carney told a news conference. The statement came as Canada suspended trade negotiations with the United States on Friday after Carney said last-minute changes to Washington's proposed terms were "unfair" and "uneconomic". Carney also directed Canada's negotiators to return to Ottawa, saying the government would not accept a trade agreement "at any price or on any deadline". The decision came hours before the US was set to impose an additional 50% tariff on Canadian goods. Carney in a statement said Canada would respond with tariffs on US goods "dollar for dollar" to protect Canadian workers and businesses. The tariffs are expected to affect roughly $20 billion of Canadian exports, including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing equipment and hockey equipment, CNBC reported. Canada had entered the negotiations seeking to preserve tariff-free access to the US for most Canadian businesses, reduce tariffs on strategic industries and provide greater certainty for businesses and workers. Carney said the two sides had made progress in recent weeks but that it had fallen short of Canada's objectives. "Last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal," Carney said in his statement. He said Canada's objective throughout the negotiations had been to secure the best deal for Canadians, rather than reach an agreement simply because of a deadline. The talks had appeared close to a breakthrough earlier in the week. US President Donald Trump had postponed the original Wednesday tariff deadline, saying a deal was close to being finalised. Canada's trade minister Dominic LeBlanc also said on Thursday that the two sides were "very close", CNBC reported. Carney said the US intended to impose the new tariffs at midnight and that Canada would match them "dollar for dollar". The Canadian government will also introduce additional measures to support businesses and workers affected by the trade dispute, building on nearly $25 billion in support provided over the past 18 months, according to Carney's statement. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer offered a different account of why the talks failed. In a post on X early Saturday, Greer said Canada had declined to finalise the deal under terms agreed earlier in the week. Greer said Washington had offered Canada significant tariff reductions on steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber, but accused Ottawa of continuing retaliatory measures against US goods and services. The collapse of the negotiations comes as Canada seeks to reduce its economic dependence on the United States. Carney said his government had been working to strengthen the domestic economy and diversify Canada's international partnerships since taking office. Canada's existing free trade agreements provide preferential access to 1.5 billion consumers, and the government expects to double that market access by the end of the year, he said. The country is also advancing nearly $500 billion in major infrastructure projects, while exports to non-US markets are expected to double over the next decade, according to Carney. He said Canada's economy was accelerating and was on course to record the second-fastest growth in the G7 over the next two years. The prime minister has previously argued that Canada cannot return to its old economic relationship with the US. The New York Times reported that Carney has been pursuing partnerships in Asia and Europe as part of a longer-term effort to reduce Canada's dependence on its southern neighbour. Canada is particularly exposed to the trade dispute because of its close economic integration with the US. The breakdown therefore carries major risks for Canadian businesses and workers, even as Carney seeks to diversify the country's trade relationships. At the same time, Carney's decision has received support from several Canadian provincial leaders. Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed the move, while British Columbia Premier David Eby said Canada would continue fighting. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, however, urged Carney to return to the negotiating table, while Canadian industry has expressed concern over the prolonged uncertainty created by the trade conflict, the New York Times reported. The latest breakdown also adds another complication to negotiations over the USMCA, the trade agreement covering the US, Canada and Mexico. For Carney, the decision represents a significant gamble: accept a deal that he believes falls short of Canada's interests or absorb the economic cost of another round of US tariffs while pursuing a more independent trade strategy. "We will not allow any nation to determine our future," Carney said. title: Trump's 75-country immigration visa ban struck down by New York judge — ‘Contrary to law’
content:
The Trump administration's policy suspending the processing of visas from 75 countries, including Afghanistan, Iran, Russia and Somalia, has been struck down by a federal judge in New York on Friday.
The Trump administration issued a policy to suspend visas for nationals it deemed likely to require public assistance in the United States.
US District Judge Jeannette Vargas, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, set aside the policy as "contrary to law and in excess of statutory authority."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio exceeded his authority by issuing the policy, which "runs afoul" of the Immigration and Nationality Act by mandating "the refusal of visas to eligible applicants without any basis in law," the judge ruled.
Vargas said the policy also undermines the congressional requirement that puts consular officers at the forefront of any visa decision.
"Congress imbued these officers with exclusive authority and discretion to determine if an immigrant is eligible for a visa based upon review of specific and detailed criteria set forth in the statute," she wrote. “The Policy, which categorically prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of the applicant, represents a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme.”
The policy was challenged by two nonprofit organisations along with 11 individuals, including six whose family members had been refused visas. The remaining five are outside the country and had filed "employment-based petitions" to come to the United States.
"We welcome this ruling because, at its heart, this case is about keeping families together," said Anna Gallagher, the executive director of CLINIC, a national nonprofit that provides training, resources, and support to a network of immigration legal service providers and was one of the plaintiffs.
"Catholic social teaching calls us to uphold the dignity of every person and recognise the family as the foundation of society," she said in a statement. "This decision affirms both those values and the rule of law, allowing families to once again move forward toward reunification."
US President Donald Trump had imposed a growing list of immigration and travel bans, mostly for people from Africa, Asia and Latin America.
On Saturday, the State Department said that the Trump administration is "protecting the American people by upholding the highest standards of screening and vetting of visa applicants," and that it would not comment on pending litigation.
At the time the policy was issued, the department said it had instructed consular officers to halt immigrant visa applications from the 75 countries in accordance with a broader order in November that tightened rules around potential immigrants who might become "public charges."
Citing data from the Council of Economic Advisers, the State Department said that more than 30 per cent of households with immigrants from these countries received some form of public assistance.
A separate notice sent to all US embassies and consulates said that non-immigrant visa applicants also should be "fully vetted and screened" for the possibility that they might seek public benefits in the United States.
The ruling is the latest example of the courts upending Trump's immigration agenda.
In June, a federal judge struck down a Trump administration policy that made it harder for immigrants from dozens of countries to enter and remain in America, affecting areas such as asylum, work permits, green cards, and citizenship applications.
The judge said the policy threw countless immigrants' lives "into indeterminate legal limbo," and accused the US Citizenship and Immigration Services of ignoring the law.

title: PM Modi meets BJP’s new national team after party slams CWC over ‘Vande Mataram’ resolution
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday met the BJP’s newly appointed national office-bearers at the party headquarters in New Delhi and posed for a group photograph with them.
Modi’s visit came after the BJP adopted a resolution highlighting the historical significance and legacy of ‘Vande Mataram’. The party also announced a nationwide campaign to spread awareness about the National Song’s history and importance.
In its resolution, the BJP strongly slammed the Congress Working Committee (CWC) for re-adopting its 1937 decision to limit the singing of ‘Vande Mataram’ at party programmes to its first two stanzas.
The BJP said it regards 'Vande Mataram' as India's National Song, an expression of reverence for Bharat Mata, a mantra of the freedom struggle and an enduring symbol of India's national consciousness.
The party stated it would strongly oppose the Congress decision to limit the National Song to two stanzas and would protect the honour, dignity and legacy of its full six-stanza version.
The BJP also said it would reaffirm the 1950 Constituent Assembly declaration and the law passed by Parliament in 2026 granting statutory protection to the National Song at par with 'Jana Gana Mana'.
The BJP resolution argued that the CWC's decision could not take precedence over the Constitution or laws enacted by Parliament. It said the political understanding reached in 1937 could not override the constitutional framework established in 1950 or the legislation passed in 2026.
As part of its nationwide campaign, the BJP said it would focus on the historical background of ‘Vande Mataram’ and its contribution to India’s freedom movement. The party will also conduct a dedicated awareness programme for young people to familiarise them with the National Song’s links to the freedom struggle and the sacrifices made during it.
The BJP said it would resist any effort to place the National Song under communal considerations, appeasement or vote-bank politics.
In its resolution, the party referred to Mahatma Gandhi’s characterisation of ‘Vande Mataram’ as an “anti-imperialist slogan” associated with the “purest national sentiment”.
CWC reaffirms its 1937 resolution
The CWC had earlier reaffirmed its 1937 decision to restrict the singing of ‘Vande Mataram’ at party events to its first two stanzas.
Congress MP KC Venugopal said the party’s stance remained unchanged and that it would adhere to the decisions taken by Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in 1937.
The BJP, meanwhile, has stated that the matter is about preserving the dignity of the National Song and honouring the contributions of those who took part in India’s freedom movement.

title: Meghan Markle’s acting comeback? Duchess of Sussex in talks for The Gentlemen Season 3
content:
Meghan Markle is in talks to join the third season of Netflix's The Gentlemen, according to Variety, in what could become her most significant acting role since she stepped away from the profession after marrying Prince Harry.
The Duchess of Sussex is said to be in very early discussions for a role in the Guy Ritchie-created crime series, with no contract currently in place. Her potential character has also not been identified. The series itself has not yet been officially renewed for a third season.
The Gentlemen stars Theo James as Eddie Horniman, an aristocrat and former British Army officer who unexpectedly inherits his family's sprawling estate following his father's death. He soon discovers that the property is at the centre of a major underground cannabis operation, drawing him into the criminal world.
The first season, released in 2024, became a successful Netflix title and expanded the world established by Ritchie's 2019 film of the same name. Its eight-episode story combined British aristocracy, organised crime and dark comedy, with James joined by Kaya Scodelario, Daniel Ings, Joely Richardson and Vinnie Jones. Netflix describes the series as a mix of crime, action, comedy and dramedy.
Season 2 is due to premiere on September 3. The new instalment follows Eddie and Susie Glass, played by Scodelario, as their criminal enterprise expands. The returning cast is joined by Hugh Bonneville, Benjamin Clementine, Benedetta Porcaroli, Amra Mallassi and Maya Jama, among others.
For Markle, the possible role would represent a return to the kind of scripted television work that established her public profile. She is best known for playing Rachel Zane on the legal drama Suits, appearing across seven seasons from 2011 to 2018. Before that, her credits included guest roles on shows such as Fringe and CSI: NY, alongside film appearances including Remember Me and Horrible Bosses.
Her acting career largely ended after she married Prince Harry in 2018 and became a working member of the British royal family. The couple later stepped back from royal duties and moved to California, where they established Archewell Productions and began developing projects for Netflix.
That relationship with the streamer could make The Gentlemen a natural fit. Markle and Harry's Archewell Productions already has a deal with Netflix, through which they have produced projects including Harry & Meghan, Heart of Invictus and Markle's lifestyle series With Love, Meghan.
Markle has nevertheless remained connected to the entertainment industry. In 2026, she made a cameo as herself in Amazon MGM's Close Personal Friends, marking her first acting appearance in more than seven years. She has also spoken about her continued interest in creative work. In a recent Variety interview, she described the return as an opportunity to “explore and play and have fun."
The latest development comes shortly after news that Markle and Prince Harry are moving back to the UK with their two children for an “extended period” after six years in California. Their representatives and Netflix have declined to comment on the reported discussions about The Gentlemen.
For now, Markle's involvement remains at the discussion stage, with no deal confirmed and no third season of The Gentlemen officially announced.

title: Stalin announces major DMK overhaul with age caps, 2-term limits and focus on young blood
content:
The DMK on Saturday approved a major organisational overhaul, introducing age caps and two-term limits for party posts and expanding its organisational districts from 78 to 110 following its electoral setback in the April 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, PTI reported. The party's executive committee, chaired by DMK president M K Stalin at the party headquarters Anna Arivalayam, passed nine resolutions aimed at restructuring the organisation. Under the new structure, each of the 110 organisational districts will broadly cover two assembly constituencies. The move is aimed at creating more localised administration, according to the report. The party will also abolish the standalone "city secretary" post in major urban centres such as Coimbatore and Tambaram. Urban areas will instead be reorganised based on voter density. Chennai Corporation Area Committees will have an average of 40,000 voters, while committees in other corporations will have around 30,000 voters. Once Stalin formally releases the boundary maps for the revamped districts, district executive committees will have to meet within 15 days under the supervision of the party headquarters to implement the changes. The restructuring introduces age limits for several organisational positions. The maximum age for a branch secretary has been fixed at 45 years, while ward committee secretaries in municipalities, corporations and town panchayats will have an upper age limit of 50 years. The maximum age for town panchayat committee secretaries has been fixed at 60 years, while the cap for district secretaries will be 70 years. All these posts will be limited to two terms. According to party sources cited by PTI, the changes are expected to reduce the territorial powers of the existing 77 district secretaries and shorten their tenure. Nearly 10 to 13 district secretaries could be affected by the age cap, with the party likely to move some of them to non-administrative state-level or zonal-level roles, the sources said. Addressing party functionaries, Stalin said the DMK had lost an election but had not suffered a permanent defeat. "Let us consider this as an opportunity we have been given to plan the future of the party," Stalin said, according to ANI. He acknowledged that the functioning of party office-bearers was among the factors behind the electoral defeat and said the party needed to accept its mistakes. Rather than examining individual constituencies and simply replacing party functionaries, Stalin said he had opted for a comprehensive self-assessment. "Even if the mistake is committed by an individual, it is the 75-year-old party that suffers because of it," he said. The party has also formed a 38-member committee to collect feedback from grassroots workers and launched a dedicated website to allow the public to submit their views, PTI reported. Stalin also took aim at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK leader C Joseph Vijay while addressing party workers. He alleged that Vijay was "busy changing the names of all the projects" introduced by the DMK and said the chief minister treated the Legislative Assembly like a "movie set". Stalin also called on DMK workers to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and focus on enrolling new members who were willing to work according to the party's principles and ideology. He said the party's objective was to remain connected with people regardless of electoral victories or defeats and to work towards making a political comeback. "We are specialists in making a comeback, and we will do it well," he added while appealing the party members to focus on grassroots mobilisation. title: राष्ट्रीय जैव विविधता प्राधिकरण (एनबीए) ने पहुंच और लाभ-साझाकरण (एबीएस) निधि से 27 राज्य जैव विविधता बोर्डों, 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश जैव विविधता परिषदों और भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद् (आईसीएआर)-भारतीय बागवानी अनुसंधान संस्थान, कर्नाटक को 2.82 करोड़ रुपये जारी किए
content:
पर्यावरण, वन एवं जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्रालय
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    राष्ट्रीय जैव विविधता प्राधिकरण (एनबीए) ने पहुंच और लाभ-साझाकरण (एबीएस) निधि से 27 राज्य जैव विविधता बोर्डों, 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश जैव विविधता परिषदों और भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद् (आईसीएआर)-भारतीय बागवानी अनुसंधान संस्थान, कर्नाटक को 2.82 करोड़ रुपये जारी किए
                              
                              
                                    
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 12:49PM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        राष्ट्रीय जैव विविधता प्राधिकरण (एनबीए) ने भारत के जैविक संसाधनों के उपयोग से उत्पन्न होने वाले 2.82 करोड़ रुपये का पहुंच और लाभ-साझाकरण (एबीएस) तंत्र के तहत वितरण किया। इसमें से 2.80 करोड़ रुपये 27 राज्य जैव विविधता बोर्डों (एसबीबी) और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश जैव विविधता परिषदों (यूटीबीसी) को जारी किए गए हैं जबकि 2.01 लाख रुपये भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद् (आईसीएआर)-भारतीय बागवानी अनुसंधान संस्थान (आईआईएचआर), कर्नाटक को जारी किए जा रहे हैं।
एनबीए को मेसर्स एडवांटा एंटरप्राइजेज लिमिटेड (पूर्व में मेसर्स यूपीएल लिमिटेड) से एबीएस के तहत 2.94 करोड़ रुपये प्राप्त हुए जिसका उपयोग फूलगोभी (ब्रासिका ओलेरासिया वेर. बोट्राइटिस ) की आठ संकर किस्मों, मिर्च ( कैप्सिकम एनम ) की पांच संकर किस्मों, भिंडी ( एबेलमोस्कस एस्कुलेंटस ) की पांच संकर किस्मों और टमाटर ( सोलनम लाइकोपर्सिकम ) की छह संकर किस्मों से जुड़े आनुवंशिक संसाधनों के उपयोग के लिए किया जाएगा।
इस मामले में, जैविक संसाधनों तक किसी अन्य कंपनी के अधिग्रहण के माध्यम से पहुंच बनाई गई थी और किसानों, समुदायों या किसी एक पहचान योग्य भौगोलिक स्रोत जैसे लाभ प्राप्तकर्ताओं का पता नहीं लगाया जा सका। इससे पहले, एनबीए ने ऐसे मामलों में लाभ साझाकरण घटक को साझा करने/उपयोग करने के लिए एक उपयुक्त कार्यप्रणाली की सिफारिश करने हेतु एक विशेषज्ञ समिति (ईसी) का गठन किया था और ईसी की सिफारिश को बाद में प्राधिकरण द्वारा अनुमोदित किया गया था। अनुमोदित कार्यप्रणाली के अनुसार, एनबीए ने 2.80 करोड़ रुपये वितरित किए। यह आवंटन विभिन्न राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में संबंधित बागवानी फसलों की खेती को ध्यान में रखते हुए किया गया है। गुजरात, पश्चिम बंगाल और मध्य प्रदेश प्रमुख प्राप्तकर्ता राज्यों में से हैं जबकि सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा प्राप्त करने वाले दस राज्य इस प्रकार हैं:
 
एसबीबी और यूटीबीसी को जारी की गई धनराशि का उपयोग जन जैव विविधता रजिस्टरों के प्रलेखन और अद्यतन, इन-सीटू और एक्स-सीटू संरक्षण, खराब हो चुके पारिस्थितिक तंत्रों के पुनर्स्थापन, जैव विविधता विरासत स्थलों को सुदृढ़ करने, जैव विविधता प्रबंधन समितियों के क्षमता विकास और सामुदायिक आजीविका संवर्धन सहित गतिविधियों के लिए किया जाना है, और इस राशि के प्राप्ति के एक वर्ष के भीतर उपयोग प्रमाण पत्र और व्यय विवरण प्रस्तुत करना होगा।
इसके अलावा, एनबीए को सुमितोमो केमिकल इंडिया लिमिटेड, मुंबई (पूर्व में एक्सेल क्रॉप केयर) से दो सूक्ष्मजीव उपभेदों, स्यूडोमोनास फ्लोरेसेंस 1% डब्ल्यूपी (स्ट्रेन आईआईएचआर-पीएफ-2) और ट्राइकोडर्मा हारज़ियानम 1% डब्ल्यूपी (स्ट्रेन आईआईएचआर-टीएच-2) तक पहुंच के लिए एबीएस राशि के रूप में 7.15 लाख रुपये प्राप्त हुए। ये उपभेद भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद् - भारतीय बागवानी अनुसंधान संस्थान (आईसीएआर- आईआईएचआर), कर्नाटक से अनुसंधान और वाणिज्यिक उपयोग के लिए प्राप्त हुए थे। चूंकि इस मामले में जैविक संसाधन सार्वजनिक अनुसंधान संस्थान से प्राप्त किए गए थे, इसलिए एबीएस राशि का 30% यानी 2.01 लाख रुपये संबंधित संस्थान आईसीएआर-आईआईएचआर को नियमों के अनुसार वितरित किया जा रहा है और शेष राशि का उपयोग एनबीए द्वारा जैविक विविधता अधिनियम की धारा 27 के अनुसार किया जाएगा।
संस्था को एक वर्ष के भीतर भंडारों के रखरखाव, अनुसंधान और जैव विविधता सर्वेक्षण कार्य, वर्गीकरण और संरक्षण में क्षमता विकास, और जैविक संसाधनों और उनके वन्य संबंधी जीवों के इन-सीटू और एक्स- सीटू संरक्षण सहित कार्यों के लिए धनराशि का उपयोग करना आवश्यक है। यह वितरण जैविक विविधता अधिनियम, 2002 और इसके संबंधित नियामक ढांचे के कार्यान्वयन को सुदृढ़ करने के लिए एनबीए के निरंतर प्रयासों का हिस्सा है, साथ ही यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि भारत के जैविक संसाधनों के वाणिज्यिक उपयोग से प्राप्त लाभों को जैव विविधता संरक्षण, सतत उपयोग और किसानों, स्थानीय समुदायों और जैविक विविधता के संरक्षण और सतत उपयोग से जुड़े अन्य लोगों के सामाजिक-आर्थिक विकास के लिए किया जाए।
एनबीए द्वारा अब तक जारी की गई एबीएस राशि कुल 185 करोड़ रुपये (यूएसडी 19.34 मिलियन) है। यह पहल जैव विविधता पर सम्मेलन (सीबीडी) और पहुंच एवं लाभ-साझाकरण पर नागोया प्रोटोकॉल, साथ ही कुनमिंग-मॉन्ट्रियल वैश्विक जैव विविधता ढांचा (केएमजीबीएफ) के तहत भारत की प्रतिबद्धताओं में भी योगदान देती है, विशेष रूप से लक्ष्य 13 में, जो आनुवंशिक संसाधनों और आनुवंशिक संसाधनों पर डिजिटल अनुक्रम जानकारी के उपयोग से उत्पन्न होने वाले लाभों के निष्पक्ष और समान बंटवारे को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए प्रभावी उपायों का आह्वान करता है।

title: India approves 1,800 km of new LPG pipelines across 6 states with  ₹7,000 crore investment to boost supply
content:
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) has cleared plans for around 1,800 km of new liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) pipelines, involving an estimated investment of ₹7,000 crore. The expansion is aimed at strengthening fuel supply networks and reducing reliance on transportation by road, as per PTI. The regulator has approved three major LPG pipeline projects spanning Telangana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Karnataka and Goa. The projects will be developed by state-run GAIL (India) Ltd, according to a PNGRB statement. Once completed, the new projects will expand the regulator-approved common-carrier LPG pipeline network from around 7,700 km to nearly 9,500 km, representing a growth of about 23.5%. The pipeline expansion is expected to strengthen LPG distribution across India, which depends significantly on imports brought in through coastal terminals before being transported to inland markets. A wider pipeline network could make the movement of LPG to consumption centres more efficient and dependable. The three newly approved projects include a 556-km pipeline connecting Cherlapally in Telangana with Nagpur in Maharashtra, a 611-km line between Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh and Sitarganj in Uttarakhand, and a 633-km pipeline linking Shikrapur in Maharashtra with Goa and Hubli in Karnataka. These projects add to the previously approved 2,757-km Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline, which is the country’s longest LPG pipeline. PNGRB stated the expanded pipeline network would reduce India’s dependence on road transport for moving LPG, thereby lowering the number of tanker movements and enhancing road safety. It is also expected to bring down transportation expenses, ease congestion and reduce carbon emissions. Moving LPG through pipelines is generally considered safer and more cost-effective for long-distance transportation. Shifting from tank trucks to pipelines could also reportedly reduce the risks linked to transporting hazardous fuel on roads. The regulator has been working towards reducing the primary transportation of LPG by road to bottling plants, particularly following several major accidents involving LPG tankers. The projects also carry strategic significance for India given the country’s substantial dependence on imported LPG. Since most LPG imports enter India through coastal terminals, substantial quantities need to be moved to inland markets. A nationwide pipeline network could provide an alternative to road transportation and help ensure uninterrupted supplies during emergencies, disruptions or sudden increases in demand. The pipelines could also provide “line-pack storage”, enabling LPG to be held within the network as it continues to flow. This additional buffer could give the supply system greater flexibility and help manage short-term interruptions. The newly approved projects are part of a wider push to develop an integrated LPG pipeline network connecting coastal import terminals with major consumption hubs while easing the burden on road-based logistics. With a total of six years of experience in journalism, he has previously worked with Vaco Binary Semantics for Google, taking on the role of news curation lead, and reported from the field on health, education, and agriculture stories for 101reporters and News9. He has also served as a content editor for entertainment and news media organisations.

Garvit holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in journalism and mass communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University and Gurugram University, respectively. During college days, he joined India’s only non-profit student journalism network, where he anchored daily news updates and produced his own weekly show called ‘Data Fix’.

He was selected for the YES Foundation Media for Social Change Fellowship in Delhi, the Talking Data to the Fourth Pillar residential workshop, and the VOICE Fellowship in Pune.

He holds certificates in COVID-19-verification reporting, data journalism, food & agriculture, tech policy, media literacy and countering misinformation, and tackling election disinformation courses from Thomson Foundation, IndiaSpend, The Dialogue, US Mission in India, and AFP.

title: पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्री श्री हरदीप सिंह पुरी की मॉरीशस की आधिकारिक यात्रा
content:
पेट्रोलियम एवं प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्रालय 
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्री श्री हरदीप सिंह पुरी की मॉरीशस की आधिकारिक यात्रा
                              
                              
                                    
मॉरीशस की ऊर्जा सुरक्षा को मजबूत करने के लिए समझौते पर हस्ताक्षर किए गए
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 10:11AM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        केंद्रीय पेट्रोलियम और प्राकृतिक गैस मंत्री श्री हरदीप सिंह पुरी ने 20-21 अगस्त 2026 को मॉरीशस गणराज्य की आधिकारिक यात्रा की।
मंत्री ने 20 अगस्त को मॉरीशस के प्रधानमंत्री महामहिम डॉ. नवीनचंद्र रामगुलाम से भेंट की। उनकी उपस्थिति में, भारत और मॉरीशस ने तेल और गैस क्षेत्र में सहयोग के लिए एक सरकारी समझौता ज्ञापन (एमओयू) पर हस्ताक्षर किए, साथ ही पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों की आपूर्ति के लिए इंडियन ऑयल कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड (आईओसीएल) और मॉरीशस के स्टेट ट्रेडिंग कॉर्पोरेशन (एसटीसी) के बीच एक दीर्घकालिक बिक्री और खरीद समझौते पर भी हस्ताक्षर किए। समझौते के तहत, आईओसीएल मॉरीशस की मोटर स्पिरिट (एमएस), हाई स्पीड डीजल (एचएसडी) और एविएशन टर्बाइन फ्यूल (एटीएफ) की संपूर्ण आयात आवश्यकता की आपूर्ति करेगा।
तेल और गैस सहयोग पर समझौता ज्ञापन दोनों देशों के बीच लंबे समय से चली आ रही ऊर्जा साझेदारी को संस्थागत रूप देता है। इसमें पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों की आपूर्ति, मॉरीशस के अधिकारियों के लिए प्रशिक्षण और क्षमता विकास तथा जैव ईंधन सहयोग शामिल है। आईओसीएल और एसटीसी के बीच पांच साल का यह समझौता मॉरीशस को दीर्घकालिक आपूर्ति की गारंटी देता है, जिससे देश को आपूर्ति की सुरक्षा मिलती है और कीमतों में उतार-चढ़ाव से बचाव होता है। हाल के वर्षों में दक्षिण एशिया के बाहर किसी भारतीय सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के तेल विपणन कंपनी द्वारा किया गया यह पहला दीर्घकालिक आपूर्ति समझौता है।
इस यात्रा के दौरान, मंत्री ने ऊर्जा एवं सार्वजनिक उपयोगिता मंत्री माननीय पैट्रिक गेर्विस असिरवाडेन, वाणिज्य एवं उपभोक्ता संरक्षण मंत्री माननीय जॉन माइकल त्ज़ौन साओ युंग सिक युएन और विदेश मामलों, क्षेत्रीय एकीकरण एवं अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार मंत्री माननीय धनंजय रामफुल के साथ उपयोगी द्विपक्षीय बैठकें कीं। उन्होंने पोर्ट लुइस के मेर रूज में इंडिया ऑयल (मॉरीशस) लिमिटेड की 27.5 टीएमटी बंकर समुद्री ईंधन भंडारण सुविधा के शिलान्यास समारोह में भाग लिया।
एक भरोसेमंद ऊर्जा साझेदार के रूप में भारत की बढ़ती भूमिका
भारत एक प्रमुख वैश्विक शोधन केंद्र के रूप में उभरा है, जहां 23 रिफाइनरियों में प्रति वर्ष 267 एमएमटी शोधित पेट्रोलियम उत्पादों का उत्पादन होता है, जिससे यह परिष्कृत उत्पादों का शुद्ध निर्यातक बन गया है। भारत पहले से ही नेपाल और भूटान की पेट्रोलियम मांग को पूरा कर रहा है और क्षेत्र के अन्य देशों और उससे बाहर के देशों को भी महत्वपूर्ण मात्रा में आपूर्ति करता है। यहां तक कि पश्चिम एशिया में चल रहे संकट के दौरान भी, भारत ने नेपाल और भूटान के प्रति अपनी आपूर्ति प्रतिबद्धताओं को पूरा किया है, जिससे यह क्षेत्र के लिए एक विश्वसनीय ऊर्जा सुरक्षा प्रदाता बन गया है। मॉरीशस के साथ समझौता भारत को उस देश के प्रमुख ईंधन आपूर्तिकर्ता के रूप में स्थापित करता है और हिंद महासागर क्षेत्र में भारत की रणनीतिक और आर्थिक उपस्थिति को मजबूत करता है।
समझौता ज्ञापन जैव ईंधन के क्षेत्र में सहयोग को भी बढ़ावा देता है
इस समझौता ज्ञापन में ज्ञान, अनुसंधान और प्रशिक्षण के आदान-प्रदान के माध्यम से जैव ईंधन के क्षेत्र में सहयोग का प्रावधान भी है। मॉरीशस ग्लोबल बायोफ्यूल्स एलायंस (जीबीए) का संस्थापक सदस्य है, जिसकी पहल भारत द्वारा शुरू की गई थी और भारत की जी20 अध्यक्षता के दौरान इसे लॉन्च किया गया था। जीबीए सचिवालय ने अपने देश सहभागिता कार्यक्रम के तहत मॉरीशस के ऊर्जा और सार्वजनिक उपयोगिता मंत्रालय के साथ मिलकर देश के लिए जैव ईंधन देश परिदृश्य नीति ढांचा विकसित किया है।
मंत्री पुरी और माननीय पैट्रिक गेरवाइस असिरवाडेन ने 21 अगस्त को संयुक्त रूप से जैव ईंधन देश परिदृश्य नीति ढांचे के शुभारंभ को देखा। यह जैव ईंधन के माध्यम से अपने ऊर्जा परिवर्तन की संभावनाओं को तलाशने में मॉरीशस के लिए एक प्रारंभिक बिंदु है।

title: Karnataka cracks down on ‘analogue paneer’, bans manufacturing, sale for 1 year: Does it apply to frozen desserts?
content:
The Karnataka government has imposed a one-year ban on the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of “analogue paneer” marketed as “paneer” officials said on Saturday, stating that the move has been taken as a public health measure. Officials clarified that the ban covers only dairy analogue products for which the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has not laid down specific quality standards or specifications. The restriction does not extend to standardised products such as frozen desserts, processed cheese and mixed-fat spreads, which are regulated under separate food safety standards According to officials, “analogue” or non-dairy paneer refers to products made to resemble paneer by fully or partly substituting milk fat or milk solids with vegetable oil, vegetable fat or other ingredients that do not come from milk. Officials said products made using non-dairy substitutes cannot be labelled, promoted or sold as “paneer” or presented to consumers as genuine paneer. "The Food Safety Division of the Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration, Karnataka, has issued a Government Notification dated August 17, prohibiting the manufacturing, processing, packing, storage, distribution, transportation, wholesale and retail sales, display for sale and supply of Analogue/Non-Dairy Paneer being sold under the name 'Paneer' in the state for a year," the department Commissioner Srinivas K, said in a statement, according to PTI. The department noted that under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, paneer is defined as a standardised food made from milk, adding milk fat is an essential component of paneer and that replacing it, or other milk components, with vegetable oil, vegetable fat or other non-dairy substances is not allowed under the regulations. "Karnataka has tested several paneer samples, and it is found that there is no adulteration. Even though there is no adulteration of paneer with vegetable oil, vegetable fat or other dairy ingredients, the prohibition is ordered in the interest of public health," the department mentioned. The department also directed food business operators not to use, stock, supply or sell analogue or non-dairy paneer as an ingredient in the preparation or manufacture of any food product. The Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration will undertake the necessary steps across Karnataka to ensure the order is properly implemented and enforced. Food business operators have been directed to strictly follow the provisions of the ban. The Bombay High Court on Friday declined to provide immediate relief to a Thane restaurant facing action by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over the alleged serving of banned analogue paneer. The court criticised the establishment for offering the non-dairy substitute to customers. A bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad invoked “poetic justice”, observing that Udupi Swaad should also face consequences after allegedly making customers consume “something rotten”. Earlier this month, the Maharashtra government imposed a one-year ban on the manufacture and sale of analogue or non-dairy paneer, citing concerns over public health and violations of food safety regulations. Under the government order, cases in which consumption of unsafe food leads to death can attract life imprisonment and a minimum fine of ₹10 lakh. Garvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram. title: US-Iran war news LIVE: Strait of Hormuz to remain shut until US corrects its behavior, says Iran's Rezaei
content:
US-Iran war news LIVE: Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), Mohsen Rezaei, on Saturday (local time) said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will not reopen until the United States fulfils its commitments and changes its behaviour amid escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington. Pezeshkian says Iran didn't compromise on any clause of MoU Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday (local time) said Tehran has not compromised on any clause of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed amid efforts to address the ongoing tensions with the US and Israel, while asserting that Iran seeks a solution through dialogue and logic. Iran warns of action against neighbours if they support US' ‘economic war’ Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), Mohsen Rezaei, on Saturday (local time), warned neighbouring countries against joining the United States' economic war against Tehran, saying their participation would lead Iran to consider them enemies. He made these remarks in an interview with IRIB and said, "We are telling all surrounding countries not to participate in the economic war with America; otherwise, we will consider them an enemy." He added that the Islamic Republic is not seeking an escalation of the conflict but warned that Tehran would respond if neighbouring countries supported Washington's economic pressure measures. Rezaei blames Trump for creating 'nuclear insecurity' In an interview with IRIB, Iran's SNSC, Rezaei, accused US President Donald Trump of creating "nuclear insecurity" instead of boosting global nuclear security, claiming that Washington's actions against Tehran have increased countries' interest in acquiring nuclear weapons. He said, "Instead of nuclear security, Trump has created nuclear insecurity," and added, "Trump's stupidity in attacking Iran increased the world's desire for the atomic bomb, especially when they saw that membership in the Atomic Energy Organization and the NPT was ineffective in preventing an American attack." Rezaei claimed that Tehran had complied with international nuclear regulations, remained a member of the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), and allowed inspections under international safeguards. Trump's plan to economically isolate Iran risks strikes across Gulf The US President is betting on new sanctions, a naval blockade, and ramped-up economic pressure against Iran's trading partners to force Tehran to accept a deal to end the war on Washington's terms. However, reports suggest that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which has claimed control of the vital Strait of Hormuz and sent volleys of attack drones across the Persian Gulf, may be impervious to such pressure and has plenty of ways to retaliate. While a key part of these efforts will come on Monday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has promised to unveil details, significant new economic pressure is likely to prompt Iran to retaliate with military strikes across the Gulf, including against energy infrastructure. Iran condemns Washington's plans to announce new sanctions On Saturday (local time), Iran denounced the United States' plan to announce new sanctions that could further strain the Islamic Republic's economy and affect its most important trading partners, including China. After nearly six months of war since the US and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran on February 28, the sides are no longer firing at each other but are also showing no sign of pursuing peace talks. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is all set to embark on two-day visit to Paris where he will meet French President Emmanuel Macron. President Donald Trump has vowed to hit Iran hard economically, after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Washington would impose measures on Tehran that have "never been seen" as soon as next week. Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday. Tensions between Washington and Tehran escalated further on Sunday after US President Donald Trump again shared an image that depicts the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz as "NEW US Territory", even as Iran reiterated that the crucial maritime corridor will remain closed unless the United States alters its stance. Deadly airstrikes in Gaza on Wednesday cast more doubt on whether new US efforts can advance a tenuous ceasefire in the Palestinian territory. title: Karnataka IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar goes missing amid KPSC row; last traced to Bengaluru airport
content:
Karnataka IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar has reportedly gone missing and has been unreachable by his family and others since August 20, with authorities looking into his whereabouts, PTI reported.
Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge confirmed that the government had received information about the matter but said no formal missing complaint had been filed by Gangwar's family or anyone else.
According to information received by the government, Gangwar was last traced to Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru. His mobile phone has reportedly been switched off, and authorities are checking his movements to ascertain whether he travelled from Bengaluru to Delhi.
'All modes of communication disconnected'
"All modes of communication with him have been disconnected, and he is not reachable. As of now, we have information that he was last traced to Kempegowda International Airport," Kharge told reporters.
He said authorities had received some information from the airport and were looking into it. "We are still investigating and will decide on the further course of action," the minister said.
Gangwar, a 2016-batch IAS officer, is currently serving as Director, MSME, in the Karnataka Department of Industries and Commerce. He had earlier served as controller of examinations at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) and was replaced from the post in March this year.
According to sources cited by PTI, Gangwar had reportedly booked a flight ticket to Delhi before he became unreachable.
KPSC developments
The development comes amid scrutiny surrounding the KPSC and allegations of corruption in recruitment examinations. However, official sources said there was no confirmation at this stage linking Gangwar's reported disappearance to developments during his tenure at the commission.
Kharge said the Karnataka Cabinet had on Friday decided to recommend to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot that KPSC chairperson Shivashankarappa S Sahukar be suspended and an inquiry initiated against him.
Sahukar is facing allegations of corruption and nepotism, including allegations that his daughter was selected for a government job using a false income certificate.
The governor had suspended Sahukar on July 13 over allegations including non-disclosure of important information and misbehaviour. However, the Karnataka High Court ordered his reinstatement on August 18, observing that the governor's decision had not been taken with the aid and advice of the Cabinet.
Kharge said the state government had decided to reiterate its earlier position and advise the governor to suspend Sahukar and initiate an inquiry.
The KPSC has also come under investigation in an alleged recruitment examination scam. The Enforcement Directorate on Tuesday searched premises linked to the KPSC, Sahukar, member Shanta Hosmani and others as part of a money laundering probe into alleged irregularities in the recruitment examination for veterinary officers.

title: ‘No adverse weather’: Kochi airport accuses SpiceJet of misinformation; airline responds— It was ‘precautionary measure’
content:
The weather conditions in Kochi city were not adverse and didn't warrant disruptions to SpiceJet services, the Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) said on Saturday, accusing the airline of spreading misinformation.
On Saturday, the airline alleged that, due to “bad weather in Kochi,” flight operations may be affected.
“Due to bad weather in Kochi, all departures/arrivals and their consequential flights might be affected. Passengers are requested to check their flight status via httpspicejet.com/#status,” SpiceJet said in a social media post.
The airport, in a passenger advisory, said it had noted ongoing operational issues with SpiceJet affecting its international services, including those from Kochi, causing considerable inconvenience and uncertainty for passengers.
“SpiceJet has issued a social media communication spreading misinformation by attributing the disruption to bad weather at Kochi,” CIAL said.
It said there were no adverse weather conditions at Kochi warranting the disruption cited by the airline. “No other airline operating from Kochi has reported such disruptions on account of weather conditions during the same period,” CIAL said.
The airport operator said that, despite ongoing passenger grievances, the airline had not adequately addressed the issues, which had worsened over the past few days.
CIAL said it had made every effort, as a responsible airport operator, to assist affected passengers and provide them with necessary support. Passengers who have booked SpiceJet flights have been advised to recheck their flight status with the airline before proceeding to the airport.
In a statement, SpiceJet Spokesperson clarified that the advisory issued by the airline on social media “was a precautionary measure intended to help passengers plan their journeys and make necessary arrangements in advance, in view of the prevailing weather conditions.”
The airline said its advisory clearly stated that flights might be affected and that it “was not an announcement of any cancellation or suspension of operations.”
The spokesperson said that there were no cancellations of SpiceJet flights from Kochi, and the airline operated both its scheduled daily departures to Fujairah and Dubai yesterday, Friday.
Reiterating its commitment, SpiceJet said it keeps its passengers and travel partners informed of any developments that may potentially affect their travel.
“Our advisories are issued with the safety and convenience of our passengers in mind, so that they have adequate information and time to plan accordingly,” it added.
SpiceJet also said it regrets any misunderstanding that may have arisen from the advisory and reassured that the airline continues to operate its scheduled services normally, subject to prevailing operational conditions.
SpiceJet was fined ₹7.5 lakh by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for informing the tribunal about their settlement at the last minute, after orders had been reserved in eight insolvency petitions against the airline.
The tribunal directed SpiceJet and Aviator ML to pay ₹7.5 lakh each to the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund.
“Payment of cost of ₹15 lakh payable equally by the operational creditor (Aviator ML) and corporate debtor (SpiceJet), that is ₹7.5 lakh each, to be deposited in the Prime Minister National Relief Fund, within a period of 7 days from today,” the bench said, passing the oral order.
Taking cognisance of the manner in which SpiceJet informed the tribunal about the settlement on the day the order was due to be pronounced, the bench expressed its displeasure, saying, “It is a fraud played with the bench.”
(With agency inputs)

title: कर्मचारी भविष्य निधि संगठन (ईपीएफओ) ने प्रतिष्ठानों से ईपीएफ कवरेज से बाहर कर्मचारियों के लिए सामाजिक सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने हेतु कर्मचारी नामांकन अभियान, 2026 का लाभ उठाने का आग्रह किया
content:
श्रम और रोजगार मंत्रालय
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    कर्मचारी भविष्य निधि संगठन (ईपीएफओ) ने प्रतिष्ठानों से ईपीएफ कवरेज से बाहर कर्मचारियों के लिए सामाजिक सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने हेतु कर्मचारी नामांकन अभियान, 2026 का लाभ उठाने का आग्रह किया
                              
                              
                                    
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 11:08AM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        कर्मचारी भविष्य निधि संगठन (ईपीएफओ) ने प्रतिष्ठानों से आग्रह किया है कि वे 29 जून 2026 से प्रभावी कर्मचारी नामांकन अभियान, 2026 (ईईसी 2026) का उपयोग करें। यह उन पात्र कर्मचारियों को नामांकित करने का एक विशेष एक बार अवसर प्रदान करता है जो 1 अप्रैल 2009 से 31 मार्च 2026 की अवधि के दौरान ईपीएफ कवरेज से बाहर रहे।
यह अभियान 31 अक्टूबर 2026 तक चलेगा और इसका उद्देश्य नियोक्ताओं द्वारा स्वैच्छिक अनुपालन को सुविधाजनक बनाना और पात्र श्रमिकों को भविष्य निधि, पेंशन और बीमा के लाभ देना है।
ईईसी 2026 के तहत, पात्र नियोक्ता उन कर्मचारियों की घोषणा करते हैं और नामांकन कर सकते हैं जो निर्धारित अवधि के दौरान ईपीएफ कवरेज से बाहर रह गए थे और घोषणा की तिथि पर जीवित हैं और प्रतिष्ठान में कार्यरत हैं। यह अभियान पूर्व अनुपालन को नियमित करने के लिए विशिष्ट छूट प्रदान करता है। इसमें कर्मचारी के हिस्से की छूट भी शामिल है, यदि पहले इसकी कटौती नहीं की गई थी, लेकिन यह अभियान की शर्तों के अधीन है।
नियोक्ताओं को निर्धारित ऑनलाइन माध्यम से नामांकन और भुगतान प्रक्रिया पूरी करनी होगी। प्रत्येक घोषित कर्मचारी के लिए उमंग ऐप के माध्यम से फेस ऑथेंटिकेशन आधारित यूएएन जनरेट किया जाएगा और अंशदान इलेक्ट्रॉनिक चालान-कम-रिटर्न (ईसीआर) के माध्यम से जमा किया जाएगा।
इस अभियान का उद्देश्य पात्र कर्मचारियों को वैधानिक सामाजिक सुरक्षा ढांचे के अंतर्गत लाने के लिए एक सुव्यवस्थित तंत्र प्रदान करके प्रतिष्ठानों और कर्मचारियों को लाभ पहुंचाना है। नियोक्ताओं को अपने रोजगार और वेतन रिकॉर्ड की समीक्षा करने और उन पात्र कर्मचारियों की पहचान करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जाता है जो निर्धारित अवधि के दौरान ईपीएफ कवरेज से बाहर रह गए थे।
ईपीएफओ नियोक्ताओं, कर्मचारियों, प्रतिष्ठानों, ठेकेदारों और अन्य हितधारकों के बीच ईईसी 2026 की प्रमुख विशेषताओं का प्रसार करने के लिए व्यापक जागरूकता और संपर्क अभियान भी चला रहा है। भारत सरकार के मंत्रालयों और विभागों, राज्य सरकारों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों, सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रमों, स्वायत्त निकायों और अन्य संगठनों को अपने प्रशासनिक नियंत्रण के अंतर्गत आने वाले प्रतिष्ठानों और सेवा प्रदाताओं के बीच इस अभियान के व्यापक प्रसार को सुगम बनाने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जा रहा है।
नियोक्ताओं को इस एक बार मिलने वाले अवसर का लाभ उठाने और 31 अक्टूबर 2026 को अभियान समाप्त होने से पहले पात्र कर्मचारियों का नामांकन पूरा करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित किया जाता है।

title: Why is Trump warming up to North Korea's Kim while turning up pressure on South Korea
content:
US President Donald Trump wants to revive his personal diplomacy with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, even as he has turned up pressure on South Korea, a longstanding US ally. Earlier this week, Trump said he was expected to meet Kim later this year. Trump's statement came days after he ordered the Pentagon to scale back joint military exercises with South Korea. But Pyongyang has responded coolly to his overturns, saying the reduction in drills does not amount to a goodwill gesture and that US policy towards North Korea remains hostile. The contrasting approach towards the two halves of the Korean peninsula raises an important question: why is Trump again reaching out to Kim, despite earlier summits not producing the desired results, while putting pressure on Seoul? Experts say the answer lies partly in Trump's transactional approach to alliances, changing US military priorities and a fundamentally different strategic position for North Korea compared with Trump's first term. Trump has long favoured leader-to-leader diplomacy with Kim. During his first term, Trump held three meetings with the North Korean leader in 2018 and 2019, including a historic summit in Singapore. The talks generated hopes of a breakthrough on North Korea's nuclear programme but ultimately failed to produce a comprehensive agreement. North Korea has since expanded its nuclear and missile capabilities and strengthened its military relationship with Russia. That means the strategic environment surrounding any new Trump-Kim engagement would be very different from that of 2018. Eugene Park, a historian of East Asia, said Trump's renewed interest reflects both changing strategic circumstances and his longstanding preference for personalised diplomacy. "North Korea occupies a considerably stronger geopolitical position than it did during Trump's first term," Park said, pointing to its advances in nuclear and missile capabilities and its closer relationship with Moscow. North Korea's support for Russia in the Ukraine war has also increased its geopolitical importance. At the same time, China has an incentive to remain engaged with Pyongyang to prevent it from moving too far into Russia's orbit, Park said. Trump, meanwhile, has repeatedly described his relationship with Kim as positive and has increasingly referred to North Korea as a nuclear power. The latest US outreach comes as Washington remains heavily engaged in the war with Iran. Reuters has reported that Trump is eager to restart talks with North Korea and secure an international diplomatic win. Dr Jojin V. John, assistant professor at the School of International Relations and Politics at Mahatma Gandhi University, said the current Trump administration's approach appears more bilateral and deal-focused than the broader regional strategy pursued during his first term. "Developments toward North Korea should be interpreted on their own terms rather than as part of a single, unified 'US regional approach'," John said. He added that one possible factor behind the renewed attention to Northeast Asia could be the timing of the US midterm elections, which can alter political incentives and foreign-policy priorities. Trump's decision to scale back US-South Korea military exercises has brought the alliance into focus. The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise was cut short after Trump described the drills as costly and "hostile" towards North Korea. He also linked his criticism of Seoul to South Korea's reluctance to support the US in its efforts over Iran. For Seoul, the exercises are an important part of preparing for a potential conflict with North Korea. For Pyongyang, they have long been portrayed as rehearsals for an invasion. Trump's decision therefore serves two possible purposes: reducing an obstacle to dialogue with Kim and pushing South Korea to assume greater responsibility for its own defence. But Park cautioned against treating Trump's pressure on Seoul and his outreach to Pyongyang as a single negotiating tactic. "I would hesitate to interpret this primarily as an effort to use North Korea as leverage against South Korea," Park said. Instead, he sees both policies as expressions of Trump's broader transactional approach to alliances and international security. The US faces greater demands on its military resources, including commitments in the Middle East, while Washington and Seoul are also discussing greater South Korean involvement in defence production and security responsibilities, Park said. "The alliance is moving toward a more balanced division of responsibilities," he said. John similarly described the Trump administration's approach as bilateral and deal-focused. He said Trump's increased criticism of South Korea and renewed interest in North Korea should be understood separately. "The South Korea posture likely reflects pressure and bargaining tactics, while the North Korea signals reflect an effort to test whether direct diplomacy can yield concessions," John said. This could be the biggest obstacle to Trump's plans. North Korea has not responded positively to Trump's latest overtures. Kim's influential sister, Kim Yo Jong, rejected the idea that Washington's decision to scale back military exercises represented a meaningful goodwill gesture. North Korea also launched about 10 ballistic missiles off its east coast, according to South Korea's military. That response is significant because North Korea is entering any potential negotiations from a stronger position than it had during Trump's first term. Back then, Pyongyang was seeking sanctions relief and had fewer strategic alternatives. It is now more closely aligned with Russia and China and has considerably stronger nuclear and missile capabilities. John said this has fundamentally altered Pyongyang's calculations. "North Korea is no longer as isolated as it once was," he said. "From Pyongyang's standpoint, this places it in a stronger position, meaning denuclearisation has arguably moved farther down the priority list or is no longer a credible expectation." North Korea could also use renewed engagement with Washington to increase its strategic autonomy from both Beijing and Moscow. "The ultimate aim for North Korea remains regime survival and securing concessions from the great powers by playing one against the other," John said. Park similarly said North Korea's increased leverage has created more favourable conditions for renewed diplomacy, but that Pyongyang has remained relatively restrained in its treatment of Trump personally. That leaves an unusual situation: Trump appears eager for a summit, but Kim has fewer reasons to accept one on Washington's terms. The biggest difference between a possible Trump-Kim meeting now and the summits of 2018-19 could be the nuclear issue. Trump's first-term diplomacy was built around the goal of denuclearisation. The Singapore summit produced an agreement committing the two sides to the "complete denuclearization" of the Korean Peninsula, but subsequent negotiations broke down. North Korea has since expanded its nuclear capabilities. Trump has himself repeatedly referred to North Korea as a nuclear power, although Washington continues to call for denuclearisation and does not formally recognise Pyongyang as a nuclear-weapon state. John said this could point towards a more pragmatic US approach. "Recent American national security strategy documents appear to give little or no attention to denuclearisation in the North Korean case," he said. Combined with Trump's public statements, this could signal, at least informally, that Washington is moving towards a posture that treats North Korea as a de facto nuclear weapons state, he said. Park, however, cautioned against assuming that diplomacy would become pointless simply because complete denuclearisation is unlikely. A future summit could instead focus on reducing tensions, maintaining communication channels, limiting missile testing or managing the risk of military escalation. "Trump might therefore regard a summit as successful if it stabilized bilateral relations and sustained high-level engagement, even without producing a comprehensive nuclear agreement," Park said. Trump's approach does not necessarily mean Washington is preparing to abandon its alliance with Seoul. Park said the more likely outcome is a transformation of the alliance, with South Korea taking greater responsibility for its own defence. "The most likely outcome is not the dissolution of the alliance but its continued transformation," he said. That could mean a more reciprocal relationship in which Seoul assumes a larger share of the military and strategic burden. John, however, pointed to an important complication: South Korea's current government may not necessarily oppose Trump's engagement with Kim. President Lee Jae-myung's administration has expressed interest in improving inter-Korean relations and pursuing an "End of War" declaration. From Seoul's current government's perspective, John said, North Korea itself is not necessarily viewed as the root problem but as a symptom of the wider security structure in Northeast Asia. A breakthrough between Washington and Pyongyang could therefore be welcomed by Seoul, particularly if it reduces tensions on the peninsula. But the approach could face resistance from conservative forces in South Korea, particularly if US pressure is perceived as weakening the alliance or forcing Seoul to assume greater strategic responsibility. A repeat of the dramatic summits of Trump's first term is possible, but expectations are likely to be much lower. Trump has a personal relationship with Kim that he believes can facilitate dialogue. But the fundamental strategic conditions have changed. North Korea is more heavily armed, less isolated and more closely connected to Russia and China. It therefore has less incentive to make the kind of concessions Washington sought during Trump's first term. For Trump, another summit could offer an opportunity to lower tensions and revive the leader-to-leader diplomacy that became a hallmark of his first term. But with North Korea now more heavily armed and geopolitically stronger, expectations of a sweeping agreement are likely to be considerably lower. Instead, any renewed engagement could focus on narrower objectives, such as restoring communication, reducing the risk of military escalation and reaching understandings on missile testing or crisis management. As Park put it, diplomatic engagement need not resolve the nuclear dispute entirely to have value.
