title: Pune property owners, landlords, PG owners, alert! Do this or face police action; tenants must pay attention, too
content:
Pune's registration department has issued a clear warning to property owners across the city. Landlords and Paying Guest (PG) operators must register their leave-and-licence agreements or risk police action. As many as 175 landlords and PG operators have faced action in just two weeks. Pune has a large floating population of students, professionals, and businesspersons from across Maharashtra and other states. Many reside in rented accommodation without formal agreements in place. Property owners must opt for registered leave and licence agreements. Notarised rent pacts are not sufficient under the current drive. Action is being taken under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Violations of orders issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita are also being pursued. Registered agreements now connect directly to the police system. Once a leave and licence agreement is registered online, the tenant's information is automatically shared with the police department. This happens through the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS). Property owners no longer need to submit tenant details to the police separately. Abhaysinh Mohite, deputy inspector general (IT) of the registration department, confirmed this integration to The Times of India. The department's i-SARITA system is now linked with CCTNS across Maharashtra. "Once a leave and licence agreement is registered online, the tenant information is automatically shared with the police department through the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS). Property owners do not need to submit it separately," Abhaysinh Mohite told TOI. Police stations can now check whether a tenancy has been registered before taking action against an owner. The police drive is focused on properties with no registered leave and licence agreement on record. Landlords and PG operators who failed to furnish the local police station with tenant details have also been targeted. Deputy Commissioner of Police Prashant Amrutkar confirmed the drive would be intensified. The campaign is being conducted under the guidance of Pune Commissioner of Police Amitesh Kumar and Joint CP Sanjay Darade. "From the data available with us, we can identify registered leave-and-licence agreements,” DCP Amrutkar told the publication. Action has been reported across Kothrud, Deccan, Ambegaon, Narhe, Chatushrungi, Khadki, Lonikand, Loni Kalbhor and other parts of the city. Property owners must register agreements through the citizens' portal. Sachin Shingvi of the Association of Service Providers urged owners to register agreements for the sake of public safety and law and order. Tenants must also ensure their landlords have completed the registration process. "Earlier, there was some trouble in sharing the tenancy data between the registration department and the police. Now, it is being done seamlessly,” he said. “Property owners must provide tenant information to the police in the interest of public peace, law and order, and security. We are creating awareness among citizens to register agreements online through the citizens' portal," he added. Sounak Mukhopadhyay covers trending news, sports and entertainment for LiveMint. title: Ladakh channels 90 million litres of glacier melt daily to 12 villages: 'This successful model is just a blueprint'
content:
Ladakh has started redirecting nearly 90 million litres of glacier-melt water every day into the Igoo-Phey Irrigation Canal, in a move aimed at strengthening water security and supporting farming in the region. The additional water is expected to benefit nearly 12 villages and increase irrigation coverage to more than 1,000 acres of farmland, The New Indian Express reported. Water from the Stok village Nallah in Leh had previously flowed into the Indus without being used for irrigation. The administration has now diverted part of the flow into the existing canal through basic earthwork, without incurring any capital expenditure, an official told Express. Although Ladakh has significant glacier and snowmelt resources, many parts of the region continue to face shortages of water for farming. Lt Governor V K Saxena identified locations where substantial amounts of glacier water were reaching the Indus and directed efforts to put the water to agricultural use. “On the directions of LG on August 14, the Irrigation and Flood Control Department successfully diverted excess glacier water from the main water channel of Nallah to the Igoo-Phey Canal by creating two trenches using a JCB,” the official was quoted as saying by Express. The Stok Nallah was found to have a discharge of around 36.60 cusecs, which works out to nearly 90 million litres a day. Two diversion channels have been created to send an additional 26 cusecs into the Igoo-Phey Canal — 19 cusecs towards Igoo village and seven cusecs towards Phey. Authorities are also working on plans to use the remaining 10 cusecs. The 43-km Igoo-Phey Canal was built in phases between 1979 and 2005. Around 200 metres of the canal runs underground, allowing the Stok Nallah to pass above it without disrupting the canal's water flow. Despite having access to the water source, the canal had suffered from inadequate water for several decades, leaving some sections defunct. “By intercepting and utilising this daily flow of 90 million litres, the administration has proven the feasibility of large-scale water diversion to bolster the region's cold desert agriculture. Crucially, this intervention will substantially augment the total water flow in the Igoo-Phey Canal, increasing it from the present 50 cusecs to nearly 80 cusecs,” the official told Express. Until now, water from the canal was supplied to villages according to a roster because of limited availability. The additional flow is expected to allow all 12 villages to receive water every day and expand irrigation across more than 1,000 acres. “The farmers will experience higher crop yields, leading to increased farm incomes, greater employment opportunities, and a revitalised rural economy,” the official told Express. Saxena said diverting 90 million litres of glacier water each day into the Igoo-Phey and Yokyur canals showed that large-scale water management could be achieved in Ladakh. He described the initiative as a major step “toward our vision of a Green, Water-Secure, and Self-Sustaining Ladakh. This successful model is just a blueprint. We will expand these cost-effective interventions across Ladakh, transforming scattered glacier flows into a permanent lifeline for agricultural prosperity, revitalised rural economies, and long-term climate resilience for the people of Ladakh”. The administration has identified several other streams near the Igoo-Phey Canal network for similar projects. These include Matho Nallah, Tuchik Chenmo Nallah, Tuchik Chon Nallah and Stakna Nallah. title: Harvard, NYU to come to India next year? Sergio Gor says top US universities ‘interested' amid ‘demand’: What he said
content:
Several leading American universities, including Harvard, New York University and Purdue, are exploring the possibility of establishing a presence in India amid strong interest among Indian students in studying in the US, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said at The Economic Times World Leaders Forum. Gor also stated he had recently spoken to the provost of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and was working to bring some US universities to India within the next year. “One of the things that I've started looking at is actually bringing US institutions to India. The demand is there,” he mentioned, adding, “We have a great amount of universities that are interested in coming here, and I'm determined over the next year, that we will have some of that happen, and we're talking about the top schools, whether that's NYU, Harvard or Purdue, we're gonna see some of that happening over the near future. And we're confident that that'll happen." Gor said Washington was committed to deepening ties with India and working closely with its young talent. He pointed to collaboration between Indian professionals and major US companies such as Google, Microsoft and Micron as examples of the partnership between the two countries. “And so you pick any US company, there's incredible Indian talent. So whether that's Google or Microsoft or Micron, those are good things that we're working together on. And that's something that'll continue to happen,” Gor stated. He described people-to-people relations between India and the US as “unmatched”. However, he said the overwhelming demand among people seeking to move to the US meant the country could not accommodate everyone. “There's such a high demand of people wanting to go to the United States. It would be impossible for us to accommodate the whole world,” he said. Gor clarified the Trump administration’s enhanced visa screening was not specifically aimed at India, stressing that Washington’s priority was to maintain secure borders and determine who enters the US, as per The Economic Times report. He said the screening process now includes examining applicants’ online activity, including their posts and statements on platforms such as X, YouTube and other forums. Gor noted that people who have publicly expressed sentiments such as “Death to America” should not expect to be granted a US visa. “And unfortunately, and this is, again, this is not targeted towards India, but the days of you tweeting Death to America, and then showing up in an embassy asking for a visa are over. We're not gonna let you in,” he stated. Gor said India, too, had the authority to determine who could enter its territory. He also mentioned that curbing visa overstays and strengthening security along the US southern border remained key priorities for the Trump administration “And by the way, India does the exact same thing. When you're coming here, applying for a visa, you get asked all sorts of questions. And several people get denied, frankly. And that's India's right. You should be able to determine who is allowed into your country,” Gor said. “In previous administrations, we had millions of individuals who would overstay their visas in the United States. So today, that is a top priority for this administration,” he further said. Garvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram. title: भारत को 'विश्व की फार्मेसी' से 'विश्व की प्रयोगशाला' बनने की दिशा में आगे बढ़ना चाहिए; कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता को मानवीय नैदानिक निर्णय का पूरक होना चाहिए, न कि उसका स्थान लेना चाहिए: केंद्रीय मंत्री श्रीमती अनुप्रिया पटेल

                        केंद्रीय स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण एवं रसायन एवं उर्वरक राज्य मंत्री श्रीमती अनुप्रिया पटेल ने कहा कि भारत को 'विश्व की फार्मेसी' होने से आगे बढ़कर अनुसंधान, नवाचार और उभरती प्रौद्योगिकियों द्वारा संचालित 'विश्व की प्रयोगशाला' बनना चाहिए।
आज अहमदाबाद स्थित आईआईएमए में "स्वास्थ्य सेवा में एआई को बढ़ावा देना" विषय पर आयोजित आईआईएमए हेल्थकेयर समिट 2026 के तीसरे संस्करण को संबोधित करते हुए मंत्री जी ने कोविड-19 महामारी के दौरान भारत के योगदान पर प्रकाश डाला। उन्होंने कहा कि भारतीय दवा उद्योग ने 200 से अधिक देशों को टीकों और आवश्यक चिकित्सा उत्पादों की निर्बाध आपूर्ति सुनिश्चित की, जबकि भारत के टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के तहत 220 करोड़ से अधिक खुराकें दी गईं।
कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) की परिवर्तनकारी शक्ति के बारे में बोलते हुए, मंत्री जी ने दवा खोज में तेजी लाने, व्यक्तिगत उपचारों को सक्षम बनाने और बेहतर स्क्रीनिंग, नैदानिक निर्णय लेने और रोग निगरानी के माध्यम से स्वास्थ्य सेवा वितरण को मजबूत करने की इसकी क्षमता पर प्रकाश डाला। मंत्री जी ने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि एआई को अपनाना सुरक्षित, जिम्मेदार और मानव-केंद्रित होना चाहिए , जिसमें रोगी की गोपनीयता के लिए मजबूत सुरक्षा उपाय हों और प्रौद्योगिकी मानव नैदानिक निर्णय का पूरक हो, न कि उसका स्थान ले। उन्होंने सरकार, शिक्षाविदों, स्वास्थ्य संस्थानों, स्टार्टअप्स और उद्योग के बीच मजबूत सहयोग के माध्यम से पायलट परियोजनाओं से जनसंख्या स्तर पर कार्यान्वयन की ओर बढ़ने का आह्वान किया। उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि स्वास्थ्य सेवा में एआई के लिए उत्कृष्टता केंद्र एम्स नई दिल्ली, पीजीआईएमईआर चंडीगढ़ और एम्स ऋषिकेश में स्थापित किए गए हैं।
मंत्री जी ने कहा कि सरकार की 5,000 करोड़ रुपये की फार्मा-मेडटेक सेक्टर में अनुसंधान और नवाचार प्रोत्साहन (पीआरआईपी) योजना का उद्देश्य अनुसंधान और उद्योग-अकादमिक सहयोग को मजबूत करना तथा नवाचार-आधारित विकास की दिशा में परिवर्तन को बढ़ावा देना है। मंत्री जी ने केंद्रीय बजट में घोषित 10,000 करोड़ रुपये के बायोफार्मा शक्ति मिशन पर भी प्रकाश डाला , जिसका उद्देश्य बायोलॉजिक्स और बायोसिमिलर्स में क्षमताओं को मजबूत करना, कुशल मानव संसाधन विकसित करना, नियामक और नैदानिक परीक्षण क्षमताओं को मजबूत करना और घरेलू जैव-औषधीय इको- सिस्टम को समर्थन देना है।
औषधि विभाग के सचिव श्री मनोज जोशी ने औषधि एवं स्वास्थ्य सेवा क्षेत्रों में कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) के बढ़ते उपयोग पर प्रकाश डाला। उन्होंने कहा कि जहां बड़ी औषधि कंपनियां उत्पादन, मानव संसाधन, विपणन, वितरण और इन्वेंट्री प्रबंधन के लिए एआई का तेजी से उपयोग कर रही हैं, वहीं स्टार्टअप, विशेष रूप से बेंगलुरु और हैदराबाद में, औषधि खोज के लिए एआई का लाभ उठा रहे हैं। इससे संभावित औषधि उम्मीदवारों की तेजी से पहचान और चयन करने में मदद मिल रही है और औषधि खोज में लगने वाला समय काफी कम हो रहा है।
उन्होंने पूंजी, सॉफ्टवेयर लाइसेंसिंग, कंप्यूटिंग क्षमता और विशेषीकृत प्रतिभा से संबंधित चुनौतियों पर प्रकाश डाला और कहा कि सरकार राष्ट्रीय बायोफार्मा मिशन और इंडियाएआई मिशन सहित कई पहलों के माध्यम से इन चुनौतियों का समाधान करने के लिए काम कर रही है । श्री जोशी ने यह भी बताया कि सरकार फार्मास्यूटिकल्स में एआई-आधारित नवाचार को मजबूत करने के लिए योग्य स्टार्टअप्स को सॉफ्टवेयर लाइसेंसिंग और परिचालन लागतों के लिए पर्याप्त सहायता प्रदान करने की दिशा में काम कर रही है।
श्री जोशी ने उचित सुरक्षा उपायों के साथ भारतीय नवप्रवर्तकों के लिए स्वास्थ्य सेवा और आनुवंशिक डेटा को सुलभ बनाने के महत्व पर जोर दिया और नैदानिक परीक्षणों, सटीक चिकित्सा और रोगी-स्तर के स्वास्थ्य सेवा डेटा के डिजिटलीकरण में एआई की क्षमता पर बल दिया।
स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण विभाग की सचिव श्रीमती पुण्य सलीला श्रीवास्तव ने सशक्त डिजिटल स्वास्थ्य इको- सिस्टम के निर्माण और कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के जिम्मेदार, साक्ष्य-आधारित उपयोग को बढ़ावा देने के लिए सरकार के प्रयासों पर प्रकाश डाला। उन्होंने कहा कि आयुष्मान भारत डिजिटल मिशन (एबीडीएम) एक अंतरसंचालनीय, खुले मानकों पर आधारित डिजिटल स्वास्थ्य इको- सिस्टम का निर्माण कर रहा है, जिसमें 96 करोड़ से अधिक एबीएचए आईडी और 1,000 करोड़ से अधिक स्वास्थ्य रिकॉर्ड स्वास्थ्य सुविधाओं और पेशेवरों के बीच डिजिटल रूप से जुड़े हुए हैं।
उन्होंने तपेदिक और मधुमेह रेटिनोपैथी जैसी बीमारियों का शीघ्र पता लगाने के लिए एआई-आधारित अनुप्रयोगों के साथ-साथ ई- संजीवनी के माध्यम से एआई-आधारित नैदानिक निर्णय सहायता के बारे में बात की, ई- संजीवनी से 20 करोड़ से अधिक रोगियों को लाभ हुआ है । उन्होंने गोपनीयता, जिम्मेदार एआई, साक्ष्य-आधारित नवाचार और सरकार, शिक्षाविदों, स्टार्टअप और उद्योग के बीच सहयोग पर जोर दिया, साथ ही डेटासेट, एआई मॉडल और टूलकिट तक पहुंच को लोकतांत्रिक बनाने के लिए इंडियाएआई मिशन और एआईकोश पर प्रकाश डाला।
आईआईएमए बोर्ड ऑफ गवर्नर्स के अध्यक्ष और ज़ाइडस लाइफसाइंसेज के चेयरमैन श्री पंकज पटेल ने दवा खोज से लेकर रोगी देखभाल तक, स्वास्थ्य सेवा मूल्य श्रृंखला में एआई की परिवर्तनकारी क्षमता के बारे में बात की। उन्होंने कहा कि एआई संभावित दवा उम्मीदवारों की पहचान में तेजी ला सकता है, नैदानिक परीक्षण डिजाइन और रोगी भर्ती में सहायता कर सकता है और शोधकर्ताओं को विफलताओं की शीघ्र पहचान करने में मदद कर सकता है।
इस कार्यक्रम के दौरान, इंडियन फार्मास्युटिकल अलायंस (आईपीए) द्वारा आईआईएम अहमदाबाद आर्काइव्स के सहयोग से शुरू की गई डिजिटल पहल, इंडिया फार्मा आर्काइव्स (https://indiapharmaarchives.com ) का अनावरण किया गया। इसका उद्देश्य भारत के फार्मास्युटिकल उद्योग के विकास को दस्तावेज़ित और संरक्षित करना है। एक जीवंत संग्रह के रूप में निर्मित, यह मौखिक इतिहास, अभिलेखीय दस्तावेज़, तस्वीरें और दुर्लभ मीडिया को एक साथ लाता है, जो पिछले एक सदी में इस क्षेत्र को आकार देने वाले लोगों, संस्थानों और उपलब्धियों को दर्शाता है। भारत में कोविड-19 वैक्सीन के विकास पर एक पुस्तक भी जारी की गई, जो वैश्विक स्वास्थ्य संकट के प्रति देश की वैज्ञानिक, फार्मास्युटिकल और संस्थागत प्रतिक्रिया के एक महत्वपूर्ण अध्याय को दर्शाती है।
आईआईएमए हेल्थकेयर समिट 2026 का आयोजन इंडियन इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ मैनेजमेंट अहमदाबाद (आईआईएमए) द्वारा किया गया था, जिसमें नीति निर्माताओं, स्वास्थ्य सेवा उद्योग के हितधारकों और शिक्षाविदों को एक साथ लाया गया ताकि भारत सरकार के इंडियाएआई मिशन और 2047 तक एक स्वस्थ और विकसित भारत के दृष्टिकोण के अनुरूप "स्वास्थ्य सेवा में एआई को आगे बढ़ाना" विषय पर विचार-विमर्श किया जा सके ।

title: Flood survivor elephant ‘Joymoti’ airlifted from Northeast to Vantara for treatment
content:
Joymoti, a 53-year-old female elephant rescued after devastating floods in Nagaland and Assam in July, has been airlifted to Vantara in Jamnagar for urgent and specialised veterinary treatment.
Joymoti was swept away by floodwaters in Nagaland during the second week of July. Local communities, with support from government agencies, later rescued her.
The elephant suffered several injuries in the incident, including wounds on her forehead, right ear, the area above her tail, left inner thigh and abdomen. She also had a deep wound around her external genital area that had become infested with maggots.
Her right eye has suffered severe damage, leaving her blind in that eye and causing persistent watering.
Joymoti also has a long-standing problem with her left hind leg after suffering a fracture during logging. The injury has affected her ability to walk normally and makes it difficult for her to reach food and water.
After her rescue, she was given first aid and basic veterinary treatment locally. This included wound dressing, pain medication, multivitamin and mineral supplements and other supportive care.
However, doctors determined that her multiple and serious injuries, advanced age and existing mobility problems required treatment at a specialised veterinary hospital.
Her transfer to Vantara was carried out specifically to provide immediate and specialised medical care. The decision to airlift her was taken considering her health and welfare, while also reducing the time and physical strain associated with a long journey by road.
At Vantara, Joymoti will undergo a detailed veterinary examination. She will receive treatment for her injuries and damaged eye, along with nutritional and other supportive care based on her medical needs.
This comes days after a teenager from West Bengal, who had been spending long periods in ponds to ease a severe burning sensation on his body, was airlifted to Mumbai for specialised medical treatment.
Iqbal, a resident of Beldanga, reportedly began staying in ponds for hours, including overnight, because leaving the water triggered an intense burning sensation across his body. A video showing him eating snacks while remaining underwater went viral on social media, drawing attention to his condition.
Following the circulation of the footage, a team of medical specialists examined Iqbal. Anant Ambani later offered medical assistance to the teenager's family and arranged for him to be taken to Mumbai for further evaluation and treatment.
Iqbal was subsequently admitted to Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital, where doctors began a detailed assessment of his condition and started treatment.
His parents said they had previously taken him to doctors for medical care, but his condition had not improved significantly. They also said the family was unable to afford prolonged treatment, making it difficult to continue seeking specialised medical help.

title: Delhi records 1,777 H1N1 cases; health ministry lists symptoms to watch for as flu infections rise across India
content:
Delhi has recorded 1,777 H1N1 cases this year, including 114 reported on Thursday, as several states report a rise in influenza and flu-like illnesses. Union Health Minister J P Nadda on Friday reviewed the national influenza situation and healthcare preparedness to manage seasonal infections, PTI reported. The Health Ministry has also urged people to remain alert to symptoms of swine flu. In a post on X on Saturday, it said H1N1 can cause fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue. Other symptoms listed in the advisory include lethargy, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, joint and muscle pain and diarrhoea. The ministry advised people not to ignore persistent symptoms and to seek medical advice at the nearest healthcare centre. The capital has recorded 2,602 influenza cases so far this year, including 2,392 Influenza-A infections and 210 Influenza-B cases, with H1N1 accounting for the majority of Influenza-A infections, according to Delhi health department data. The health department reported 159 new influenza cases on Thursday, including 114 H1N1 cases. Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the capital was fully equipped to handle the seasonal rise in infections. Singh made the remarks after attending a meeting chaired by Union Health Minister Nadda to review preparedness for seasonal influenza and vector-borne diseases. On Friday, Nadda reviewed the national surveillance and epidemiological situation, trends in influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infections (SARI), testing and laboratory surveillance, and preparedness of healthcare facilities to manage seasonal influenza cases. According to the health department, there is no shortage of hospital beds, doctors, medicines or essential medical equipment in Delhi. It said patient numbers were being monitored and hospital arrangements were being strengthened according to requirements. Of the 2,392 Influenza-A cases recorded in Delhi this year, 1,777 are H1N1, while 37 are H1, 138 are H3 and 440 fall under other Influenza-A categories. The 210 Influenza-B cases include 200 Victoria strain infections and 10 other cases. Seasonal influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses circulating globally. The Delhi health department said young children and elderly people with co-morbidities are among those most vulnerable to the infection. H1N1 symptoms can include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, chills and fatigue. In some cases, particularly among vulnerable groups, influenza can lead to serious complications. The most vulnerable include the elderly and those suffering from diabetes, hypertension and chronic kidney disease. India generally experiences two seasonal influenza peaks each year, between January and March and during the post-monsoon period. H1N1 is the predominant subtype in Delhi this year, while H3N2 was predominant last year, the department said. The increase is not limited to Delhi. According to a report by The Hindu, H1N1 and influenza-like illnesses are rising in cities including Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai, while Kerala has recorded a significantly higher number of cases and deaths. In Mumbai, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation recorded 309 H1N1 cases between June 1 and August 15, compared with 72 during the same period in 2025. Bengaluru has also reported an increase in influenza-like illnesses, viral fever and respiratory infections, particularly among children. Doctors at Bengaluru's Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health were reportedly confirming around two to three H1N1 cases a day among children who were tested. Paediatricians in Chennai have also reported H1N1 cases among children over the past two weeks, with a slight increase during the latest week, The Hindu reported. Kerala has recorded a much larger number of influenza cases and deaths than the other states. The state recorded 526 Influenza-A cases and six deaths in May, which rose to 2,050 cases and 26 deaths in June and 2,899 cases and 31 deaths in July. Up to August 17, another 1,476 cases and 21 deaths were reported. The cumulative tally stood at 7,421 cases and 88 deaths, with almost all fatalities reported among people aged over 50. However, the situation is not uniform across the country. Telangana health officials said H1N1 cases were lower than during the corresponding period last year. The Delhi State Health Mission is monitoring influenza through the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme, tracking morbidity and mortality associated with the infection. The State Surveillance Unit is also monitoring daily data on influenza, influenza-like illness and severe acute respiratory infection cases through the IDSP-IHIP portal. The health department said advisories have been issued to hospitals and district officials on screening, reporting and monitoring influenza and COVID-19 cases. It has also circulated guidelines covering patient categorisation, treatment, ventilatory management, mask use and home care. Authorities have advised people to maintain respiratory hygiene, use masks in crowded places, wash their hands frequently and avoid close contact with people suffering from respiratory illnesses. The department has also advised people not to take medicines without consulting a doctor. title: 'Manan Mishra will remain president as long as...': BCI chief hits back at critics, refuses to resign
content:
Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman and BJP MP Manan Kumar Mishra has refused to step down from his post, saying he is an elected representative of the country's lawyers and has the support of more than two-thirds of BCI members. Mishra's remarks came after BCI Co-Chairman YR Sadasiva Reddy sought his resignation within 15 days, alleging financial and administrative irregularities in the functioning of the Council. "I am an elected representative. I was neither selected nor nominated to the Bar Council of India," Mishra told ANI, explaining that the BCI is a statutory body established under the Advocates Act. Mishra said more than 2.5 million lawyers across the country participate in the electoral system, first electing representatives to State Bar Councils, whose representatives then elect members of the BCI. These members collectively elect the chairman and vice-chairman. "This is my seventh term. I have been elected unopposed for the last six terms. Even today, more than two-thirds of the Bar Council members support me," he said. In a six-page letter to Mishra on Saturday, Reddy called on him to resign and raised several allegations, including the alleged transfer of ₹150 crore of BCI funds to a private trust, Live Law reported. Reddy alleged that the Council's existing trust was rendered inactive before a new trust, BCI Trust PEARL – First, was registered on September 17, 2020, with trustees allegedly chosen by Mishra. According to Reddy's letter, a resolution was subsequently moved to transfer ₹150 crore of BCI funds, comprising contributions from advocates across the country, to the trust. Reddy questioned the legal basis for the alleged transfer, saying he knew of no provision under the Advocates Act, 1961, that allowed the corpus of a statutory regulator to be transferred to a private trust registered by its chairman. He also alleged that law colleges seeking BCI approval or renewal were asked to make contributions to the trust, ranging from ₹25 lakh to ₹1 crore. Reddy further alleged that a large number of Council employees were associated with Mishra personally, including members of his family, and claimed the Council had not received records of advertisements, selection committees or merit lists supporting these appointments. Mishra rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless. Regarding the trust, he said its functioning was transparent and that its managing trustees included BCI members and senior advocates. "Anyone is welcome to examine the accounts; the trust undergoes an annual audit," Mishra said, adding that the audit report is incorporated into the budget, published and made available in the public domain. He also rejected allegations relating to the appointment of relatives, saying there was no substance to the claims. Reddy's letter also referred to the controversy surrounding NALSAR University, Hyderabad. On August 13, Mishra had issued a directive asking State Bar Councils not to enrol students from NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch. Reddy criticised the directive, saying it was issued without placing material before the Council or passing a resolution approving the decision. The directive was withdrawn hours later. The episode led to criticism from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and spokesperson Saurav Das. Dipke called for Mishra's resignation, following which Mishra responded on August 14 and said the BCI's interests were similar to those of the satirical party. Separately, a petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging Mishra's continuation as BCI chairman. According to ANI, the plea alleges that Mishra's tenure has continued for more than a decade in violation of the governing rules. It questions the legality of his uninterrupted tenure and cites Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules, which the petitioner contends prescribes a two-year term for the chairman. Mishra, however, has maintained that his position is based on the electoral support of lawyers. "Manan Mishra will remain president as long as the country's lawyers, the voters, want him to stay," he told ANI. A postgraduate in History from the University of Delhi, Prabhakar combines strong editorial judgment with a keen interest in public policy, governance, economics, and global affairs. Before joining LiveMint, he worked with leading digital publications, including News9Live and The Times of India, where he handled breaking news, copy editing, headline writing, live coverage, and newsroom coordination.

title: “मिशन जीरो-स्वच्छता कार्यों में होने वाली मौतों को समाप्त करना” पर राष्ट्रीय कार्यशाला
content:
सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय 
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    “मिशन जीरो-स्वच्छता कार्यों में होने वाली मौतों को समाप्त करना” पर राष्ट्रीय कार्यशाला
                              
                              
                                    
स्वच्छता कार्यों में शून्य मृत्यु दर प्राप्त करना माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के विजन के अंतर्गत एक प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकता है; सुरक्षित, व्यवस्थित और सम्मानजनक स्वच्छता सेवाएं सुनिश्चित करने के लिए समग्र सरकारी दृष्टिकोण की आवश्यकता है: सचिव सुधांश पंत
नमस्ते, गरिमा योजनाएं मशीनीकरण को बढ़ावा देने और स्वच्छता कर्मचारियों और उनके आश्रितों के लिए व्यावसायिक सुरक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा और आजीविका के अवसर सुनिश्चित करने के लिए हैं
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        आज ओडिशा के भुवनेश्वर स्थित लोकसेवा भवन के राज्य सम्मेलन केंद्र में संस्थागत तंत्र को मजबूत करने, उपयुक्त प्रौद्योगिकियों को बढ़ावा देने, परिचालन तत्परता सुनिश्चित करने और देश भर के शहरों में मशीनो से स्वच्छता सेवाओं को बढ़ाने के उद्देश्य से, "मिशन जीरो: स्वच्छता कार्य में होने वाली मौतों को समाप्त करना" विषय पर एक राष्ट्रीय कार्यशाला का आयोजन किया गया।
इस कार्यशाला में ओडिशा के माननीय मुख्यमंत्री श्री मोहन चरण मांझी ने शिरकत की। उपस्थित अन्य गणमान्य व्यक्तियों में भारत सरकार के सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के सचिव श्री सुधांश पंत; ओडिशा सरकार की मुख्य सचिव श्रीमती अनु गर्ग; ओडिशा सरकार के आवास एवं शहरी विकास विभाग की अपर मुख्य सचिव श्रीमती उषा पाधी; सीपीएचईईओ के सलाहकार श्री वी.के. चौरसिया; डब्ल्यूएटीसीओ के प्रबंध निदेशक श्री देबब्रत मोहंती; नमस्ते कार्यक्रम के कार्यान्वयन के लिए नोडल एजेंसी एनएसकेएफडीसी के प्रबंध निदेशक श्री प्रभात कुमार सिंह; यूएमसी की सुश्री मेघना मल्होत्रा और श्री ज़ेरक्स राव; भुवनेश्वर नगर निगम के नगर आयुक्त श्री चंचल राणा (आईएएस); और पिंपरी चिंचवड नगर निगम के नगर आयुक्त डॉ. विजय सूर्यवंशी (आईएएस) शामिल थे।
  
वरिष्ठ सरकारी अधिकारी, शहरी स्थानीय निकाय (यूएलबी), स्वच्छता क्षेत्र के विशेषज्ञ, निर्माता, प्रौद्योगिकी प्रदाता, नागरिक समाज संगठन और स्वच्छता कार्यकर्ता एक सुरक्षित, सम्मानजनक और पूरी तरह से मशीनों से स्वच्छता प्रणाली के निर्माण पर विचार-विमर्श करेंगे।
कार्यशाला का मुख्य उद्देश्य स्वच्छता कार्यों में होने वाली मौतों को शून्य तक पहुंचाने के समग्र लक्ष्य के साथ संस्थागत तंत्रों को मजबूत करना, उपयुक्त प्रौद्योगिकियों को बढ़ावा देना, परिचालन तत्परता सुनिश्चित करना और शहरों में मशीनों से स्वच्छता सेवाओं का विस्तार करना था।
 
कार्यशाला को संबोधित करते हुए सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के सचिव श्री सुधांश पंत ने दोहराया कि स्वच्छता कार्यों में शून्य मृत्यु दर प्राप्त करना माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के दृष्टिकोण के अंतर्गत एक प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकता है। उन्होंने स्वच्छता सेवाओं को सुरक्षित, व्यवस्थित और सम्मानपूर्वक प्रदान करने के लिए सरकार के समग्र दृष्टिकोण की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया।
श्री पंत ने बताया कि मशीनीकरण को बढ़ावा देने और सफाई कर्मचारियों और उनके आश्रितों के लिए व्यावसायिक सुरक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा और आजीविका के अवसर सुनिश्चित करने के लिए नमस्ते और गरिमा योजनाएं लागू की जा रही हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि 2024 में शुरू किए गए स्वच्छता सारथी/कचरा बीनने वाले घटक ने कचरा बीनने वालों को सामाजिक और आर्थिक सशक्तिकरण पहलों के दायरे में लाकर ढांचे को और मजबूत किया है।
 
सचिव ने आगे कहा कि आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया स्वच्छता इकाइयों (ईआरएसयू) के माध्यम से व्यवस्थित स्वच्छता सेवा वितरण सुनिश्चित करने, मिशन जीरो एजेंडा को आगे बढ़ाने और स्वच्छता कर्मचारियों और उनके परिवारों के लिए कल्याणकारी उपायों की व्यापकता प्राप्त करने के उद्देश्य से नमस्ते कार्यक्रम को 2031 तक बढ़ा दिया गया है।
 
इस कार्यशाला ने हितधारकों को अनुभव साझा करने, नवाचारों को प्रदर्शित करने और सुरक्षित स्वच्छता संचालन के लिए व्यावहारिक समाधानों पर चर्चा करने के लिए एक मंच भी प्रदान किया।
सचिव ने सुरक्षा उपकरण और साजो-सामान के बाज़ार का दौरा किया और हितधारकों से बातचीत की, जहां स्वच्छता कर्मचारियों की सुरक्षा और कार्यक्षमता बढ़ाने के लिए डिज़ाइन की गई प्रौद्योगिकियों और उपकरणों का प्रदर्शन किया गया। उन्होंने कचरा बीनने वालों और स्वच्छता कर्मचारियों से बने 'कचरे से धन' स्वयं सहायता समूहों द्वारा स्थापित स्टालों का भी दौरा किया, जहां आजीविका सृजन, उद्यमिता और टिकाऊ अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन के अवसरों के बारे में बताया गया।
गौरतलब है कि इस कार्यक्रम में भारत सरकार और ओडिशा सरकार के प्रतिनिधियों, शहरी स्थानीय निकायों के वरिष्ठ अधिकारियों, सीपीएचईईओ, स्वच्छता क्षेत्र के संस्थानों, नागरिक समाज संगठनों, प्रौद्योगिकी और उपकरण प्रदाताओं के साथ-साथ स्वच्छता कर्मचारी एक साथ आए।
विभिन्न हितधारकों की भागीदारी ने खतरनाक मैनुअल स्वच्छता प्रथाओं को समाप्त करने के लिए सरकारों, शहरी स्थानीय निकायों, प्रौद्योगिकी प्रदाताओं और समुदायों के बीच समन्वित कार्रवाई के महत्व का उल्लेख किया।
कार्यशाला ने एक सुरक्षित, गरिमापूर्ण, प्रौद्योगिकी-संचालित और टिकाऊ स्वच्छता प्रणाली के निर्माण के प्रति सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता की पुष्टि की, जहां स्वच्छता कर्तव्यों का पालन करते समय किसी भी स्वच्छता कर्मी की जान न जाए।
मिशन जीरो दृष्टिकोण का उद्देश्य मशीनीकरण, संस्थागत तैयारी, श्रमिक सुरक्षा, सामाजिक सुरक्षा और आजीविका सहायता के माध्यम से स्वच्छता कार्य में परिवर्तन लाना है, जिससे पूरे देश में स्वच्छता कार्यों में होने वाली मौतों को शून्य तक लाने का मार्ग प्रशस्त हो सके।
***

title: अधिकार प्राप्‍त समिति ने महिला नेतृत्व वाले ग्रामीण उद्यमों के विकास में तेजी लाने के प्रस्तावों की समीक्षा की
content:
ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    अधिकार प्राप्त समिति ने महिला नेतृत्व वाले ग्रामीण उद्यमों के विकास में तेजी लाने के प्रस्तावों की समीक्षा की
                              
                              
                                    
                              
                        
                        
                              प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 9:53AM by PIB Delhi
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        श्री रोहित कंसल, सचिव (ग्रामीण विकास) की अध्यक्षता में ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय की अधिकार प्राप्त समिति ने आज महिला नेतृत्व वाले ग्रामीण उद्यमों को मजबूत करने और उनका विस्तार करने तथा लघु स्वयं सहायता समूह उद्यमों को उच्च स्तरीय, विकासोन्मुखी व्यवसायों में परिवर्तित होने का मार्ग प्रशस्त करने के लिए डीएवाई-एनआरएलएम के गैर-कृषि आजीविका (एनएफएल) घटक के अंतर्गत प्रस्तावों पर विचार किया ।
 
इस बैठक में संयुक्त सचिव (ग्रामीण आजीविका) श्री अमित शुक्ला और संयुक्त सचिव (ग्रामीण आजीविका) सुश्री स्वाति शर्मा भी उपस्थित थे। चर्चा का मुख्य विषय ग्रामीण महिलाओं के लिए उद्यमिता आधारित आजीविका के अवसरों को बढ़ावा देना और 6 करोड़ लखपति दीदियां बनाने के राष्ट्रीय लक्ष्य में योगदान देना था।
 
समिति ने बिहार, जम्मू और कश्मीर, उत्तर प्रदेश और गुजरात से चार नए इनक्यूबेटर प्रस्तावों पर विचार किया, जिनमें क्रमशः आईआईटी पटना, आईआईएम जम्मू, आईआईएम लखनऊ और आईआईटी गांधीनगर को प्रस्तावित इनक्यूबेटर भागीदार के रूप में शामिल किया गया है। ये प्रस्ताव संबंधित राज्यों के प्रधान सचिवों/सचिवों, राज्य मिशन निदेशकों/एसआरएलएम के सीईओ और प्रस्तावित इनक्यूबेटर संस्थानों के प्रतिनिधियों द्वारा प्रस्तुत किए गए। इन चारों कार्यक्रमों के माध्यम से व्यावसायिक रणनीति, मार्गदर्शन, वित्तीय योजना, औपचारिकीकरण, प्रौद्योगिकी अपनाने, बाजार पहुंच और वित्त तक पहुंच जैसे क्षेत्रों में व्यवस्थित उपायों द्वारा 600 से अधिक उच्च क्षमता वाले ग्रामीण उद्यमों को सहायता प्रदान करने का प्रस्ताव है।
 
इन्क्यूबेटर उप-योजना असम, बिहार, पश्चिम बंगाल और कर्नाटक में सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न हुए चार इन्क्यूबेटर कार्यक्रमों के अनुभव पर आधारित है, जिन्होंने 600 से अधिक स्वयं सहायता समूह (एसएचजी) उद्यमों को सहयोग प्रदान किया। कार्यक्रम का तब से काफी विस्तार हुआ है और वर्तमान में 13 राज्यों में 14 इन्क्यूबेटर कार्यक्रम चल रहे हैं, जो आईआईएम, आईआईटी और प्रमुख इन्क्यूबेशन संस्थानों सहित प्रमुख व्यावसायिक और शैक्षणिक संस्थानों के साथ साझेदारी के माध्यम से लगभग 2,100 ग्रामीण स्वयं सहायता समूह (एसएचजी) उद्यमों को सहयोग प्रदान कर रहे हैं। पूर्व के कार्यक्रमों ने राजस्व वृद्धि, व्यवसाय के औपचारिकरण में सुधार और अतिरिक्त रोजगार सृजन सहित ठोस परिणाम प्रदर्शित किए हैं।
 
नए इनक्यूबेटर खाद्य एवं कृषि-प्रसंस्करण, वस्त्र एवं हस्तशिल्प, विनिर्माण, खुदरा एवं सेवाएं, पर्यटन से जुड़ी गतिविधियां, डिजिटल उद्यम और अन्य स्थानीय रूप से प्रासंगिक विकास क्षेत्रों पर ध्यान देंगे। एक प्रमुख विशेषता यह है कि मजबूत विकास क्षमता वाले उद्यमों के चयन के लिए एक पारदर्शी, योग्यता-आधारित चुनौती कोष स्थापित किया गया है, साथ ही राज्य ग्रामीण आजीविका मिशनों के अंतर्गत उद्यम समर्थन को संस्थागत रूप देने के लिए समर्पित राज्य इनक्यूबेशन सेल भी स्थापित किए गए हैं।
समिति ने पश्चिम बंगाल और गोवा में स्टार्ट-अप ग्राम उद्यमिता कार्यक्रम (एसवीईपी) के विस्तार के प्रस्तावों पर भी विचार किया जिसका उद्देश्य ग्रामीण गैर-कृषि उद्यमिता तंत्र को और मजबूत करना और अधिक स्वयं सहायता समूह के सदस्यों को टिकाऊ उद्यम स्थापित करने और विकसित करने में सक्षम बनाना है।
ये पहलें महिला नेतृत्व वाले आर्थिक विकास और लखपति दीदी पहल के प्रति सरकार की प्रतिबद्धता को मजबूत करती हैं, जिससे ग्रामीण महिला उद्यमियों को निर्वाह स्तर के व्यवसायों से उच्च कारोबार, मजबूत बाजार संबंधों, वित्त तक बेहतर पहुंच और अधिक रोजगार क्षमता वाले उद्यमों की ओर बढ़ने में मदद मिलती है।
अधिकार प्राप्त समिति ने नवाचार, संस्थागत साझेदारी, प्रसार, डिजिटल अपनाने, बाजार पहुंच और परिणाम-आधारित निगरानी पर जोर दिया, जिसका उद्देश्य डीएवाई-एनआरएलएम के तहत महिला नेतृत्व वाले ग्रामीण उद्यमों के संवर्धन और सतत विकास के लिए एक मजबूत राष्ट्रीय तंत्र का निर्माण करना था।

title: Lunar Eclipse 2026 date and time: Will this astronomical event be visible in India? More details here
content:
Another astronomical event is set to dazzle the skies this month after 12 August total solar eclipse. The cosmic wonder slated to happen later this month has aroused curiosity among skywatchers about exact date and time and its visibility. Let's find out the exact date, time and more details about the upcoming partial lunar eclipse. The partial lunar eclipse will begin on the night of 27 August in the US and will be visible in other countries on 28 August 2026. New Yorkers and much of the US East Coast residents will be able to view the penumbral phase at 9:23 PM EDT on 27 August. The partial eclipse will begin at 10:33 PM and reach its maximum at 12:12 AM on 28 August 28 and end at 1:51 AM. The exact local timing changes depending upon the location. The partial lunar eclipse will neither be visible in Delhi nor from any other part of India. This cosmic event will be visible from much of North and South America and parts of Europe and Africa, according to National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). In Europe, West in Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Pacific, Atlantic, Indian Ocean and Antarctica some parts of the eclipse will be visible, Time and Date said. “At maximum eclipse, about 93% of the Moon's diameter will be inside Earth's dark central shadow, called the umbra. The Moon will not be completely covered, but it can look dramatically darkened, with a rusty, coppery tint along the covered edge,” the space agency said. A lunar eclipse is safe to watch with naked eyes, unlike a solar eclipse. For a closer view of Earth's curved shadow moving across the Moon, spectators can use binoculars or a small telescope. This celestial event is notable as the August 2026 lunar eclipse will turn the Moon noticeably darker and, in some locations, reddish as it would pass through Earth's shadow. title: डॉ. एल. मुरुगन की अध्यक्षता में 57वें आईएफएफआई की प्रथम संचालन समिति की बैठक आयोजित की गई, जिसमें महोत्सव की तैयारियों की समीक्षा की गई
content:
सूचना और प्रसारण मंत्रालय 
                        
                        
                        
                        
                              
                              
                                    डॉ. एल. मुरुगन की अध्यक्षता में 57वें आईएफएफआई की प्रथम संचालन समिति की बैठक आयोजित की गई, जिसमें महोत्सव की तैयारियों की समीक्षा की गई
                              
                              
                                    
डॉ. मुरुगन ने युवा और उभरते फिल्म निर्माताओं के लिए अधिक अवसरों और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर पहुंच मजबूत करने का आह्वान किया
आईएफएफआई का उद्देश्य भारतीय और वैश्विक सिनेमा के सर्वश्रेष्ठ प्रदर्शन के साथ-साथ रचनात्मक आदान-प्रदान और भारत की बढ़ती रचनात्मक अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूत करना है
                              
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        
                        भारत के 57वें अंतर्राष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव (आईएफएफआई) की संचालन समिति की पहली बैठक 21 अगस्त 2026 को कर्तव्य भवन-2, नई दिल्ली में सूचना एवं प्रसारण राज्य मंत्री डॉ. एल. मुरुगन की अध्यक्षता में आयोजित की गई, जिसमें महोत्सव के आगामी संस्करण की तैयारियों की समीक्षा की गई और विश्व स्तरीय अंतर्राष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव के रूप में इसकी स्थिति को और मजबूत करने के उपायों पर विचार-विमर्श किया गया।
भारत का 57वां अंतर्राष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव (आईएफएफआई) 20 से 28 नवंबर 2026 तक गोवा में आयोजित होने वाला है।
बैठक को संबोधित करते हुए डॉ. एल. मुरुगन ने आईएफएफआई के 57वें संस्करण के लिए अपने दृष्टिकोण को रेखांकित किया, जिसमें उन्होंने युवा छात्रों, उभरते फिल्म निर्माताओं और भारतीय फिल्म उद्योग के गुमनाम नायकों के लिए अधिक अवसरों पर जोर दिया। उन्होंने कहा कि आईएफएफआई को युवा प्रतिभाओं को अपनी रचनात्मकता प्रदर्शित करने, स्थापित फिल्म निर्माताओं से सीखने और वैश्विक फिल्म समुदाय से जुड़ने के लिए एक मंच प्रदान करना चाहिए, साथ ही दुनिया भर से उत्कृष्ट फिल्मों और अग्रणी रचनात्मक प्रतिभाओं को भारत लाकर अपनी अंतरराष्ट्रीय पहुंच को मजबूत करना चाहिए।
डॉ. मुरुगन ने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि श्री अश्विनी वैष्णव के नेतृत्व में मंत्रालय भारत की ऑरेंज इकोनॉमी को बढ़ावा देने और देश के रचनात्मक उद्योगों को मजबूत करने के लिए नई पहल कर रहा है, जिससे प्रतिभा, नवाचार और वैश्विक सहयोग के अवसर पैदा हो रहे हैं।
डॉ. मुरुगन ने मास्टरक्लास, स्थापित फिल्म निर्माताओं के साथ व्यवस्थित संवाद और युवा एवं उभरती प्रतिभाओं के लिए सार्थक मार्गदर्शन के अवसरों के विस्तार की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया। उन्होंने भारतीय सिनेमा की विविधता और शक्ति को प्रदर्शित करने के साथ-साथ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहयोग और पेशेवर आदान-प्रदान के अवसरों को मजबूत करने के महत्व पर भी प्रकाश डाला।
आईएफएफआई के विकास और निरंतर सफलता में गोवा सरकार की महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका को स्वीकार करते हुए, मंत्री जी ने गोवा के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री स्वर्गीय श्री मनोहर पर्रिकर की विरासत को श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित की, जिनकी दूरदृष्टि ने गोवा को अंतरराष्ट्रीय सिनेमा के लिए विश्व स्तर पर मान्यता प्राप्त गंतव्य में बदलने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। उन्होंने आईएफएफआई को वास्तव में विश्व स्तरीय सांस्कृतिक आयोजन बनाने की दिशा में गोवा के माननीय मुख्यमंत्री श्री प्रमोद सावंत के निरंतर समर्थन और प्रयासों की भी सराहना की।
कार्यक्रम के दौरान सूचना एवं प्रसारण मंत्रालय के सचिव श्री चंचल कुमार ने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि भारत की बढ़ती रचनात्मक अर्थव्यवस्था को बढ़ावा देने और भारतीय एवं अंतर्राष्ट्रीय रचनात्मक समुदायों के बीच सहयोग को मजबूत करने के लिए आईएफएफआई को एक प्रमुख मंच के रूप में उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए। उन्होंने महोत्सव में भाग लेने वाले फिल्म निर्माताओं, सिनेमा प्रेमियों, प्रतिनिधियों और अतिथियों के लिए उच्च गुणवत्ता वाला और निर्बाध अनुभव सुनिश्चित करने के महत्व पर भी बल दिया।
एनएफडीसी के प्रबंध निदेशक श्री प्रकाश मगदुम ने 57वें आईएफएफआई के लिए की जा रही तैयारियों और विभिन्न पहलों पर एक प्रस्तुति दी। आईएफएफआई के महोत्सव निदेशक श्री आशुतोष गोवारिकर ने संचालन समिति की सिफारिशों का स्वागत किया और मास्टरक्लास को सुदृढ़ बनाने, युवा फिल्म निर्माताओं के लिए अवसरों को बढ़ाने, भारत और विदेश से उत्कृष्ट फिल्मों के चयन और भारत तथा विश्व भर के प्रमुख फिल्म निर्माताओं और रचनात्मक हस्तियों की भागीदारी के महत्व पर जोर दिया।
गोवा सरकार के सूचना एवं जनसंपर्क सचिव ने समिति को राज्य सरकार द्वारा की जा रही तैयारियों से अवगत कराया और आश्वासन दिया कि 57वें अंतर्राष्ट्रीय फिल्म महोत्सव (आईएफएफआई) के लिए सभी आवश्यक गतिविधियों को समय पर पूरा करने और सुचारू व्यवस्था सुनिश्चित करने के लिए सभी आवश्यक प्रयास किए जाएंगे।
संचालन समिति के सदस्यों ने आईएफएफआई के अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पहुंच बढ़ाने पर विशेष बल दिया, जिसके तहत दुनिया भर से उत्कृष्ट फिल्मों का चयन करने और विभिन्न देशों के प्रमुख फिल्म निर्माताओं, कलाकारों और रचनात्मक पेशेवरों को आमंत्रित करने के लिए विशेष प्रयास किए जाएगें। इस महोत्सव को केवल सिनेमा के उत्सव के रूप में ही नहीं, बल्कि रचनात्मक आदान-प्रदान, सहयोग और भारत की बढ़ती रचनात्मक अर्थव्यवस्था को बढ़ावा देने के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण मंच के रूप में भी देखा जाता है।
संचालन समिति ने महोत्सव के सफल आयोजन के लिए सूचना एवं प्रसारण मंत्रालय, एनएफडीसी, गोवा सरकार और सभी संबंधित हितधारकों के बीच घनिष्ठ और निरंतर समन्वय के महत्व पर जोर दिया। समिति ने विश्वास व्यक्त किया कि 57वां आईएफएफआई सिनेमा, रचनात्मकता, सांस्कृतिक आदान-प्रदान और वैश्विक सहयोग के लिए एक अग्रणी अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंच के रूप में अपनी स्थिति को और मजबूत करेगा, साथ ही भारतीय फिल्म निर्माताओं और रचनात्मक पेशेवरों को दुनिया के साथ सार्थक रूप से जुड़ने के अधिक अवसर प्रदान करेगा।
बैठक में सूचना एवं प्रसारण मंत्रालय के सचिव श्री चंचल कुमार; श्री आशुतोष गोवारिकर, प्रसिद्ध फिल्म निर्माता और महोत्सव निदेशक, आईएफएफआई; श्री प्रकाश मगदुम, प्रबंध निदेशक, राष्ट्रीय फिल्म विकास निगम (एनएफडीसी); सचिव, आईपीआर, गोवा सरकार; और प्रसिद्ध संचालन समिति के सदस्य सुश्री भावना खेर, राम संपत, अपर्णा पुरोहित, प्रेरणा सिंह, नमिता, सुहासिनी मणिरत्नम, अभिषेक जैन संतोष सिवन, गौरव बनर्जी, आदित्य भट्ट, प्रशांत चोथानी और धरम गुलाटी उपस्थित थे।

title: The week in charts: Hawkish RBI minutes, drought warning, rural workforce
content:
From the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI's) minutes signalling hawkish caution even as rates stayed on hold, to India's exports finding strong footing across key markets in July, Skymet sharply revising down its monsoon forecast and raising drought odds, rural women driving a jump in labour force participation, and foreign portfolio investors returning to Indian equities in force—here are this week's news in numbers.
Hawkish signal
The latest RBI minutes strike a hawkish tone, with policymakers focused on the risk that inflation could remain elevated even as the repo rate was kept unchanged at 5.25% and the stance remained neutral at the August meeting. Inflation pressures have not become broad-based. Monetary policy committee (MPC) member Ram Singh noted that 69% of the weighted consumer price index (CPI) basket recorded inflation of 4% or less in June, while cautioning that the distribution was shifting towards higher inflation. The governor and other members said there were limited signs of generalization, but warned that food and fuel shocks could trigger second-round effects. A Mint analysis of CPI items also shows that 28% recorded inflation above 4% in July.
Trade momentum
India’s exports grew across several key markets in July 2026, according to preliminary trade data released by the commerce ministry. The US remained India’s largest export destination, accounting for 20.4% of overall exports, while shipments rose nearly 13% from a year ago. Exports to the US reached their highest level since March 2025, before tariffs took effect. However, the July figures may partly reflect commodity prices, which can inflate shipment values. Four other countries among the top 10 destinations recorded strong double-digit growth. Exports to Singapore jumped 83.7% year-on-year, followed by Malaysia at 73%, Japan at 65.3%, and China at 64.6%. The top 10 markets accounted for over half of overall exports.
Drought concerns
Private weather agency Skymet has turned more pessimistic on the 2026 monsoon as the season has progressed. In April, the weather agency had forecast rainfall at 94% of the long-period average (LPA), with a 70% chance of below-normal or drought conditions. By August, the agency revised their forecast to 85% of LPA and raised the probability of drought to 70%, up from 30%, citing a strengthening El Niño and uncertainty over a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. Rainfall was already 13% below LPA between June and July, and Skymet expects August and September to remain deficient. A weaker monsoon could hurt kharif crop yields, reduce rural incomes and tighten water availability, while also pushing up food prices in the coming months.
Numbers talk
₹8,452 crore: The corpus accumulated under the Prime Minister’s Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations (PM CARES) Fund by the end of FY25, after earning over ₹470 crore in interest, according to the fund’s audit report. Within this, just ₹87 lakh was spent in FY25.
98%: The shortfall from the Centre’s target for forest cover under the Green India Mission between FY16 and FY25, with just 0.03 million hectares added against a target of 1.4 million hectares, according to a new report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
₹7,877 crore: The investment approved for 31 electronics component projects under the first tranche of the IT ministry’s ₹40,000-crore Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme, covering mobile enclosures, copper coils, rare-earth magnets and other components.
₹13,041 crore: The investment approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs for four railway track-quadrupling projects on the Howrah-Chennai network and a highway project in Bihar. The four projects will expand the existing rail network to about 410 kilometres.
₹10,000 crore: The planned investment to develop more than a dozen new national waterways over five to 10 years, expanding India’s operational network and creating commercially viable cargo and passenger corridors.
Rural surge
India’s labour force participation rate (LFPR) among people aged 15 years and above rose sharply in July, led by rural women, according to the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) monthly data released by the statistics ministry. Rural female LFPR jumped 220 basis points to 38.8% in July 2026 from 36.6% in June. It was also up from 36.9% a year ago.
Urban female LFPR, in contrast, rose just 50 basis points from June to 25.3% in July, but remained below 25.8% in July 2025. Male LFPR was broadly stable, rising 40 basis points in rural areas to 78.3%, while urban male LFPR edged down 10 basis points to 75.2%.
FPI rebound
Foreign portfolio investors’ (FPI) return to Indian equities gathered pace in July, extending the recovery that began in June after a prolonged sell-off. The consumer services sector attracted the strongest inflows, attracting $1.06 billion in July, followed by healthcare at $0.81 billion and consumer durables at $0.77 billion. The healthcare sector, particularly, saw a sharp turnaround after nearly 15 months of consecutive net outflows, according to a Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) analysis.
Metals and mining attracted another $0.51 billion. On the other hand, capital goods recorded the largest net outflow at $0.66 billion, followed by telecommunications at $0.60 billion and automobiles and auto components at $0.47 billion.

title: Keeping the UN afloat: Trump admin plans $725 million payment as global body battles funding crisis — will it help?
content:
The Trump administration has notified the US Congress of its intention to provide $725 million to the United Nations, a move that aid experts say could help the global body manage its mounting financial pressures, Reuters reported.
The proposed payment comes as the United Nations faces a funding crisis caused by unpaid contributions from member states. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said earlier this year that the organisation faced an "imminent financial collapse" because of outstanding payments.
A US State Department notification to Congress dated August 4, seen by Reuters, said the administration was obligating $725 million for the UN's regular budget.
However, a US official told Reuters that the payment would be contingent on continued reforms at the organisation and that no funds had been transferred as of Friday.
The proposed payment would cover less than 20% of the more than $4 billion that the UN said Washington owed in May. The US disputes that figure, saying its outstanding dues are considerably lower and that it has made some payments.
Eugene Chen, a former UN official, told Reuters that a transfer of the proposed amount would help the organisation pay salaries for a period, although it might not cover all its expenses.
"It keeps the ship afloat a little longer," Chen said.
He added that if the US did not make further payments, it could potentially lose its voting rights in the UN General Assembly in January.
Under Article 19 of the UN Charter, a member state can lose its General Assembly voting rights if its arrears exceed the amount of contributions due for the preceding two full years, although grace periods are possible.
Ronny Patz, an expert in UN finance at German think tank IDOS, said a significant payment could help the organisation avoid immediate spending cuts.
"If they pay a big chunk, the UN still runs on zero reserves but it gets through the year," Patz told Reuters.
The proposed funding comes despite the Trump administration's criticism of the UN and its agencies. Washington has reduced funding to several UN bodies and refused to make some mandatory payments to the regular and peacekeeping budgets.
A State Department official said the US had achieved what it described as "historic reforms" at the UN over the past six months, including the first real cut to the organisation's budget, resulting in nearly $1 billion in reductions.
Devex reported in April that the administration had set conditions for releasing funds, including further cost-cutting and measures to counter China's influence.
The planned payment also comes ahead of Trump's expected speech to the UN General Assembly in New York next month.
The UN said in May that Washington owed more than $4 billion, including $2.04 billion for the regular budget, $2.2 billion for current and past peacekeeping missions and $44 million for UN tribunals.
The US is the largest contributor to the UN budget. However, the Trump administration has also withdrawn from dozens of UN and other international organisations and sharply reduced voluntary funding to UN agencies.
As of August 18, 129 of the UN's 193 member states had paid their contributions in full, according to a UN document reviewed by Reuters. China, the second-largest contributor after the US, was not among them.
The UN is undergoing a reform and cost-cutting programme known as "UN80" amid the financial crisis. It has already reduced its 2026 budget by 9.2% and moved more than 2,000 jobs from expensive locations such as Geneva and New York to lower-cost hubs.

title: India economic growth may beat RBI forecast: Deputy governor says 7% pace possible as indicators improve
content:
India’s economy may outperform the central bank’s forecasts this financial year, according to Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta, as growth closer to 7% leaves policymakers watching for the need to raise borrowing costs if it further fans inflation.
In a speech on Thursday, Gupta painted an upbeat picture of India’s economy, based on stronger-than-expected high-frequency indicators. She added that a 7.5% pace “is a given” for India over the long-term, and that “we should aspire to do better than that.”
Gupta’s comments add to increasingly optimistic assessments of India’s outlook, suggesting the country is set to remain the world’s fastest-growing major economy. Expectations of strong economic growth also shows why Gupta has recently turned relatively hawkish. Minutes of the RBI’s August policy meeting released this week showed Gupta raising the possibility of a rate hike later this year.
India’s one-year overnight index swaps rate has jumped 11 basis points since the minutes — the most since May — indicating traders now expect a hike sooner than previously anticipated. 
The OIS curve now implies a probability of three-to-four increases, with a 45-50% chance of the first move in October and a hike in December fully priced in, according to Abhishek Upadhyay, economist at ICICI Securities Primary Dealership. At the start of this week, market pricing reflected around two-three rate rises spread over the rest of the financial year that ends March, he said.
India’s gross domestic product data for the April-June quarter are due later this month, with economists’ predictions generally ranging between 6.9% to 8%. 
The brisk pace points to the economy’s resilience despite shocks, such as a deficient monsoon and elevated energy costs. Last week, Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated his ambition to make India a developed nation by 2047. Such a feat may require a sustained 8% plus growth rate for at least two decades, economists say. 
“We can definitely say the economy is far more resilient and better than what we were expecting three months back,” said Vivek Kumar, economist with QuantEco Research. He pointed to healthy corporate earnings, rising exports and bank credit, record high vehicle sales and index of industrial production growth reaching two-year highs.   
Kumar is among economists who are predicting the RBI will deliver its first hike in almost four years in December. India has so far stood apart from many regional peers by leaving policy unchanged since the conflict in the Middle East began, even as central banks from Japan to Australia and Indonesia tightened monetary settings. 
A flash survey by HSBC Holdings Plc. out earlier in the day, however, painted a mixed picture. 
The figures showed that services purchasing managers’ index advanced to 54.5 in August from 53.3 last month, while the manufacturing purchasing managers’ index fell to 52.9 from 53.5. That left the composite index at 54.6, up from a more than a four-year low of 54.3 in July.

title: Scottie Scheffler is about to beat Tiger Woods’ $121 million career earnings, with a little help from Tiger himself
content:
Scottie Scheffler is on the verge of overtaking Tiger Woods as the PGA Tour's all-time leading money earner. The world number one trails Woods by just $1,034,755 in career earnings, Golf.com reported. Scheffler has accumulated over $119 million while Woods has over $120 million. A top-three finish at the BMW Championship at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis would see Scheffler claim the record. Scottie Scheffler is completing his seventh full PGA Tour season. He has made 157 starts and averaged $763,054 per start across that period. Woods, by contrast, averaged $284,574 per start across his own first seven seasons. Woods also recorded 16 more wins than Scheffler during that comparable stretch. Rory McIlroy sits third on the all-time earnings list with $116,488,372. He offered a measured perspective on the growing prize funds. "If sponsors are willing to pay that, then that's the market value," McIlroy said. “We are professional golfers. Like, we’re not just Bobby Jones out there, not playing for prize money. We turned pro to make money playing golf,” he added. Meanwhile, the earnings gap tells a story that extends well beyond individual performance. Scheffler himself acknowledged this at the BMW Championship press conference. “A lot to do with the purses and all that. I’m not really too close to him in terms of career wins,” he said. Of course, he is not close to Tiger. Woods has 82 PGA Tour victories. Scheffler has 21. Tiger Woods won 75 top-5s, 89 top-10s and 119 top-25s while Scheffler has won 68, 88 and 122, respectively. Tiger also won 12 runner-ups, compared to Scheffler’s 15. "What, am I like a fourth of the way there? Tiger did a lot for the game of golf, and he put us in a position where we’re able to earn some pretty good stuff financially, so that’s something we’re very grateful for," Scheffler said. “Tiger’s contributions to the game, when you look at where the purses were at before, he came out on Tour to where they’re at now is a pretty stark difference,” he added. For sure, the escalating prize funds across professional golf reflect a dramatic shift in the sport's commercial power. Woods played a central role in attracting sponsors, television deals and global audiences. The competitive threat posed by LIV Golf and its Saudi-backed funding also forced the PGA Tour to increase its purses. The BMW Championship carries a $20 million purse this week. When Woods started his career, such figures were unimaginable for regular Tour events. So, when Scottie Scheffler overtakes Tiger Woods, he has none other than Tiger himself to thank. title: Iran announces ‘offensive’ war doctrine: What has Tehran prepared in retaliation against US? Army spokesman reveals
content:
Iran’s military doctrine has been gradually moving from “defensive to an offensive” approach, Army spokesman Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said on Saturday, attributing the change to lessons learned from the country’s recent conflicts, according to Turkey-based Anadolu news agency. Speaking to state news agency IRNA, Akraminia said the transition had taken shape during what he referred to as the 12-day and 40-day wars. “Our country’s military doctrine was defensive in the past, but gradually during these two wars, we witnessed the military doctrine moving from a defensive posture toward an offensive one,” Akraminia stated. Akraminia clarified that moving to an offensive military doctrine does not automatically involve launching preemptive attacks. However, he said Iran had used such a strategy during the war when it targeted a US base in Jordan before Washington officially joined the conflict. He claimed the strike caused “serious damage” to American equipment, infrastructure and personnel. According to Akraminia, the doctrine also calls for an immediate response to any attack, with Tehran potentially mounting a counterattack that is wider in scope than the original strike, adding that Iran’s move towards an offensive military doctrine was reflected in the recent wars through quicker and wider responses to attacks, along with preemptive strikes. He also stated the army had prepared a plan to reward those who kill or capture US troops if American forces launch a ground incursion into Iran. Under the proposed scheme, Iranian military personnel and civilians legally licensed to own hunting weapons would be eligible for a 5-billion-toman reward, roughly $26,000, for killing or capturing US troops entering Iran. The payout would rise to 10 billion tomans, or about $53,000, if a woman carried out the act. The army would also buy the weapon used in the operation for twice its market value, place it in a military museum bearing the owner’s name and give the person a replacement weapon, Akraminia noted. Akraminia said the merger of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters with the General Staff of the Armed Forces was intended to streamline Iran’s military structure, strengthen coordination and enable quicker decisions and responses to emerging threats. He also said Tehran was using legal and diplomatic channels to seek clarification from Qatar over the fate of three Iranian Air Force Su-24 pilots who remain unaccounted for. According to Akraminia, Brig. Gen. Majid Kazemi, one of four pilots involved in the attack on a US base in Qatar, was killed and his remains were later buried in Shiraz. The whereabouts of the other three pilots remain unknown. He said Iran’s Foreign Ministry and army were raising the matter with Qatari and international authorities, while calling on Doha to clarify the pilots’ status in line with international conventions. Akraminia also claimed that US influence in the region had weakened significantly, citing the newly established defence and security pact between Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan as an example of regional cooperation without Washington’s involvement. He said the pact’s eventual effectiveness remained to be seen but mentioned that its formation reflected what he described as Washington’s waning regional influence. He also called it the first regional defence and security arrangement formed without US participation. As the conflict approached its six-month mark, the US and Iran had stopped exchanging fire but had yet to resume peace negotiations. As per Reuters, Oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had nearly come to a standstill, with Tehran maintaining pressure by threatening to attack unauthorised tankers attempting to pass through the strategic waterway. title: Consumers queue up for premium petrol as E20 concerns refuse to die down
content:
New Delhi: Worried that ethanol-blended E20 petrol could hurt vehicle mileage and engine life, consumers are increasingly trading up to premium, high-octane petrol, driving its share of sales to 12-15% from about 4% in March, according to petrol pump dealers and industry executives.
The shift is notable because premium petrol is also blended with 20% ethanol. Consumers are nevertheless paying ₹110-115 a litre for higher-octane variants such as Indian Oil Corp.’s XP95, Bharat Petroleum Corp.’s SPEED and Hindustan Petroleum Corp.’s poWer95, commonly known as “branded petrol”, compared with about ₹102 for regular petrol, in the belief that their higher octane rating and additive packages can mitigate some of the problems they associate with E20.
“Both fuels contain 20% ethanol, but due to its higher octane rating, the impact on mileage is negligible,” said Prabhat Kumar Singh, president of the Bihar Petroleum Dealers Association (BPDA), which counts 4,500 fuel retail outlets as members. “Also, the availability of the fuel at almost every retail outlet has helped increase its sales threefold.”
The surge has gathered pace in recent weeks as concerns over E20’s impact on vehicles persist, even as the government maintains that the fuel is safe and has no significant adverse impact on vehicle performance. Dealers expect demand for premium petrol to rise further unless consumers are given more choice, including access to E10 or ethanol-free petrol.
“The demand for Octane 95 petrol was around 4-5% earlier, now it is around 15% on an average,” a New Delhi-based fuel retail pump dealer said on condition of anonymity. “Even a daily commuter using an entry-level bike now asks for this expensive variant.”
Monty Sehgal, national spokesperson of the Federation of All India Petroleum Traders, which represents over 80,000 pumps, said Octane 95 now is over 12% of their sales, and a proportionate drop has been seen in regular petrol sales.
“As the demand for ethanol-free petrol grows, the Centre can look at making this variant either ethanol free or E10 (blended with 10% ethanol),” Sehgal said. “This would not require any infrastructure change or logistical issue as the blending is done at the depots and they would just have to lower the blending for one variant.”
Meanwhile, enquiries for Octane 100, an ethanol-free fuel with a higher additive content, have also increased, although actual sales remain limited because of scarce availability and its steep price of ₹160-170 a litre. Retailers estimate that the fuel accounts for only about 1% of overall petrol sales.
“We have seen instances where people have come up with innovative ideas and fill half the tank with Octane 95 or the regular fuel, and the other half with Octane 100,” said the Delhi-based retailer mentioned above.
The Union government’s chief economic adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran had also pitched for reintroducing E10. “Restoring a lower blend at the pumps, say, E10, alongside the option to buy E20, would calm most public concern,” he wrote in a recent column in The Indian Express.
Even oil marketing companies (OMCs) are sensing the shift. “There has been an increase in the premium petrol demand in the last few months, but that has not led to a massive jump in overall petrol sales,” said an executive with an OMC, who did not want to be named, adding that along with the shift to high-octane petrol, there is also a surge in diesel sales, implying a parallel consumer shift from petrol to diesel, where there is no blending of ethanol or any other biofuel as of now.
Data from the government’s Vahan portal showed that diesel car sales jumped to 71,385 units in July 2026 from 64,853 in June.
Queries emailed to the state-run OMCs, and the ministries of petroleum & natural gas, and road transport & highways, remained unanswered till press time.
Options needed
Calls for providing additional options to consumers—in the form of E10 or even ethanol-fuel variants—have grown in the past few months. Consumer organisations and opposition political parties have been questioning the government over the ethanol blending policy and the alleged impact on the vehicles and their fuel efficiency.
Ashim Sanyal, managing trustee of Consumer VOICE, pointed out that a vehicle is a significant asset for most consumers, and they naturally prefer fuel that they believe can support better engine performance and longevity. “It would be useful for policymakers to keep these consumer concerns in mind as the country moves towards higher ethanol blending,” Sanyal said.
Kirit Parikh, former member (energy) at the erstwhile Planning Commission, said there needs to be clarity on the impact of ethanol-blended fuel on engines, and consumers need to be offered such fuels at cheaper rates to make up for any additional maintenance cost.
“In countries like Brazil, vehicles are engineered to run on higher blends of ethanol, but our cars may not be that prepared,” Parikh said. “Further, if reduction of crude imports is the target, much more aggressive promotion and growth of electric vehicles would be a much better move.”
Government’s defence
Meanwhile, the government and state-run OMCs have maintained that E20 petrol is safe and does not lead to any major impact on vehicles other than some components. According to the government, it rather improves acceleration of vehicles, apart from the larger economic benefit of reducing the crude oil import bill, which annually accounts for over $123 billion.
Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha on 10 August, Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said the ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process.
“Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, driveability, startability, corrosion resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards,” Gopi had said.
Gopi added that E20 was rolled out only after validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, reasonable material compatibility and emissions performance, and no significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear was found due to E20 use.
Other issues
Consumer concerns extend beyond vehicle performance. Amid concerns about high levels of chloride and moisture contamination in E20 petrol, earlier this month the three state-run OMCs—Indian Oil Corp. Ltd, Bharat Petroleum Corp. Ltd and Hindustan Petroleum Corp. Ltd—said in a joint statement that nationwide testing of E20 petrol found no evidence to support claims of high chloride contamination or moisture, and that fuel quality remained within prescribed limits.
The OMCs said they have also enhanced surveillance by conducting water ingress and density tests 8-12 times daily at every retail outlet. More than 100 petrol samples from refineries showed chloride levels at or below the standard one part per million (ppm), while ethanol samples from 80 distilleries recorded chloride content below 3 ppm.

title: Jaishankar to visit Russia on August 23-24, co-chair India-Russia inter-governmental commission
content:
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar will visit Russia on August 23-24 to co-chair the 27th session of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC). The visit is being undertaken at the invitation of Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov, the Ministry of External Affairs said. During the visit, Jaishankar will also meet Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov and exchange views on regional and global issues, the ministry said. The details were shared by the Ministry of External Affairs in a press release on Saturday. The release read, "The External Affairs Minister, S. Jaishankar, will undertake an official visit to Russia on 23-24 August 2026 to co-chair the 27th Session of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC)." "During the visit, EAM will also meet Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation H.E. Mr. Sergey Lavrov and exchange perspectives on regional and global issues," it added. The India-Russia Intergovernmental Commission has two divisions — the IRIGC-TEC, which covers trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation, and the IRIGC-M&MTC, which deals with military and military-technical cooperation. Jaishankar and Manturov co-chair the IRIGC-TEC, while the military and military-technical cooperation division is headed by the defence ministers of the two countries. Jaishankar last visited Moscow in November 2025 to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Heads of State Council meeting and participate in high-level discussions. During that visit, he also held talks with Lavrov on bilateral, regional and global issues, including cooperation through the SCO, BRICS, the United Nations and the G20. The latest visit comes ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's expected trip to New Delhi early next month. title: India gets FDI approvals of  ₹4,896 cr under eased norms for land-border countries; not clear origin is from China
content:
India received 29 foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals under a revised framework that allows automatic approval for certain investments by entities with as much as 10% shareholding by foreigners based in countries sharing a land border with the country, the government said on Friday. The proposed investments totalling ₹4,895.65 crore as of 20 August are in sectors such as information technology, artificial intelligence, information and communication, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, data centres and transport services. The proposals are from investors in jurisdictions including Mauritius, the US, Korea, Japan, Singapore, Luxembourg and the Cayman Islands, the commerce ministry said in a statement. The ministry did not identify the investors or name the origin country of the investments. The revised framework removes the requirement of prior government approval for FDI proposals by entities with a maximum 10% holding by investors based in countries sharing a land border with India. This provides investors with greater certainty, reduces transaction time and strengthens the ease of doing business in India. Following the notification of Press Note 2 of 2026 and the consequent amendment to the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, on 1 May 2026, the beneficial ownership test is now applied at the level of the investor entity. The investments are subject to applicable sectoral caps, entry routes and other conditions. The entity can invest without obtaining any other approval after reporting the relevant information to the government. Earlier, such foreign investors had to obtain prior government approval under Press Note 3 of 2020, even when the stake was very small. This had been a longstanding concern among investors seeking greater clarity and ease of investment. Press Note 3 of 2020 was introduced in April 2020 and required prior government approval for FDI from entities based in countries sharing a land border with India, as well as investments where the beneficial owner was situated in or was a citizen of such a country. The revised framework is aimed at addressing concerns arising from the earlier regime, particularly in cases involving small, non-controlling beneficial ownership through investment structures involving third-country jurisdictions, while continuing to retain safeguards for investments involving control or ownership beyond the prescribed threshold. An expert pointed to how it was not clear which of India's land border countries (LBCs) the latest FDI was from. "The real measure of the reform’s effectiveness is how much previously approval-constrained LBC-linked capital entered India because of this relaxation. This requires disclosure of beneficial ownership, control rights and ultimate source of capital, rather than merely the registered jurisdiction of the investing entity,” said Ram Singh, a professor at the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade. The government in its statement said the latest figures indicate that the calibrated relaxation is facilitating foreign investment into India while providing greater certainty to investors and reducing the time involved in processing investments. While easing the FDI norms, the government also said that any investment from countries sharing a land border with India in capital goods, electronic capital goods, electronic components, polysilicon and ingot-wafer sectors will continue to be considered on a case-by-case basis, but approval or otherwise will be given within 60 days. (The first and fourth paragraphs of this story have been revised to reflect the correct meaning of the 10% threshold.)
