title: CJI Surya Kant lauds Justice Sanjay Karol's empathy, leadership on farewell
content:
CJI Surya Kant lauds Justice Sanjay Karol's empathy, leadership on farewell
New Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday paid glowing tributes to Justice Sanjay Karol on his last day in office, describing him as a judge whose career was marked by "seriousness towards the law, sensitivity towards people and an unshakeable regard for the office he serves".
Heading a ceremonial bench comprising Justices Karol, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, the CJI referred to his long professional association with the retiring judge, recalling that he had known him first as a member of the Bar, later as a fellow advocate general, then as a colleague in Himachal Pradesh and finally as a fellow judge of the Supreme Court.
"What has struck me the most this morning is not the impressive journey just recounted, but the affection with which it has been spoken of. The Bar remembers Justice Karol not simply for the judgments, but for his patience, courtesy, willingness to listen, and sense of reassurance that accompanied his courtroom presence. That, perhaps, is one of the finest tributes that can be paid to anyone who has occupied judicial office," the CJI said.
He said Justice Karol's quality of listening also explains what is distinctive about his judicial work.
"Over the years, he has repeatedly noticed what the law can sometimes overlook the unpaid labour of a homemaker, the dignity of a tribal woman, or the needs of those living with mental illness. He gave legal visibility to such overlooked realities by recognising them as respected integrals of our society," the CJI said.
CJI Kant also spoke about Justice Karol's administrative record.
Justice Karol, as the chief justice of the Tripura High Court, brought pendency down from over 60,000 cases to under 27,000 within 10 months through disciplined listing, sustained docket attention, and by taking on some of the heaviest boards himself, the CJI said.
His tenure at the Patna High Court presented a different set of challenges, the CJI said, noting that Justice Karol led one of the country's most heavily burdened high courts for more than three years, including a substantial period under the pressures of the COVID-19 pandemic.
As Patron-in-Chief of the Bihar State Legal Services Authority, he also helped establish the State Mental Health Authority and continued to focus on people whose difficulties often remain outside the reach of the justice delivery system, CJI Kant said.
"It was a reminder that Brother Karol has always chosen to lead from the front. On the Bench, this rigour never lost sight of the litigant's actual problem," he said.
In his farewell address, Justice Karol reflected on four decades in courtrooms first as an advocate and for the last 19 years, as a judge.
He spoke of the "eloquent silences" of courtrooms and said the essence of the judicial process was not merely the arguments presented, but also understanding what people were seeking in the spaces between those arguments.
Bar leaders, including Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and SCBA President Pradeep Rai, also paid rich tributes to Justice Karol.
Mehta described Justice Karol as an empathetic judge who, even while dismissing a case or delivering an adverse verdict, would look at the person on the losing side and express his regret.
Mehta also highlighted Justice Karol's practice of appointing young lawyers as amici curiae, saying that he had encouraged hundreds of young students and lawyers by giving them opportunities to assist the court.
SCBA President Rai said Justice Karol would be remembered not only as a judge of law but as "a judge with heart", particularly for preserving dignity and giving confidence to those appearing before the court.
Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati recalled how Justice Karol would ask in court, "Who's the youngest in the Court?", creating opportunities for young lawyers to assist him. Advocate Shikhil Suri recalled Justice Karol telling a young junior counsel that a brief represented not merely a case but the life, struggles and destiny of a person.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayan recalled Justice Karol's warmth in court and particularly referred to his recognition of the role and value of homemakers.
Born on August 23, 1961, in Himachal Pradesh, Justice Karol studied in Shimla and obtained his law degree from Himachal Pradesh University. He served as advocate general of Himachal Pradesh from 1998 to 2003 and was designated as senior advocate in 1999.
He was elevated as a judge of the Himachal Pradesh High Court on March 8, 2007, became chief justice of the Tripura High Court in November 2018 and was subsequently transferred as chief justice to the Patna High Court in November 2019.
He was elevated to the Supreme Court on February 6, 2023.

title: Keralam CM Satheesan hails Cardinal Cleemis as guiding light for society
content:
Keralam CM Satheesan hails Cardinal Cleemis as guiding light for society
Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Saturday described Cardinal Mar Baselios Cleemis Catholicos, Major Archbishop of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church, as a guiding light for society.
He was speaking after inaugurating the valedictory function of the Cardinal's episcopal silver jubilee held at Pattom here.
Satheesan said he was attending the event not as the chief minister but as a brother of Cardinal Cleemis.
"Whenever I have visited him, he has showered me with love and affection, given me confidence, and provided the energy to face all crises. I desire to say with pride that Cardinal is, in every sense of the word, like a brother to me. He is the same to everyone who knows him," he said.
Satheesan said Cardinal Cleemis, as the successor to Archbishop Mar Ivanios, had guided the Malankara Catholic Church through difficult times and continued to spread light everywhere.
"In the Church, in the spiritual realm, and in public life, wherever he intervenes, his mature actions and words bring warmth, love, and a sense of harmony to even the most tense environments. He always shares actions and words that make us feel the presence of a divine force within his heart," he said.
Referring to Chapter 60 of the Book of Isaiah in the Bible, Satheesan described Cardinal Cleemis as a light that guides society.
"I wish to specifically mention that he lives by shining in that light and sharing it with others. Literally, the words of Prophet Isaiah align with him and his deeds," he said.
Satheesan said the Bible spoke extensively about light, which removed darkness and ignorance and brought illumination and wisdom.
"His journey is driven by the grand mission of leading humanity out of darkness and ignorance toward the paths of wisdom," he said.
He also referred to the First Letter of St Paul to Timothy regarding how a leader of the Church should conduct himself.
"Cleemis Bava is someone who upholds both the essence of that faith and the duty of a clean conscience with equal dedication," he said.
Satheesan said the Cardinal had more missions ahead and sought his blessings as the government navigated complex pathways.
"Similarly, at a time when the Christian community across the country faces a deep sense of insecurity, I hope his leadership will guide them out of that anxiety, instil confidence, and lead them toward true paths of faith and hope," he said.
Union Minister Suresh Gopi, Health Minister K Muraleedharan and Shashi Tharoor MP attended the event.

title: ‘India could use water as weapon’: Pakistan minister warns amid Indus Water Treaty row
content:
‘India could use water as weapon’: Pakistan minister warns amid Indus Water Treaty row
The remarks come amid renewed tensions between the two nuclear-armed neighbours over the Indus Waters Treaty.
Pakistan’s Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has warned that India’s decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance has created a new challenge for Islamabad, saying Pakistan now faces the possibility of India using water as a weapon by withholding supplies when they are needed for crops and releasing them when they are not.
“It's untouchable because it is an international agreement and this time around the Indian government has unilaterally held it in abeyance and that sort of creates a new challenge that first time probably water has been weaponized in modern history and we now face this threat that you know they can use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan water when it needs for its crops and release it when we don't need it,” he said at an Asia Society event.
“So these dams that we are constructing would also be our buffer but I think at the same time we cannot let this go unnoticed. We are using all the diplomatic," he added.
Also Read | Strategic logic behind India’s Indus Waters Treaty stand
Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif on India and IWT
The remarks come amid renewed tensions between the two nuclear-armed neighbours over the Indus Waters Treaty, with Pakistan repeatedly raising concerns over the impact of India’s decision to suspend the pact.
The issue was also raised by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the eve of the country’s Independence Day, when he warned India against threatening Pakistan’s water supplies and said Islamabad would give a “direct response” if its access to water was jeopardised.
Speaking at an event, Sharif said Pakistan wanted peace and not war, but cautioned that its desire for peace should not be mistaken for weakness.
“Every drop of water is our red line,” Sharif said, as quoted in a report by the Associated Press. He warned that Pakistan would respond if India threatened its water supplies, adding that any threat to Pakistan’s sovereignty would draw a strong response.
Sharif’s remarks came in the backdrop of the four-day military conflict between India and Pakistan in May 2025, which followed the Pahalgam terror attack and further strained ties between the two countries.
Also Read | Nailing Pakistan's lies on Indus water sharing
India on Indus Waters Treaty
India had decided to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed.
The Cabinet Committee on Security met on April 23, a day after the attack, following which India announced that the treaty would remain in abeyance. New Delhi said the circumstances and conditions under which the treaty had been negotiated had fundamentally changed.
India has maintained that the treaty cannot function in its present form and will remain in abeyance until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably” ends its support for cross-border terrorism.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also defended the decision, saying that “water and blood cannot flow together”. The government has described keeping the treaty in abeyance as part of the measures taken in response to the Pahalgam attack.
A fortnight after the terror attack, India and Pakistan exchanged missile, drone and other strikes before a ceasefire brought an end to the four-day military conflict in May 2025.
India has since maintained its position on the treaty.
“India's position on the Indus Water Treaty is consistent. The IWT stands in abeyance in response to Pakistan's continued sponsorship of cross-border terrorism. Pakistan must credibly and irrevocably abjure its support for cross-border terrorism,” Jaiswal had said.
His clarification came after a Pakistan minister issued a stark warning to India over the treaty, saying Islamabad would “cut off those hands” that he claimed sought to control the Indus water.

title: NHRC directs Punjab govt to probe allegation against CM's wife of demanding  ₹5 cr to suppress rape case
content:
NHRC directs Punjab govt to probe allegation against CM's wife of demanding ₹5 cr to suppress rape case
New Delhi, The NHRC has issued a notice to the Punjab government and its police chief over a complaint alleging that Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's wife demanded ₹5 crore to suppress a rape case, officials said on Saturday.
The National Human Rights Commission directed the authorities to inquire into the allegation and submit an action taken report within two weeks.
No immediate reaction was available from the Punjab government.
"The complainant alleged that a retired judge publicly stated that a demand of ₹5 crore was made in connection with a rape case, allegedly involving the wife of the chief minister of Punjab," the proceedings dated August 21 read.
An NHRC official said the Commission has taken cognisance of the allegation of the complainant that the wife of Chief Minister Mann sought ₹5 crore to suppress a rape case. According to the complaint, the allegation has been levelled by a former Punjab judge, the official said.
The complaint, filed by Legal Rights Observatory , raised concerns that such "interference" could compromise the victim's right to dignity, safety, fair investigation and access to justice, they said.
The complainant has requested independent verification of the allegation, preservation of evidence, and "impartial inquiry into any attempt to dilute or influence the investigation", and emphasised that a rape victim's right to justice must remain "above influence, status, or position".
The allegation prima facie seems to be a violation of the human rights of the victim, an NHRC bench presided over by its member Priyank Kanoongo said after taking cognisance of the matter under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, according to the proceedings.
"The registry is directed to issue a notice to the chief secretary of the Punjab government, and the DGP of Punjab, with directions to 'get the allegations made in the complaint inquired into, and to submit an action taken report within two weeks for perusal of the Commission'," the bench said.
"Let a copy of this proceeding be also transmitted to the Joint Secretary, Women Safety Division, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi, for information," it said.

title: BJP passes resolution on 'Vande Mataram', condemns Congress move to sing 2 stanzas
content:
BJP passes resolution on 'Vande Mataram', condemns Congress move to sing 2 stanzas
The resolution stated that the legacy of the National Song cannot be “reduced to the calculations of contemporary vote-bank politics.”
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday passed a resolution opposing the Congress Working Committee’s decision to reaffirm its 1937 resolution and restrict the singing of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas at party programmes, while seeking to uphold the National Song’s historical legacy.
The resolution stated that the legacy of the National Song cannot be “reduced to the calculations of contemporary vote-bank politics.”
ALSO READ: Congress, BJP trade charges over National Song uproar in assembly
Deep Dive
BJP resolution on Vande Mataram
A statement issued by the party said it regards Vande Mataram as the National Song of Bharat, an expression of reverence for Bharat Mata, a mantra of the freedom struggle and an immortal symbol of India’s national consciousness.
The party resolved to “uphold the honour, dignity, legacy and national status of the complete Vande Mataram as the National Song of Bharat and as an immortal symbol of India’s national consciousness and freedom struggle… To affirm the constitutional and statutory status of Vande Mataram as established by the Constituent Assembly’s 1950 pronouncement and reinforced by Parliament’s 2026 amendment extending statutory protection to the National Song equivalent to that accorded to the National Anthem,” the resolution said.
Lashing out at the Congress for refusing to sing all stanzas of the National Song, the BJP said it will reject every attempt to subordinate the National Song to communal pressure, political appeasement, or narrow vote-bank considerations.
The CWC earlier decided to abide by its 1937 resolution on Vande Mataram and sing only two stanzas of the National Song, instead of its full rendition, at all party events.
“…To remind the Congress that a resolution of its Working Committee cannot override the constitutional institutions or laws of the Republic of India, and that a political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026….To expose before the people of Bharat the historical and political context in which the truncation of Vande Mataram took place, including the objections raised by the Muslim League and the subsequent politics of communal and separatist demands,” the resolution said.
Earlier, Union home minister Amit Shah had dubbed the Congress resolution as anti-national and designed to foster vote-bank politics.
ALSO READ: 'Will she teach patriotism?' BJP on Sharmila Tagore's Vande Mataram remark
To counter the opposition’s claims that some faiths have reservations about the stanzas with religious imagery, the BJP said it will recall and disseminate Mahatma Gandhi’s testimony that Vande Mataram had become an “anti-imperialist cry” and that he associated it with “the purest national spirit,” demonstrating its larger national meaning beyond the literary or religious context of particular stanzas.
The party will undertake a nationwide campaign to take the history, meaning, national significance and glorious legacy of Vande Mataram to every corner of Bharat.
“…To educate and mobilise the people, especially the younger generation, so that the complete six-stanza National Song and its history are not forgotten and future generations understand the sacrifices, struggles and patriotic awakening with which Vande Mataram is inseparably associated,” the resolution said.
The party urged citizens to remember that the words Vande Mataram were once “powerful enough to frighten an empire.”

title: ‘611 schools without buildings’: Rajasthan govt admits lapses amid CJP ‘checks’, blames Congress, Gehlot
content:
‘611 schools without buildings’: Rajasthan govt admits lapses amid CJP ‘checks’, blames Congress, Gehlot
The BJP dubbed the poor condition of government schools as the “sin” of the previous Congress government that the current administration was trying to fix.
As the Cockroach Janta Party turned its focus to the condition of government-run schools in Rajasthan, the state government informed the Assembly on Friday that as many as 611 schools are functioning without their own buildings.
Highlighting the lack of proper infrastructure in schools, Rajasthan's BJP government shifted the blame on the previous government led by Congress under chief minister Ashok Gehlot, India Today reported.
Schools without buildings, govt blames Congress
The government, referring to an audit conducted after the Jhalawar school accident, said the report had exposed the poor condition of government schools. The BJP dubbed the poor condition of government schools as the “sin” of the previous Congress government that the current administration was trying to fix. At least seven students died and 28 injured last year in July when the roof a school building in Jhalawar, Rajasthan collapsed while the students were gathering for morning prayers.
The government made the disclosure on the lack of infrastructure in schools in response to a question from Leader of Opposition (LoP) Tika Ram Jully. According to Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) data for 2025-26 under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan cited by India Today, 611 government schools in the state do not have buildings.
CJP's school ‘inspection’ campaign
The numbers that draw a grim picture on Rajasthan's education system comes amid the attack on CJP volunteers who were on their way to inspect a government school in Jaipur’s Bagru assembly constituency.
The incident occurred near Rampura Kanwarpura village, where CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka and his team planned to visit a government school to assess its infrastructure and facilities.
“They attacked us and fractured the arm of one of our volunteers,” he said, alleging that those involved were workers of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
In a video purportedly showing the incident, a group of people can be seen confronting the CJP team, while chants of “Jai Shri Ram” can be heard.
According to the party, the visits were aimed at assessing the condition of school buildings, the education system and facilities available to students.
Ranka had earlier posted on social media about the condition of the primary school at Rampura Kanwarpura. According to him, the main school building has become unsafe and has been closed after portions of the roof and beams deteriorated. The structure is being supported with iron angles.
Students have consequently been shifted to a shed around 50 metres from the main building, where they are studying under a tin roof, Ranka alleged. He also claimed that animal fodder was lying inside the shed and that bricks had fallen from portions of the structure.

title: Imphal-Dimapur-Guwahati bus service resumes after 3 years in violence-hit Manipur
content:
Imphal-Dimapur-Guwahati bus service resumes after 3 years in violence-hit Manipur
Public transport on the Imphal-Dimapur-Guwahati route resumed after nearly three years, with 125 passengers travelling in two buses and five wingers on Friday.
Public transport services on the Imphal–Dimapur–Guwahati route resumed after nearly three years, with 125 passengers travelling in two buses and five wingers on Friday, in a significant step towards restoring connectivity in violence-hit Manipur.
The buses have crossed Kangpokpi, a Kuki-majority district, and Senapati, a Naga-majority district, before entering Nagaland en route to Guwahati — a journey being seen as a symbolic step towards restoring normal life and connectivity in the state.
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, along with Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen and Saitu MLA Haokholet Kipgen, during their last visit to Kangpokpi district on August 8, had announced the reopening of national highways for free movement of all communities and stated that the Imphal–Dimapur–Guwahati bus service would be resumed soon.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah had directed the Manipur government to ensure free movement along all national highways in Manipur with effect from March 8, 2025. However, Kuki-Zo groups had defied Shah’s directives and foiled government attempts twice in Kangpokpi district.
One of the travellers, Kiyam Kumarjit Singh, belonging to the Meitei community from Thoubal district, said that this new journey should usher in love, peace, and harmony among all communities in the state, and help people move beyond what had happened in the past. “Let us all forgive and forget the past,” he added.
Nivedita from Khundrakpam village in Imphal East district also thanked the government.
The ethnic clashes in Manipur first began between the Meitei and Kuki communities before involving almost every community. The state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities shut each other out from the areas they dominate since ethnic clashes began in May 2023, leaving at least 260 people dead and displacing 60,000.
The Meiteis, mostly Hindu, live largely in the Imphal Valley. The Kukis, predominantly Christian, reside in the hills. The state government has maintained that there are no buffer zones dividing communities in the state, but it has identified certain sensitive areas.
A new government was formed in February, nearly a year after the imposition of President’s Rule. It includes representatives from all three major communities as part of an attempt to maintain ethnic balance.

title: ‘Misinformation’: Cochin airport rejects SpiceJet’s ‘bad weather in Kochi' claim
content:
‘Misinformation’: Cochin airport rejects SpiceJet’s ‘bad weather in Kochi' claim
The authorities said there was no adverse weather in Kochi that could disrupt the flights at the airport.
SpiceJet on Saturday said its flights to and from the Cochin airport in Kerala’s Kochi have been affected due to “bad weather”, prompting a clarification from the airport authorities.
The Cochin airport said in a post on X, denying Spicejet’s claims of bad weather in the city, and called the airline's social media post regarding the same “misinformation”
“CIAL has noted continuing operational issues faced by SpiceJet, affecting its services internationally, including those from Kochi, causing considerable inconvenience and uncertainty to passengers. At a time when the airline is yet to satisfactorily address the concerns of affected passengers, SpiceJet has issued a social media communication spreading misinformation by attributing the disruption to bad weather at Kochi,” the airport’s X handle shared a clarification.
The authorities said there was no adverse weather in Kochi that could disrupt the flights.
“However, there were no adverse weather conditions at Kochi warranting the disruption cited in the communication. It may also be noted that no other airline operating from Kochi has reported such cancellations on account of weather conditions during the same period. Despite the continuing passenger grievances, the issues have not been adequately addressed or rectified by the airline and have continued to worsen over the past few days. CIAL, on its part, as a responsible airport operator, has made maximum efforts to assist the affected passengers and provide necessary support and solace to them. Passengers who have booked SpiceJet flights are therefore advised to recheck their flight status with SpiceJet before proceeding to the airport,” the post further read.
What SpiceJet claimed
SpiceJet had said earlier that its services at the Cochin airport, which included all departures and arrivals, “might be affected” due to “bad weather” in Kochi. The airline requested that passengers check their flight status before coming to the airport.
“#WeatherUpdate: Due to bad weather in Kochi (COK), all departures/arrivals and their consequential flights might be affected. Passengers are requested to check their flight status via https://spicejet.com/#status,” the carrier said in a post on X.
This comes as SpiceJet continues to grapple with mounting operational pressures, with its July cancellation rate touching 8.58 per cent and the airline facing an NCLT matter over insolvency proceedings.
SpiceJet escaped immediate insolvency on Wednesday after lessor Aviator ML withdrew its ₹60-crore insolvency plea following a settlement. But seven other lessor petitions remain, keeping the threat of insolvency alive.

title: Seek medical advice if experiencing H1N1 symptoms: Govt's directive as cases surge
content:
Seek medical advice if experiencing H1N1 symptoms: Govt's directive as cases surge
Delhi has recorded 2,392 Influenza-A cases this year, including 1,777 H1N1 cases, according to health department data
Delhi-NCR has reported a rise in Influenza A (H1N1) cases, commonly known as swine flu, with health officials and experts urging people to recognise symptoms early and follow basic precautions to limit transmission.
In a directive issued on Saturday, the government listed some common symptoms of H1N1 or swine flu and urged people experiencing them to immediately seek medical advice.
Delhi has recorded 2,392 Influenza-A cases this year, including 1,777 H1N1 cases, according to health department data. As many as 114 H1N1 cases were reported in the capital on Thursday alone.
Deep Dive
“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue. Recognise the signs early and don’t ignore persistent symptoms,” the Ministry of Health said in an X post.
Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the city was fully equipped to deal with the seasonal rise in infections, with no shortage of beds, doctors, medicines or essential medical equipment. The government is also monitoring the patient tally and strengthening hospital arrangements according to requirements.
What are the symptoms of H1N1?
H1N1 can cause symptoms similar to those of seasonal flu. According to the Ministry of Health, common symptoms include fever, cough, Sore throat, headache, runny nose, body ache and fatigue
Dr Neetu Jain, Senior Consultant, Department of Pulmonary, Critical Care, and Sleep Medicine at PSRI Hospital, said H1N1 symptoms can also include cold, watery eyes and general weakness.
Dr Jain said, “H1N1 cases are particularly high in Delhi-NCR this year. The number of cases is said to be six times higher than in previous years…First, the weather conditions, high temperatures and high humidity, can lead to an increase in H1N1 cases, flu cases, and viral infections in general”.
Dr Randeep Guleria, Chairman, Internal Medicine, Respiratory & Sleep Medicine, Medanta Gurugram, said most cases present with mild symptoms such as fever, sore throat and cough. Body aches and cough, however, can sometimes persist for a few weeks.
Also Read: Why H1N1 cases are rising in Delhi and how to protect yourself?
How does H1N1 spread and how can you prevent it?
Experts have stressed the importance of basic precautions and public awareness in limiting the transmission of the virus.
Arjun Dang, CEO of Dr Dang's Lab, said regular hand hygiene and appropriate masking can help limit transmission. He also advised people who test positive to isolate and undergo treatment under the guidance of a physician.
Home-collection services and molecular testing systems can also help detect infections faster, allowing timely clinical intervention, Dang said.
People at higher risk, including immunocompromised individuals and those with comorbidities, should remain particularly vigilant and seek medical advice and timely testing if they develop symptoms.
How is H1N1 treated?
H1N1 is a treatable illness, and most cases are mild and self-limiting, according to the experts cited above.
Dr Jain said antiviral medicines may be given to help improve the chances of a quicker recovery, while supportive care may also be required.
Dr Guleria said most cases resolve on their own, although some patients, particularly elderly people and those in high-risk groups, may require hospitalisation.
(With inputs from ANI, PTI)

title: Haridwar: 3 killed, 6 injured as 4 motorcycles collide on Kanwar route
content:
Haridwar: 3 killed, 6 injured as 4 motorcycles collide on Kanwar route
Three people were killed and six injured after four motorcycles collided on Haridwar’s Kanwar Patri amid poor visibility due to darkness and rain, police said.
Three persons were killed and six others injured after four motorcycles collided on the Kanwar stretch along the Ganga canal in Haridwar’s Kaliyar area on Friday night, police said.
The accident took place on the Kaliyar road, popularly known as the Kanwar Patri in Uttarakhand, amid poor visibility due to darkness and rain, police officers said, adding that the two motorcycles travelling in opposite directions collided head-on, following which two other bikes coming from behind rammed into the vehicles.
Also Read: 4 of family killed after being hit by speeding SUV on Jaipur highway
“As soon as information about the accident was received, police teams from Civil Lines and Kaliyar police stations reached the spot and launched a rescue operation. Three youths died, while six others were injured. Postmortem of the deceased were conducted and our further legal formalities are underway,” Superintendent of Police (rural) SC Suyal said.
Police identified the deceased as Ayan (18) from Bijauli; Raju Singh (24) from Rehmatpur; and Rajeev Singh (22) from Saharanpur.
Also Read: Bihar: 5 killed, 2 injured as speeding bus ploughs into crowd watching orchestra
Police officers said that of the six injured people, Aditya Chandra (24) from Khanjanpur was critically injured. He was referred by doctors at Roorkee Civil Hospital to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rishikesh, for further treatment.
It came days after four people were killed and three others injured after an Eco van crashed into a commercial vehicle parked on the roadside near Manimai temple on the Haridwar highway in Doiwala of Dehradun on Wednesday.

title: Judges not gods, won't get every judgment right: Outgoing SC Judge Sanjay Karol
content:
Judges not gods, won't get every judgment right: Outgoing SC Judge Sanjay Karol
New Delhi, Judges are not gods and they will not get every judgement right, retiring Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Karol said in his farewell address on Saturday.
He also said that judging requires a certain degree of humility and the ability to see the real person behind every litigant.
The apex court on Saturday bid an emotional farewell to Justice Karol, with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Bar leaders, including Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Supreme Court Bar Association President Pradeep Rai, paying glowing tributes to the outgoing judge on his last working day.
"The Constitution does not ask us merely to apply the law correctly. It asks us to apply it justly. That is perhaps why the responsibility of judging has always seemed larger to me than simply deciding who is legally correct.
"We, as judges, are not gods. We will not get every judgment right. What was always in our hands was simple: to see the person, not just the petitioner. A petition can only tell you the facts of a case, but it cannot tell you what the person has already lost or what he is hoping to seek from the courts. And perhaps that is why I have always said that judging requires certain level of humility," Justice Karol said.
Justice Karol was elevated to the Supreme Court on February 6, 2023. A ceremonial bench on his last day in office comprised CJI Kant and Justices Karol, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
In his farewell address, Justice Karol reflected on his nearly four-decade journey in the legal profession and said the courtroom had never been merely a workplace for him, but a vehicle for something "greater and more important" than himself.
"I will not pretend that this journey has been mine alone. This courtroom has not left me; it has supported me," he said.
Justice Karol said he spent 40 years in courtrooms, initially as an advocate appearing before the Bench and, for the last 19 years, as a judge.
He spoke of the importance of listening beyond the spoken arguments and said there were "eloquent silences" in courtrooms that judges must learn to understand.
"In the silence of the Bar, there is a way of listening," he said, emphasising that what mattered in the judicial process was not merely the arguments advanced, but also what people were praying for "in the spaces between the words".
Recalling his first visit to courtroom No. 1 of the Supreme Court in 1996, Justice Karol said the bench appeared to him to be almost six feet above the ground.
"Judging from there has taught me something about this courtroom's symbolism. From below, the height of the bench can appear to signify authority. From the comfort zone, it signifies something quite different, and that is responsibility with dignity and honesty," he said.
Justice Karol said the true significance of the Supreme Court lay in the faith of an ordinary citizen who enters its doors believing that someone would listen.
"But we must also remember those who never reach those doors because justice is too distant, too expensive, too intimidating," he said.
Reflecting on the meaning of constitutionalism and justice, Justice Karol said the simplest way to understand concepts such as law, due process and constitutional legality was through the idea of "dharma", not as ritual, but as duty.
"The duty of a judge is to respect justice and see that the person standing before the court, however small, however wretched, is seen and heard," he said.
Addressing members of the Bar, Justice Karol said the principles of judging extend beyond courtrooms and robes, with every individual called upon to be a judge of their own choice, conduct and use of power.
"There may be no courtrooms, no robes, no technical grounds, but in these small choices, each of us dispenses the measure of justice that we take," he said.
"A judge is a judge before he dons and after he takes off the robes," he said.
Recalling a point made by the CJI a day earlier, Justice Karol said India had not only a living Constitution but also has to "live the Constitution".
"The greatness of our Constitution is tested not only in great cases. It is tested in ordinary conduct," he said.
Concluding his address, Justice Karol said he was returning to "the most distinguished constitutional office" that of the ordinary citizen.
Born on August 23, 1961, Justice Karol completed his schooling in Shimla and obtained his law degree from the Himachal Pradesh University.
He was appointed advocate general of Himachal Pradesh in 1998 and served in the post until 2003. He was designated a senior advocate in 1999 and elevated as a judge of the Himachal Pradesh High Court on March 8, 2007.
He was elevated as the chief justice of the Tripura High Court in November 2018 and was subsequently transferred as the chief justice of the Patna High Court in November 2019, before being elevated to the Supreme Court on February 6, 2023.

title: Delhi techie dies after assault by in-laws following dispute with wife
content:
Delhi techie dies after assault by in-laws following dispute with wife
Police identified the deceased as Vinay Gupta, a resident of Laxmi Park, who married about three and a half years ago. Police did not identify the wife
A 31-year-old software engineer allegedly died after being assaulted by his wife’s family members following a matrimonial dispute at his residence in outer Delhi’s Nihal Vihar on Friday, police said. Police said four people have been detained for questioning but not yet arrested.
A case under sections 103(1) (murder) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has been registered.
Police identified the deceased as Vinay Gupta, a resident of Laxmi Park, who married about three and a half years ago. Police did not identify the wife. They have four-and-a-half-month-old twin children, a boy and a girl, police said.
Wife called family after argument
According to police, a dispute broke out between the couple at their residence on Friday morning.
“Following the argument, Gupta’s wife called her family members, who reached the couple’s house in Nihal Vihar. The woman’s family members allegedly assaulted Gupta severely. He sustained injuries in the assault and later died,” a senior police officer said.
Gupta was employed as a software engineer with an MNC in Noida, while his wife is a homemaker.

title: Family-linked appointments, funds diversion: BCI co-chair's allegations against Manan Mishra
content:
Family-linked appointments, funds diversion: BCI co-chair's allegations against Manan Mishra
Co-chair alleged that staff appointments were made without a transparent recruitment process and that several employees are personally connected to Mishra.
Bar Council of India (BCI) co-chairman and senior advocate YR Sadasiva Reddy has demanded the immediate resignation of BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, alleging irregularities in appointments to the Council, diversion of funds and a lack of transparency in its functioning.
In a letter dated August 22 addressed to Mishra, Reddy sought his resignation and called for an independent inquiry into the allegations. He also demanded a special meeting of the BCI to consider the issues raised in the notice.
“I address this communication to you not as an adversary, but as an elected member of the Bar Council of India, presently holding the office of co-chairman, and as a member of this profession for over three decades,” Reddy said in the letter, shared by Live Law.
Deep Dive
The demand comes amid the recent controversy over Mishra's decision to refuse enrolment to the graduating batch of NALSAR University of Law following a row over the reported objection of students to having Chief Justice of India Surya Kant attend their convocation. Lawyer bodies subsequently demanded Mishra's removal, while lawyers also held protests outside the BCI office. The Cockroach Janta Party had also joined the protests, seeking his resignation.
He said he was writing after “long reflection” and felt that remaining silent would amount to a failure of the trust placed in him by advocates.
Allegation of family-linked appointments
One of the key allegations raised by Reddy concerns appointments to the BCI's establishment. He alleged that staff appointments were made without a transparent recruitment process and claimed that several employees are personally connected to Mishra.
“Appointments to the establishment of the Council made without any transparent process of recruitment,” Reddy said, listing it as the first ground for seeking Mishra's resignation.
According to Reddy, he did not previously question the process because he had no reason to believe it was otherwise.
However, after examining the current staff list and the details of employees, Reddy alleged that he found “a pattern that no responsible Member can overlook”.
“A striking proportion of the staff are persons connected to you personally, several of them being members of, or related to, your own family,” the letter shared by Live Law alleged.
Reddy further claimed that he could not find any record placed before the BCI showing an advertisement, selection committee proceedings or comparative merit list to justify the appointments.
BCI funds and powers
Reddy also questioned the manner in which the BCI's financial and regulatory powers are being exercised.
“The Bar Council of India is not the personal estate of any individual,” he said, stressing that the body is a statutory institution constituted under the Advocates Act, 1961.
He said the Council holds funds contributed by lakhs of advocates and exercises regulatory powers over the entry of young lawyers into the profession. “Every rupee it holds is held in trust,” Reddy said.
According to him, the powers exercised by the BCI are conferred by Parliament for the benefit of the legal profession and not for the benefit of the person occupying the chair.
Reddy said his assessment was based on what he had personally witnessed during BCI meetings. He alleged that under Mishra's chairmanship, the Council had “drifted very far” from the standards expected of a statutory body.
Demand for special audit
As part of his demands, Reddy called for a special audit of the accounts of the BCI and BCI Trust PEARL-First from the date of their registration.
He sought an independent audit by a firm empanelled with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and demanded that the report be circulated among all BCI members and published.
He also called for an immediate direction that no contribution, donation or payment of any kind be accepted by the BCI, or any trust or body connected with it, from law colleges, universities or their managements.
Reddy further demanded that the Council publish on its website the complete staff position referred to in his allegations concerning appointments.
Reddy said there were capable people within the Council who could restore the institution and suggested that Mishra's voluntary resignation was “the one course still open to you that would be to your credit.”
“The Bar of this country deserves better than what it is presently receiving from its own Council,” he added.

title: Bihar: 5 killed, 2 injured as speeding bus ploughs into crowd watching orchestra
content:
Bihar: 5 killed, 2 injured as speeding bus ploughs into crowd watching orchestra
Five people were killed and two injured after a speeding bus allegedly ploughed into a crowd watching an orchestra programme at a village in Bihar’s West Champaran.
Five people died and two others were injured after a speeding bus allegedly ran over them while they were watching an orchestra programme organised as part of the Chhathi ceremony of a newborn in a village near Lauriya in Bihar’s West Champaran late Friday evening, police said.
The crowd spilled onto the road while watching the programme when a speeding bus allegedly lost control and ploughed into the gathering around 11pm at Bankatwa Parautola, Lauriya’s station house officer (SHO) Inderjeet Paswan said.
“The gathered crowd spilled onto the road while watch the orchestra show. Suddenly, a speeding bus en route to Bettiah from. Gorakhpur lost control and ploughed into the gathering and as a result five people died and two were injured,” the station house officer said.
Two people died on the spot, while three died during treatment at a government hospital, Narkatiaganj’s sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) Jai Prakash Singh said.
The bus driver sped away with the bus but later fled, leaving the bus behind. The bus was seized by police, an officer said.

content:
BCI Co-Chair seeks Chairman Manan Mishra's resignation, cites NALSAR row: 'The Bar deserves better'
BCI Co-Chair YR Sadashiva Reddy cites ₹150 crore fund diversion, family appointments and NALSAR action among reasons for seeking Manan Mishra’s resignation.
Bar Council of India (BCI) Co-Chairman and senior advocate YR Sadashiva Reddy has demanded Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra’s resignation, saying “the Bar deserves better.”
Reddy has cited alleged diversion of ₹150 crore in funds, family appointments and the “illegal” action against NALSAR students among the reasons for seeking Mishra’s resignation, Live Law reported.
Reddy, in his letter, said he was writing to Mishra “not as an adversary” but as an elected member of the Bar Council of India and a member of the profession for over three decades.
He said remaining silent would amount to “a dereliction of the trust reposed in me by the advocates of this country.”
Reddy said the Bar Council of India is not the “personal estate” of any individual but a statutory body established under the Advocates Act, 1961.
He said it holds funds contributed by lakhs of advocates and exercises regulatory powers over entry into the legal profession, with its funds and powers meant to serve the Bar rather than the individual occupying the chairman’s post.
'The Bar of this country deserves better'
Reddy has demanded that Mishra resign within 15 days of receiving the letter. He has also sought a special meeting of the BCI to consider the matters raised in the letter, along with a special audit of the accounts of the BCI and BCI Trust PEARL First.
He further called for an immediate halt to contributions, donations or payments from law colleges, universities or management by the council or any trust or body connected with it, and sought publication of the complete staff position on the BCI website.
“I hold no personal animosity towards you,” Reddy said, adding that he had served alongside Mishra on the council for a decade. He said the institution “will not recover while you remain in the Chair” and concluded “The Bar of this country deserves better than what it is presently receiving from its own Council. I ask you to allow it that opportunity.”
Manan Mishra says he won't quit, fires at CJP
Manan Mishra on Friday dismissed calls for his resignation, a demand also backed by Abhijeet Dipke's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). His remarks came days after the CJP announced support for a protest at BCI, New Delhi seeking Mishra's resignation and called on “legal cockroaches” to join in.
The Rajya Sabha MP also rejected the use of this term for advocates and said: "Don't you dare use the term "legal cockroaches" ever again. I am telling you this. A lawyer cannot be a cockroach. Lawyers belong to a respected class; they are a highly intelligent group."

title: Bank holiday today: Why are branches closed on August 22? Check full schedule
content:
Bank holiday today: Why are branches closed on August 22? Check full schedule
Banks are closed on August 22 and will also remain closed on Sunday; while more holidays are listed next week
Banks across India will remain closed on Saturday, August 22, 2026, as it is the fourth Saturday of the month. Under Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, banks remain shut on the second and fourth Saturdays, though digital banking and ATM services will continue to be available.
The holiday is in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) rules under which banks remain closed on the fourth Saturday of every month.
Customers planning to visit a bank branch today for banking activities will have to wait until the next working day.
Why are banks closed today?
August 22 is the fourth Saturday of the month, which makes it a scheduled bank holiday under the RBI’s banking holiday rules. The second and fourth Saturdays are observed as holidays for bank branches.
The holiday applies to physical branch operations, so customers who need to visit a branch for banking-related work will be unable to complete those activities today.
What about UPI, ATMs and online banking?
While bank branches are closed, customers can continue to use digital and self-service banking facilities for routine transactions.
UPI and other digital payment services can be used for payments, while ATMs can be used for cash withdrawals and other available services. Customers, therefore, do not necessarily have to wait for bank branches to reopen to conduct routine transactions.
However, people whose banking work requires a physical visit to a branch will have to plan their visit after the holiday.
Banks will remain closed tomorrow
Customers planning to complete bank-related work in person will have to wait one more day, as Sunday, August 23, is also a bank holiday.
People who need to visit a branch in person will have to wait until Monday, August 24, when banks reopen.
Three more closures in August
The RBI holiday further lists three more holidays during the coming week.
On August 25, the holiday is listed as First Onam/Milad-i-Sherif (the Birthday of the Prophet Muhammad).
On August 26, banks will observe Id-E-Milad/Baravafat/Milad-un-Nabi (Birthday of Prophet Mohammad)/Thiruvonam, according to the holiday matrix.
Another holiday is listed for August 28, covering Raksha Bandhan/Pang-Lhabsol/Friday following Eid-i-Milad-ul-Nabi/Sree Narayana Guru Jayanthi/Ayyankali Jayanthi.
Customers planning to visit bank branches during the coming week should therefore check the holiday details before visiting a branch.

title: Over 50 detained, crowd at Jantar Mantar despite no nod: What happened at ‘Reservation Hatao Andolan’
content:
Over 50 detained, crowd at Jantar Mantar despite no nod: What happened at ‘Reservation Hatao Andolan’
The protesters had gathered at Jantar Mantar despite the police's repeated reminder that no permission had been granted to stage a demonstration there.
More than 50 people protesting against the caste-based reservation policy were detained at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on Friday as they gathered under the banner of Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA). The detention followed a stand-off with security personnel in the afternoon, officers aware of the matter said.
The protesters had gathered at Jantar Mantar despite the police's repeated reminder that no permission had been granted to stage a demonstration there. In the morning, hundreds of protesters, mobilised by different organisations representing people from general castes to seek reforms in reservations and quotas, arrived at Jantar Mantar.
ALSO READ: 'Assist the poor, irrespective of caste’: 5 demands at Reservation Hatao Andolan in Delhi
Deep Dive
By noon, police released another statement saying the protest had been permitted, but at Ramlila Ground.
Some protesters alleged that internet jammers had been deployed around the site, making it difficult to access social media from the area. The claim could not be independently verified.
Why were anti-reservation protesters detained?
In a letter, deputy commissioner of police (central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said, "...for peaceful protest of maximum of 500 persons at Ramlila Ground for Reservation Hatao Andolan has been considered in this office and we have no objection..."
However, the protesters, refused to leave Jantar Mantar and had a stand-off with the security personnel guarding the Jantar Mantar protest site.
What is Reservation Hatao Andolan
The protest drive was led by an Instagram page 'Reservation Hatao Andolan', which later called on its followers to participate in an in-person demonstration at Jantar Mantar on August 21. The page has amassed 5.6 million followers on the platform.
What are their demands
The Reservation Hatao Andolan protesters said the government should consider the economic condition of the candidates rather than caste alone. "A poor person, irrespective of caste, should be provided assistance for education, coaching and other needs," news agency PTI quoted a protester associated with the Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha as saying.
Another protester demanded that the existing reservation system should be reassessed to ensure benefits reach the most disadvantaged. "Our contention is that the government should examine whether the present system is achieving its intended purpose and whether benefits are reaching people at the grassroots level," he said.
The protesters have also demanded that a creamy-layer criterion be introduced or income-based exclusion within reserved categories be strengthened.
One of the demands is of providing targeted support for economically weaker people by expanding scholarships, fee assistance, coaching and educational support.
The Reservation Hatao Andolan has sought policy changes and a review of provisions concerning SCs, STs and OBCs, including higher-education reservation policies.
The protesters also raised issues relating to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and higher education policies, including the University Grants Commission framework.
A protester sought the re-evaluation of the reservation policies in light of current social and economic conditions.

title: 'Manan Mishra ji alarms are ringing': CJP's dig as BCI Co-Chair gets behind resignation demand
content:
'Manan Mishra ji alarms are ringing': CJP's dig as BCI Co-Chair gets behind resignation demand
BCI Co-Chairman and senior advocate YR Sadashiva Reddy has sought Mishra’s resignation, saying “the Bar deserves better”.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Friday hailed the Bar Council of India (BCI) co-chairman's call for Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra’s resignation. Co-Chairman and senior advocate YR Sadashiva Reddy sought Mishra’s resignation, saying “the Bar deserves better”, according to a letter shared by LiveLaw.
"The call for Manan Mishra’s resignation is louder today! Now the BCI’s co-chairman has asked him to resign citing that the lawyers deserve better. A huge question mark on financial decisions by Mishra," Das wrote in a post on X.
In a direct dig at the BCI chairman, Das said, "Manan Mishra ji, the alarm bells are ringing. Legal Cockroaches will ensure accountability!"
ALSO READ: CJP's Saurav Das sues commentator for ₹2 crore over home address disclosure
Deep Dive
The jibe came a day after Mishra's remarks against the Cockroach Janta Party. On Friday, the BCI chairman dismissed calls for his resignation and raised objections over the CJP calling the lawyers "legal cockroaches".
"Don't you dare use the term "legal cockroaches" ever again. I am telling you this. A lawyer cannot be a cockroach. Lawyers belong to a respected class; they are a highly intelligent group," said Mishra.
Manan Mishra's tenure challenged in SC
Manan Mishra's tenure as BCI chairman has also been challenged in the Supreme Court, with a petition questioning the senior advocate's more than a decade-long term in the office. The petition, filed by advocate Yogamaya MG, has claimed that Mishra's uninterrupted tenure was in violation of the rules.
The petitioner has contended that Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules prescribes a two-year limit for the Chairman's term. Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules allow a two-year tenure for the Chairman and Vice-Chairman, or until cessation of membership, whichever is earlier. The petition said that an administrative notification cannot extend the tenure beyond what the Rules permit.
ALSO READ: 'Lawyers can't be cockroaches': BCI Chairman Manan Mishra says he won't quit, fumes at CJP
He has also challenged an April 2025 gazette notification that purportedly extends Mishra's tenure until 2030, arguing that such an extension is inconsistent with the statutory framework governing the BCI.
The petition traces Manan Kumar Mishra's tenure as BCI Chairman back to 2012. It stated that although he briefly demitted office in 2014, he returned as Chairman in November that year and has continued in the position ever since. Mishra was once again elected unopposed in March 2025, which the petitioner claimed marks his seventh consecutive term at the helm of the BCI.
The petition also raised questions about the political activities of Mishra while he has remained Chairman of the BCI. It referred to his becoming a Rajya Sabha member after being nominated by the BJP in 2024.

title: 4 of family killed after being hit by speeding SUV on Jaipur highway
content:
4 of family killed after being hit by speeding SUV on Jaipur highway
Four members of a family were killed and another injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them on State Highway-2 in Jaipur’s Fagi on Friday.
Four members of a family were killed and another was injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them on the Fagi-Chaksu Road in Jaipur district on Friday, police said.
The family was returning home to Kumhar locality on Diggi Road in Fagi after working in their fields when the car hit them on State Highway-2.
Police identified the deceased as Satyanarayan (65), his wife Manmouj (60), their daughters-in-law Amrita Devi (35) and Shimla Devi (23).
Satyanarayan’s son and Amrita’s husband, Badrinarayan Kumhar (38), was injured in the accident.
Badrinarayan said he was thrown to the side due to the impact of the collision, while the other four members of his family were crushed by the vehicle. “I was thrown away by the impact of the Bolero, but my parents, my wife and my younger brother’s wife were crushed before my eyes,” he said.
Locals alerted the police and ambulance services following the accident. Police reached the spot and the bodies were taken to Fagi Sub-District Hospital in a 108 ambulance.
Amrita is survived by a 15-year-old daughter and a 13-year-old son. Her five-year-old son had died in a road accident a few years ago. Shimla, who had studied nursing, is survived by her eight-month-old daughter, Vanshika. Her husband, Suresh, works with a jewellery company in Jaipur.
Madhorajpura Station House Officer (SHO) Randhir Singh said the driver fled after abandoning the vehicle at the accident site. “After the accident, the driver fled, leaving the SUV at the spot. Information about the driver is being gathered,” Singh said.
Following the accident, angry residents blocked the road, demanding ₹1 crore in compensation and contractual government jobs for the families of each of the deceased. Police and officials held talks with the protesters, following which the blockade was cleared.
Deputy chief minister Premchand Bairwa expressed grief over the deaths and said he had directed officials to extend all possible assistance to the affected families. “The news of the loss of lives in the road accident on SH-2 Chaksu Road in Fagi, Dudu Assembly constituency, is extremely sad and painful,” Bairwa said in a social media post.
Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal also expressed condolences to the bereaved family and demanded an investigation into the accident.
Police said an investigation into the circumstances leading to the accident was underway and efforts were being made to trace the driver.

title: 50+ Youth Congress workers detained in Pune after clash with ABVP members ahead of Rahul Gandhi's event
content:
50+ Youth Congress workers detained in Pune after clash with ABVP members ahead of Rahul Gandhi's event
Based on a complaint filed by an ABVP member, police registered a first information report on Saturday morning against 50 to 60 Youth Congress workers.
Pune Police have booked 50 to 60 Youth Congress workers following a clash between members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the National Students Union of India (NSUI) at a university hostel, ahead of Rahul Gandhi’s meeting with female students at a city-based college on Saturday evening.
The incident took place at the College of Engineering, Pune (COEP) hostel campus late on Friday, following which police personnel were deployed in large numbers at the premises to prevent any further trouble.
Also read | Face off between ABVP, NSUI at COEP varsity campus ahead of Rahul Gandhi’s event in Pune
The FIR was registered on Saturday morning based on a complaint filed by an ABVP member. Police have booked 50 to 60 Youth Congress workers under Sections 115(2), relating to voluntarily causing simple physical hurt; 189(1), relating to unlawful assembly; 351(1), relating to criminal intimidation; and other relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Maharashtra Police Act.
ABVP alleges students were pressured
ABVP State Secretary Atharva Kulkarni alleged that NSUI workers were pressuring university students to attend Gandhi’s programme, claiming that the organisers were struggling to get an audience.
Also read | Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign gets police nod
“Around 100-150 NSUI workers entered the COEP campus and heckled female students. Some of the students who tried to intervene were also targeted,” he alleged.
NSUI denies allegations
NSUI cadres, however, claimed that some university students had planned to attend Gandhi’s interaction to raise the issue of scholarship money that they said they were not receiving from the state government. They denied the ABVP allegation that any student was heckled.
“When ABVP cadres came to know of this, they went to the university and requested them not to attend Gandhi’s event. We also went there and protested against ABVP for trying to stop students from attending Gandhi’s event,” said city Congress youth president Akshay Jain.
‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign
Earlier, Pune police had granted permission for Rahul Gandhi’s interaction with female students under the party’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign at the AISSPMS ground on August 22, but have imposed 30 conditions on the organisers.
The conditions place the onus of maintaining law and order squarely on the organisers. Police warned that they can cancel the permission and initiate legal action if any activity detrimental to public order is detected during the programme.
“We have received permission from Pune police. We will comply with the conditions police have laid out for the event,” said senior Congress leader Mohan Joshi.
The Congress programme is part of its nationwide ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign, launched to highlight issues concerning students and the education system.

title: Bengaluru: Second IISc student suicide in 15 days as 22-yr-old dies in hostel
content:
Bengaluru: Second IISc student suicide in 15 days as 22-yr-old dies in hostel
A 22-year-old first-year MTech student allegedly died by suicide at IISc Bengaluru, the second such death at the institute in 15 days, police said.
A 22-year-old first-year MTech student allegedly died by suicide in his hostel room at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, on Thursday, police said, in the second such incident at the institute in 15 days.
The student was pursuing MTech in the Department of Computer Science and Automation (CSA). He had been staying at the institute’s Krithika hostel since August 3, when the new academic session for postgraduate programmes began.
The IISc administration did not respond to HT’s queries seeking comment.
In a condolence message to the IISc community, registrar Prof D Nagesh Kumar said the institute was “extremely saddened” by the student’s death on August 20 and expressed condolences to his family and friends.
“We are committed to ensuring that the IISc campus is a safe and inclusive space for everyone,” Kumar said, while urging students and other members of the campus community experiencing emotional distress to use the mental health support services available through the institute’s Wellness Centre.
These include a 24×7 emergency counselling helpline, online counselling, and consultations with counsellors and psychiatrists, the registrar said.
A spokesperson for Sadashivanagar police station said a UDR (Unnatural Death Report) had been registered. “We have sent the body for post-mortem and informed the family. Further investigation is underway,” the spokesperson said on Friday.
The latest incident comes 15 days after the death of 19-year-old, a second-year BTech student, who allegedly died by suicide in his hostel room on August 6. He was a resident of Karnataka’s Chikkaballapura district.

title: Kerala varsity VC alleges foreign forces try to turn youngsters into 'cockroaches'
content:
Kerala varsity VC alleges foreign forces try to turn youngsters into 'cockroaches'
Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala University Vice Chancellor Mohanan Kunnummal on Saturday alleged that some foreign forces were deliberately trying to turn youngsters into "cockroaches" and make them drug addicts, asserting that he was only doing what a VC was expected to do.
Kunnummal was responding to criticism over his recent remarks at an event organised to honour students who excelled in competitive examinations, where he had said students were not "cockroaches" but strong lions.
He had asked students in the audience to raise their voices if they were not cockroaches, but only one or two responded.
Explaining the incident, the VC said the children in the audience were very young and had remained silent because they had not understood what he meant when he asked whether they were cockroaches.
"Some foreign forces are deliberately turning youngsters into cockroaches. They are trying to destroy them by making them drug addicts," he said while responding to a TV channel.
Kunnummal said if he does not resist this, how can he be a vice chancellor?
The VC said some children later told him that they had not heard what he had said at the function and claimed that older students would have responded.
He also alleged that the raising of dissenting voices from abroad could not be viewed as a coincidence.
"A young man comes from America, and many people are supporting him. Can all this be a coincidence? Shouldn't a university vice chancellor think about all this?" he asked.
Responding to criticism over his alleged remarks that those opposing Vande Mataram "do not know their mother", Kunnummal said his words had been misinterpreted.
He said he had intended to refer to the idea of respecting the earth and alleged that he was being branded as a "Sanghi" with certain ulterior motives.
Kunnummal said only people with "malicious intentions" had distorted his remarks and turned them into controversies.
On allegations about his affiliation with the RSS, he said the country was being governed by people who believed in RSS ideology and that they did not need his help.
"I am only doing what a vice chancellor is supposed to do," he said.
The VC also criticised the Students' Federation of India , the students' wing of the CPI, which has been staging protests against him over various issues.
He alleged that SFI activists recently portrayed him as the mythical demon king Mahabali and buried the effigy in front of the university.
This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

title: NHAI orders audits, inspections for new national highways inaugurated by PM Modi
content:
NHAI orders audits, inspections for new national highways inaugurated by PM Modi
NHAI has issued new safety and quality guidelines for newly inaugurated highways, including independent audits and frequent inspections of major projects.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued new quality, safety and event-management guidelines for newly inaugurated national highway projects, including provisions for independent audits of major projects and more intensive inspections after highways open to traffic.
The guidelines, issued on Friday, come after a review of existing protocols and incorporate “experience and lessons learnt” from recent inauguration and foundation-stone laying events by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The move comes weeks after the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway, inaugurated in April, developed potholes, cracks and a cave-in following intense rain.
Also Read: Centre considering 65-km expressway linking Delhi-Dehradun to Noida, Faridabad
NHAI has also directed its media teams to proactively monitor print and digital media reports after such events and, in coordination with regional offices, prepare ready responses or “counter narratives” to address reports it considers “factually incorrect or politically motivated”.
In its policy circular, NHAI said the addendum supersedes an earlier addendum issued in October 2025.
Greenfield expressways, high-speed corridors, specialised projects and projects with a total capital cost of more than ₹2,500 crore may undergo an independent audit by a reputed third-party entity or premier institutions such as Indian Institute of Technology (IITs) and National Institute of Technology (NITs). The audit may examine the anticipated impact of traffic after opening, drainage and related issues.
Also Read: 80 days of Delhi–Dehradun E-way: Light rain creates sinkholes in Shamli, videos viral
The NHAI has also prescribed joint inspections of newly opened highway stretches by the contractor or concessionaire’s project manager and the supervision consultant’s team leader. These are to be conducted weekly for the first three months and fortnightly for the next three months, covering pavement and riding quality, drainage, safety installations and embankment slopes.
Route patrol vehicles will also regularly cover the full length of highways after opening. Defects or anticipated deterioration are to be geo-tagged and immediately reported to the project director, contractor or concessionaire and supervision consultant for rectification.
The circular sets out arrangements for large Prime Ministerial events, noting that attendance can range from 25,000 to one lakh people. It calls for adequate venue capacity, parking, connectivity, security, crowd management and contingency measures for adverse weather.
It also says the number of officials at a function should preferably be restricted to 500 and that event preparations should be completed at least 24 hours before the programme.

title: Kerala HC allows conditional suspension of jail sentence of 4 convicts in 2003 Muthanga land agitation cases
content:
Kerala HC allows conditional suspension of jail sentence of 4 convicts in 2003 Muthanga land agitation cases
Thiruvananthapuram: The Kerala High Court on Friday allowed the conditional suspension of the five-yearjail sentence imposed on four convicts in the case of attempt to murder of police constable Abdul Salam and forest range officer PK Sasidharan in connection with the 2003 Muthanga land struggle in Wayanad
Thiruvananthapuram: The Kerala High Court on Friday allowed the conditional suspension of the five-yearjail sentence imposed on four convicts in the case of attempt to murder of police constable Abdul Salam and forest range officer PK Sasidharan in connection with the 2003 Muthanga land struggle in Wayanad.
The four accused -- M Geethanandan (72), Binu (54), Ramesan (53) and Anilkumar (48) -- were found guilty by the Kalpetta Sessions Court on July 31 in the case and imposed five years rigorous imprisonment and fines of ₹10,000 each for a range of offences including attempt to murder, wrongful restraint, wrongful assembly and rioting.
The HC bench of Justice A Badharudeen, hearing petitions filed by the accused challenging their conviction by the sessions court, held that they have an ‘arguable case.’
The appellants’ counsel had pointed out that the sessions judge did not conclusively find commission of the offences and only prima facie found the offences. The standing counsel for the CBI, which investigated the cases with regard to the Muthanga land agitation, also submitted that they are filing an appeal to ‘address the flaws in the judgement.’
“Going through the judgement and the period of sentence imposed, at par with the arguments advanced pointing out the innocence of the applicants, the appellants have an arguable case. Since it is submitted by the learning public prosecutor that the appellants have criminal antecedents, there is no reason to disallow the application and therefore, the petition to suspend the sentence is allowed on the following conditions,” the High Court ruled.
The court directed the apellants to deposit the entire fine amount imposed by the sessions court, execute bail bond of ₹1 lakh each with two solvent sureties and not get involved in any other crimes. The accused must not be released on bail until the fine amounts are realised, the court ordered.
The cases pertain to the historic agitation for land spearheaded by the Adivasi Gothra Maha Sabha under the leadership of Geethanandan and CK Janu inside the Wayanad wildlife sanctuary in Muthanga in January 2003 in protest against then UDF government’s inaction on allotting land parcels to tribals.
Clashes broke out on the morning of February 19, 2003 when personnel from the police and forest departments began an operation to evict the protesters from the wildlife sanctuary in Muthanga. Pellets and tear gas shells were fired by the police in a bid to clear the area. The tensions escalated when constable Salam and forest officer Sasidharan were detained by the tribals, resulting in police firing. One tribal, Jogi, was killed in the firing, while police constable Vinod succumbed to fatal injuries sustained during the clashes.
While official records point to only two fatalities, unofficial estimates by human rights groups and tribal outfits stated over a dozen deaths. The alleged indiscriminate firing by the police on the tribals, allegedly without any provocation, were widely condemned by rights groups and remains a dark chapter in the history of Adivasi land rights in Kerala. Late Justice VR Krishna Iyer, in a preliminary report, termed the police action as ‘excessive’.
The incident led to policy changes in the allotment of land to tribals in the state and propelled successive governments to address landlessness among tribals.

title: ‘My son rushed woman to hospital’: Andhra MP Lingamaneni Ramesh on Hyderabad Aston Martin crash
content:
‘My son rushed woman to hospital’: Andhra MP Lingamaneni Ramesh on Hyderabad Aston Martin crash
Ramesh said that Sanjush was driving the vehicle when the accident occurred and immediately took the injured woman to a hospital.
Andhra Pradesh Rajya Sabha MP and Jana Sena Party (JSP) leader Lingamaneni Ramesh reacted on Friday amid reports of his son's involvement in connection with the death of a 26-year-old woman in a Hyderabad road accident. The politician said that his 21-year-old son took the victim to hospital immediately and reported the incident to police.
Lingamaneni Sanjush, the MP's son, was booked after a woman died after being hit by a high-speed Aston Martin he was allegedly driving.
In a statement issued on Friday, Ramesh said, "It is deeply unfortunate and heartbreaking that the road accident which occurred in Hyderabad on 16th of August, 2026 and which led to the unfortunate loss of the young woman. I extend my heartfelt condolences to her family. No words can lessen their grief, and my family and I stand with them during this extremely painful time. We will extend every possible support to the bereaved family. I request you all not to speculate or prejudge the circumstances. The investigation must establish the complete facts."
Also read | Son of Jana Sena MP booked after his Aston Martin kills woman in Hyderabad
Ramesh added that Sanjush was driving the vehicle when the accident occurred and immediately took the injured woman to a hospital.
“Immediately after the accident, my son, Sanjush, who was driving the vehicle, shifted the young woman to the hospital without any delay. He subsequently reported the accident to the police authorities and provided all the necessary details. A case was duly registered, and three separate medical tests were conducted on my son, which returned negative. The investigation is presently underway, and my son is fully co-operating with the authorities,” Ramesh was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.
The accident took place near Inorbit Mall in Hyderabad’s Madhapur area, where 26-year-old Bharati Mukhi, who worked at a store, was fatally hit by an Aston Martin on August 16. Police have named 21-year-old Sanjush as the accused and registered a case under Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for allegedly causing death by a rash or negligent act.
‘Nothing is being concealed’, says Ramesh
The MP said his family had not attempted to avoid the legal process and maintained that nothing was being concealed in the matter.
Also read | Drug, alcohol tests of accused in Hyderabad Aston Martin crash return negative
"Nothing is being concealed in this matter, nor have we attempted to avoid the legal process in any way. We have the utmost respect for the law, and my son has complied with every procedure required by the authorities," the statement reads.
Ramesh also said he would extend his full cooperation to the police and the ongoing investigation.
MP urges public not to spread unverified information
Ramesh appealed to the public to respect the grief of the bereaved family and refrain from circulating false or unverified information about the accident.
It added, "As a person holding a responsible position, I assure everyone that I will extend my complete cooperation to the Police Department and the ongoing investigation. We have full faith that the truth will emerge through a fair and impartial legal process. At this sensitive and painful time, I humbly request everyone to respect the grief of the bereaved family, refrain from spreading false or unverified information and allow the law to take its course."
(With inputs from ANI)
