title: Badminton World Championships: India’s hopes rest on doubles after Sindhu, Ayush exit
content:
Contrasting games, similar fortunes — the Indian singles campaign at the badminton World Championships ended in heartbreak with P.V. Sindhu and Ayush Shetty bowing out of the competition in the pre-quarterfinals here on Thursday.
The day that started with an Indian victory ended with one but the results in between left the two doubles pairs, one each in men and women, shouldering the host’s hopes in the prestigious tournament.
Badminton World Championships: Treesa-Gayatri in semifinals, assured of medal
Treesa Jolly and Gaytri Gopichand advanced to the quarterfinals with a 21-16, 21-12 win against Japan’s Rin Iwanaga & Kie Nakanishi while Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, returning to competitive action after almost three months, struggled to find their rhythm before prevailing 21-23, 21-19, 21-17 against Junaidi Arif and Roy King Yap of Malaysia.
Sindhu fought her way back into the match after losing the first game and kept pushing hard in the decider before faltering right at the end of the 88-minute long battle, going down 21-11, 15-21, 21-17 to World No. 3 Wang Zhi Yi.
The high-intensity face-off kept the packed, vocal crowd on the edge of their seats all through with neither player willing to concede any quarter.
Wang, playing from the slower side, raced ahead in the opening game and never let her grip slip, her impeccable defence returning everything Sindhu tried to throw at her while using her flat drives and deceptive cross-court drops at crucial moments.
The long rallies that Sindhu had warned about a day before were duly played out — the longest of them being 54 shots even as 40-plus rallies were the norm throughout.
Sindhu hit back after the change of ends, racing to an 8-4 lead before Wang clawed back but unforced errors coupled with Sindhu’s quick returns and shuttle placement saw her lose ground.
The decider stayed level for large parts, the players constantly exchanging the slimmest of leads and staying level right till 15-15, when Wang took a medical time-out for a cramp in her left leg after a failed dive. She came back, took off a couple of points and hobbled again, this time clutching her right thigh. And then she closed out the match.
Earlier Ayush, who had had two wildly different matches before this, failed to capitalise on his chances against Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan to go down tamely 21-19, 21-11. The last time the two had played at the China Open, Ayush had won in three games but on Thursday, the Indonesian raised his game to another level and never allowed Ayush a look in.
In the morning, Treesa and Gayatri extended their dream run, knocking out the seventh-ranked last year’s bronze medalists to reach the quarterfinals for their best ever show in the tournament.
It was a roller-coaster for Treesa and Gayatri in the opening game. They led 13-9 at one point, dropped seven consecutive points to trail 13-16 and then reeled off eight straight points to win 21-16.
The momentum carried on in the second game as the youngsters became the first Indian women’s doubles team to reach the last eight of the Championships after Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa — the only Indian women’s pair to win a medal in the event — since 2015 and raised hopes of a second medal in the category.
As the day came to a close, a rusty Satwik and Chirag, playing their first match of the tournament, failed to convert their chances to concede the first game before regrouping and finding the momentum, then kept going, riding as much on the late-night, packed stands as their own stubbornness to prove a point.
They kept rotating, Chirag shouldering as much of the back court duties and winners as Satwik before taking the decider 21-17.
Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, meanwhile, lost to China’s Guo Xinn Wa & Chen Fang Hui 21-16, 21-5.

title: India vs Sri Lanka Tests: Bowling coach Bahutule backs Kuldeep for 2nd Test; keeps Saransh Jain in contention
content:
Nostalgia may have enveloped Sairaj Bahutule when he entered the SSC Ground. He would have remembered his last Test played at the same venue in 2001, a game India lost. The Indian spin-bowling coach, though, quickly immersed himself in the nets here Friday (August 21, 2026).
Later, near the dugout, he spoke to the media about the twirly men under his watch. Many questions centred around Kuldeep Yadav, a fine talent but seemingly rusty at the moment.
“Kuldeep has been bowling extremely well. It’s just that due to the situation that arose in Galle, he had to play a different role. He tried his best to execute that role,” Bahutule said.
Getting more technical in his analysis, the spin-coach added, “We had to see how the trajectory and the speeds work in every session. As the days went by, there was a demand for different types of speeds and trajectories; he definitely was making an effort to bowl that.”
Turning his eye towards Manav Suthar, Bahutule said, “He is somebody who has bowled a lot in domestic cricket and has done the hard yards. He understands his bowling well. What we try to do is to see how that awareness of bowling gets better in different conditions, on different pitches, and against different batters. He is very accurate, and his trajectories are getting better. He puts in a lot on the ball, the revolutions are good and he is somebody who is like a banker for us.”
Bahutule also spoke about the essential nature of ideal preparation. “It’s very difficult for a player sometimes to adjust to different formats. But I think what we did coming early on this tour was — in that warm-up game and in the open net sessions — we trained well and got to understand the conditions and could adapt to them. The amount of cricket being played is quite a bit, but our job as coaches is to manage their minds and help them adapt,” he said.
Saransh in the fray
With Sri Lanka adding left-handed batters to the squad, the temptation to play off-spinner Saransh Jain is real, and Bahutule did not deny that.
“There is another day to go before the Test. We will have a look at the pitch and understand what will be the need. Yes, the (left-handed) additions are there in their team. We will definitely consider him (Saransh Jain) once the pitch is completely ready to play,” he said.
The speculation over Kuldeep’s berth in the playing eleven lingered, and when another question was raised, Bahutule said, “He has been a fabulous bowler over the years. Yes, the pitches sometimes are slow, and sometimes the ball operates differently for the spinners on certain surfaces. But for me, he has always been a match winner, and he definitely is in the scheme of things. When the ball becomes softer, it becomes even more difficult for a wrist-spinner like him.”

title: Portugal get their revenge on Spain — this time in cricket — after WC heartbreak
content:
Portugal have found a rather unexpected way to avenge their FIFA World Cup heartbreak against Spain.
Just over a month after Cristiano Ronaldo and Co. were knocked out of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by their neighbours, Portugal got one back â not on a football pitch, but on a cricket field.
Portugal defeated Spain by 57 runs in the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Sub Regional Qualifier C in 2026, ending Spain's campaign and keeping their own dream of reaching the 2028 T20 World Cup alive.
The football defeat had come in July, when Spain edged Portugal 1-0 in the Round of 16 at the Dallas Stadium in Arlington, USA. Mikel Merino scored the decisive goal in stoppage time of regulation time, sending Ronaldo's Portugal out of the tournament.
This time, though, it was Portugal celebrating at Spain's expense.
Portugal turn the tables on Spain
Led by former Australia international 
Moises Henriques
, Portugal produced a composed performance to claim the crucial qualifying victory.
Spain captain Christian Munoz-Mills won the toss and chose to field, but Portugal built a competitive total of 160/6.
Dhavalkumar Norotam made 23 and Christopher De Freitas scored 39 as Portugal made a steady start without quite managing to dominate the Spanish attack. 
Henriques, meanwhile, contributed 18 but could not convert his start into a substantial innings.
Portugal accelerated late in the innings through Craig Cachopa, who struck 25 off 21 balls, while Carlos Nunes added 15 off nine. Jeremy Martins provided an important final push with an unbeaten 18 off just eight deliveries.
Yasir Ali and Lorne Burns were Spain's best bowlers, taking two wickets apiece.
Spain's chase initially threatened to become interesting, but Portugal's bowlers quickly put the brakes on the pursuit.
Sebastian de Oliveira made the breakthrough early, while Martins also chipped in as Portugal reduced Spain to 32/3. Yasir Ali and Daniel Doyle Calle then began rebuilding the innings and gave Spain hope of mounting a serious chase.
Portugal close the door on Spain
Siraj Ullah Khadem changed the complexion of the contest in the 11th over when he bowled Yasir for 29.
With the pitch making life difficult for incoming batters, Portugal steadily tightened their grip. Khadem finished with impressive figures of 2/19, while Edward Fleming delivered the decisive blow with a three-wicket haul for just 13 runs.
Spain's promising chase soon turned into a procession, and Martins completed the job by bowling Lorne Burns as Portugal wrapped up a 57-run victory.
The triumph sends Portugal into the ICC Men's T20 World Cup Europe Qualifier in 2027, putting them one step closer to a place in the global qualifying tournament for the 2028 T20 World Cup.
Portugal join Jersey and Denmark in the Europe Qualifier, while Scotland enter directly because of the exceptional circumstances surrounding their participation in the 2026 T20 World Cup. Italy and the Netherlands, meanwhile, advance directly to the Global Qualifier.
For Portugal, the result offers a wonderfully light-hearted twist to their recent sporting rivalry with Spain: Spain may have won the football battle, but Portugal have claimed the cricket rematch.

title: India vs Sri Lanka Tests: Visitors brave the heat in Colombo nets ahead of 2nd Test
content:

title: In Pulwama, cricket heals wounds of the past
content:
Under lights cricket in once-volatile and conflict-ridden Pulwama district in south Kashmir has come as a catharsis for locals. For a change, hundreds of locals, along with family members and carrying food items, stayed back till late Wednesday (August 19, 2026) night to watch the first match of the Royal Premier League Pulwama.
“The scenes at the stadium in Pulwama were unprecedented. It has provided a platform to locals to laugh and smile. It’s also an act to bring positivity. Kashmir’s youths are witness to the misery in the past. This is a small effort to give them a chance to be happy and hopeful,” Pulwama legislator Waheed-ur-Rehmaan Parra told The Hindu.
Also Read | How Jammu & Kashmir moved from the periphery to the centre: Ranji Trophy
Irfan Sarkar, a local youth from Pulwama, in a rare galvanisation of support to cricket with local sponsors, has provided digital boards, replays on live screens, social media streaming and commentary.
“It’s the 2nd Edition of the Royal Premier League Pulwama. Ten teams will play all their games under floodlights, which allows locals to attend matches after sundown. Around 20,000 attended the first match. They were cheering, drumming and celebrating every moment together,” said Mr. Sarkar.
Pulwama has been on the edge, with youths clashing with security forces on the streets during street uprisings of 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2016 over a slew of issues. Scores of civilians died and many local youths took to militancy after Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani was killed in an anti-militancy operation in south Kashmir in 2016. Still, Pulwama is known from raids by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), State Investigation Agency and the J&K Police.
Nightlife has been a dream for the turmoil-hit district. However, cricket in the past two years has acted as a healing process for locals. “Kashmir is watching. Kashmir is playing. Kashmir is celebrating. This is more than cricket. It is hope over fear, unity over division, and life over darkness,” said Mr. Parra.
The cricket tournament has allowed the eateries to do business till midnight. “Chicken items are selling like hot cakes. It’s rare to see customers after 10 p.m. in the district,” said Niyaz Ahmad, a local eatery owner.
Mr. Parra said sees night cricket also taking cricketing talent to a new level. “It allows sports lovers to exhibit their talent and perform under pressing conditions of crowds. It will help players to grow mentally tough,” said Mr. Parra.

title: Pakistan vs England Test: Brook maintains stranglehold over Pakistan for dominant England
content:
England's Harry Brook extended his remarkable record against Pakistan to put the hosts into a commanding position on the second day of the first test at Headingley.
Brook cashed in on some indisciplined bowling from a lightweight seam attack to make 91 from 93 balls as England opened a 195-run lead with two first innings wickets still standing.
It took the Yorkshireman's average in his 12 test appearances against Pakistan above 85.
Dropped on one at second slip by Salman Ali Agha off Khurram Shahzad, Brook illuminated a grey, rain-shortened day for his home crowd with an innings containing 13 fours before falling to spinner Ali Usman who finished with 5-92.
Brook shared a fifth-wicket partnership of 120 with the recalled Dan Lawrence who made 51 from 79 balls.
Lawrence, back after two years in the wilderness, filled the boots of Ben Stokes after his retirement in positive fashion, before top-edging a sweep off Usman.
The pair made the most of the base laid earlier by Joe Root and Jordan Cox.
Root made 66 – his 109th test innings of 50 or more - and Cox 73 – the first of his career – in a stand of 150 for the third wicket.
It was a surprise when Root played across a straight ball from Khurram Shahzad to be trapped lbw, four balls after Cox departed after misjudging the length of a full ball from Usman to be caught behind.
Cox, given his chance at No 3 by Jacob Bethell’s knee injury, hit Khurram for seven fours in the space of 12 balls on the way to a maiden test half-century.
England, who were helped by some poor ground fielding from Pakistan, closed on 366-8 after Usman dismissed Gus Atkinson and Ollie Robinson with successive balls in the 80th over.
Even though England now have caretaker coach Marcus Trescothick in charge after the exit of Brendon McCullum from the red ball side, the run rate was up with there with the Bazball era.
"Headingley is one of quickest-scoring grounds in the country and Tres has been really good with us," said Cox.
"He has told everyone: ‘bat your way, bat how you want to and enjoy it’ and that’s what we’ve done.
"Hopefully the boys can get 50 runs tomorrow – we’ve still got Jamie Smith and Jofra Archer in there who can give it a good whack - and then get to our work."
Pakistan, who last won a test in England eight years ago, are in a tight corner. With better weather forecast for the remaining three days, they look unlikely to receive much assistance from the elements in their efforts to get out of it.
"England have the upper hand but we will try to score as many runs as we can second innings," said Usman.
"We have to get the two wickets as soon as possible and then try to score runs as a batting unit. Hopefully our batters can make a comeback and save the test match."

title: Premier League: Man United, Tottenham suffer shock defeats in season opener
content:
Manchester United
 and Tottenham Hotspur's new-season optimism was punctured in emphatic fashion as both clubs suffered shock defeats in their 
Premier League
 openers on Saturday.
United, under permanent manager Michael Carrick and with a revamped midfield, were beaten 0-2 by promoted Hull City, while Tottenham's expensive new-look squad was completely outplayed in a 0-3 defeat at Brentford.
For two clubs carrying significant expectations into the new campaign, the opening-day setbacks served as an early reminder that rebuilding ambitions do not necessarily translate into immediate results.
Man United stumble at Hull
Hull marked their return to the top flight after a nine-year absence with a memorable victory, while United were left to reflect on a performance that raised more questions than answers.
First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, both coming from set pieces, condemned United to a disappointing defeat against a side widely expected to be involved in the relegation battle.
Carrick, rewarded with a permanent contract after guiding United to third place last season and Champions League qualification, acknowledged that his side still have work to do.
"It was never going to be perfect,â Carrick said.
United had strengthened their midfield during the summer with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Brighton's Carlos Baleba could reportedly be another target. Marcus Rashford also returned from his loan spell at Barcelona and came on as a halftime substitute against Hull.
However, neither Rashford nor the new midfield additions could inspire a response as United struggled to create momentum.
The result underlined the scale of the task facing Carrick at a club that have not won the Premier League since 2013 under Alex Ferguson.
âOne game doesnât change the direction of everything,â Carrick said. âIt doesnât change the direction of the football club.â
Tottenham humbled, while other promoted clubs shine
Tottenham's defeat was arguably even more striking given their summer spending. Spurs have invested around $300 million in new players, with Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali arriving from Newcastle for a club-record $133 million.
Yet Brentford's settled side exposed Tottenham's lack of cohesion, racing into a 2-0 lead by the 33rd minute through Keane Lewis-Potter and Vitaly Janelt. Michael Kayode added a third shortly after halftime, while Igor Thiago struck the post with a penalty as Brentford threatened an even heavier defeat.
Elsewhere, Everton began with a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace, watched by new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a season-ticket holder at the club. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry scored for Everton.
Ipswich also enjoyed a winning return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 thanks to Jack Clarke's 90th-minute goal. Leeds United claimed another late victory, with Anton Stach's 88th-minute free kick securing a 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Arsenal had already made a winning start to their title defence, beating second-tier champions Coventry 3-0 on Friday.
On Sunday, Manchester City will look to recover from their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal when they visit Bournemouth, while Liverpool travel to Newcastle.

title: Shoriful Islam makes history with record seven-wicket haul against Australia
content:
Bangladesh pacer 
Shoriful Islam
 etched his name in the record books on the second day of the second Test against Australia in Mackay, becoming the first bowler from his country to claim a seven-wicket haul against Australia. He also became the first Bangladesh bowler to take seven wickets in a Test innings, with his sensational figures of 7/48 now the best-ever by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests.
Shoriful produced a sensational spell of 7/48 in 15 overs to overshadow 
Mitchell Starc
's six-wicket haul and keep Bangladesh alive in a Test that appeared to be slipping away after they were bowled out for just 64.
The left-arm pacer also registered the best figures by a Bangladesh bowler away from home in Tests, surpassing Taijul Islam's 7/138 against Zimbabwe in Harare earlier this year.
Shoriful tears through Australia
Australia began their innings at 41/3 but recovered through a 77-run partnership between Steve Smith and Cameron Green. Smith made 42 off 74 balls, including six fours, while Green continued the repair work with a fluent 67 off 105 balls, hitting 10 boundaries.
Shoriful, however, kept Bangladesh in the contest with his pace, movement and bounce. He eventually reduced Australia to 148/8 before the hosts' lower order mounted another resistance.
Green and Nathan Lyon added 38 runs before Shoriful ended Green's resistance with a pinpoint yorker to complete his magnificent seven-wicket haul. Lyon then remained unbeaten on 32 off 62 balls, including four boundaries and a six, and helped Australia reach 210.
Lyon and Josh Hazlewood added another 24 runs for the final wicket, frustrating Bangladesh before Taijul Islam dismissed Hazlewood to end the innings.
Australia's total gave them a commanding 146-run first-innings lead.
Shoriful's achievement came only one Test after Hasan Mahmud had set a new Bangladesh record against Australia with 6/55 in Darwin. Hasan's nine wickets in that match helped Bangladesh secure their first-ever Test victory in Australia.
Starc strikes again as Bangladesh struggle
Earlier, Australia had won the toss and opted to field, with Starc responding to Bangladesh's first-Test victory in emphatic fashion.
The left-arm quick tore through the Bangladesh batting lineup with astonishing figures of 6/12, while Pat Cummins claimed three wickets as the visitors were dismissed for just 64. Shoriful was Bangladesh's top scorer with 14.
Bangladesh began their second innings under pressure and reached 39/3 by the end of the first session. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto was unbeaten on 23, with Mushfiqur Rahim on four.
Starc had already taken two wickets, while Cummins added one as Bangladesh trailed by 107 runs.
Despite Shoriful's historic spell, Australia remain firmly in control and Bangladesh face a daunting task to avoid conceding the series-levelling Test.

title: Ronaldo becomes first player in the Football history to achieve unprecedented feat
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has added another remarkable milestone to his extraordinary career, becoming the first professional footballer to score in 25 consecutive league seasons. The 41-year-old Portuguese superstar achieved the feat on Friday, August 21, during Al-Nassr's Saudi Pro League clash against Al-Riyadh.
Ronaldo extends historic scoring streak
Ronaldo began his senior scoring run during the 2002-03 season, when he found the net for Sporting CP as a teenager. More than two decades later, that streak remains unbroken. His latest goal came after he was introduced as a substitute in the 62nd minute. Ronaldo eventually found the net in the 83rd minute, converting a low cross from Ayman Yahya with a composed left-footed finish from inside the area.
The goal saw Ronaldo surpass Swedish great Zlatan IbrahimoviÄ, who had previously held the record with goals in 24 consecutive league seasons.
977 career goals and counting
The landmark strike took Ronaldo's official senior career tally to 977 goals for club and country. His goals have come across five clubs and the Portugal national team:
Ronaldo's latest effort also helped Al-Nassr secure a 4-0 away victory over Al-Riyadh, giving the defending Saudi Pro League champions a perfect start to their 2026-27 campaign.
Ronaldo's race to 1,000 goals
The historic achievement comes as Ronaldo continues his pursuit of the extraordinary 1,000-goal milestone. The Portuguese forward is now just 23 goals short of reaching four figures in official senior football.
However, the next chapter of his career could also be his final one. Ronaldo recently indicated that the 2026-27 season could probably be his last in professional football, while his current Al-Nassr contract runs until June 2027.

title: Saransh Jain makes India debut at 33: Who is the allrounder taking on Sri Lanka?
content:
NEW DELHI: Saransh Jain's long wait for India recognition ended on Sunday when the 33-year-old allrounder made his Test debut against Sri Lanka in the second match of the series.
Jain was presented his India cap by veteran allrounder 
Ravindra Jadeja
 during the team's huddle, marking the culmination of a domestic career that has stretched over a decade.
His debut also makes Jain the first India player to make his international debut after turning 33 since Robin Singh in 1998.
India captain 
Shubman Gill
 won the toss and opted to bat first, backing his team to make the most of the conditions.
"Batting first, yes. It looks like a much harder wicket than Galle. The pitch got slower and started to turn, but this will be a good wicket to bat on," Gill said.
2nd Test - Playing XIs
- India XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill(c), Rishabh Pant(w), Ravindra Jadeja, Dhruv Jurel, Saransh Jain, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna
- Sri Lanka XI: Lahiru Udara, Kamil Mishara, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva(c), Sonal Dinusha, Niroshan Dickwella(w), Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando
Who is Saransh Jain?
Born in Madhya Pradesh, Jain is a left-handed batter and right-arm offspinner whose strongest credentials have come in red-ball cricket.
In 54 first-class matches, he has scored 2,223 runs at an average of 31.75 and taken 188 wickets at 27.30. He has also played 67 List A and 20 T20 matches, but it was his consistency in the longer format that eventually pushed him into India's reckoning.
Jain is the son of former first-class cricketer Subodh Jain and has spent much of his career away from the spotlight.
He made his Ranji Trophy debut in 2014 but emerged as a significant domestic performer only in 2022. 
Having played just eight first-class matches until then, Jain starred in the Ranji Trophy knockouts for Madhya Pradesh, taking 13 wickets and scoring a half-century as the team won its maiden title.
Late bloomer earns India call-up
The latest Ranji Trophy season was arguably Jain's best yet. He scored 518 runs at an impressive average of 57.55 and claimed 30 wickets at 20.43.
That came after an outstanding Duleep Trophy campaign for Central Zone, where Jain scored two half-centuries and took 16 wickets across two matches to earn Player of the Series honours.
His performances eventually brought him closer to the India setup. Last month, Jain was among the net bowlers preparing India's batters ahead of the one-off Test against Afghanistan in New Chandigarh.
Now, after years of domestic cricket and a breakthrough in his early 30s, Jain has finally received his opportunity at the highest level â making his India debut at an age when most players are already well into their international careers.

title: India seek 2-0 sweep: Gill, Jaiswal look to bounce back; Kuldeep to miss out?
content:
Having found their âsweet spotâ in Tests, India will look to carry their winning momentum into the second and final game against an injury-hit Sri Lanka at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo on Sunday.
Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant and left-arm spinner Manav Suthar were the stars of Indiaâs 165-run win in Galle, with Suthar registering match figures of 10/131. If captain 
Shubman Gill
 and opener 
Yashasvi Jaiswal
 get going, India will fancy a 2-0 clean sweep in Colombo that would strengthen their push for a 2027 World Test Championship final slot and lift them from fifth to fourth in the standings.
Indiaâs last overseas Test series win came in the West Indies in July 2023, when they prevailed 1-0. Since then, they have lost 1-3 in Australia and drawn series in South Africa (1-1) and England (2-2). At home, they have suffered 0-3 and 0-2 whitewashes against New Zealand and South Africa respectively.
The Galle victory, however, has revived their campaign. Padikkal (167 and 44), Rahul (82 and 35) and Pant (66) handled Sri Lankaâs spin attack adroitly, while Suthar underlined his credentials as a serious Test prospect.
The focus will now turn to Gill and Jaiswal, both of whom struggled in Galle. Sri Lankaâs premier left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya dismissed Gill in both innings, while Jaiswal was run out in the first before edging Asitha Fernando to the wicketkeeper in the second.
Kuldeep or Saransh?
The key selection call is whether India persist with left-arm wrist-spinner 
Kuldeep Yadav
, who took just one wicket for 103 runs in Galle, or hand a debut to 33-year-old off-spinning allrounder Saransh Jain. Jain could offer greater variety against Sri Lankaâs left-handers.

You can’t do that in a two-Test series, the most you can do is draw it. A short turnaround between Tests is fine. Other teams are doing that as well.”
Despite India’s poor Test run under his watch, with the team having lost 10 Tests since he took charge in July 2024, Gambhir said he remains unfazed.
Asked about his discussions with selection chief Ajit Agarkar, Gambhir said, “It’s only about how we want to move forward in cricket. Rankings do not matter. We are not struggling. Since the England tour, we have played reasonable Test cricket.”

India vs Sri Lanka Live: SSC promises a different challenge

India vs Sri Lanka Live Score: India look to seal series in Colombo
India head into the second and final Test against Sri Lanka at the Sinhalese Sports Club with a chance to complete a 2-0 series sweep. Their 165-run victory in Galle has given Shubman Gill’s side confidence, with Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant and Manav Suthar making key contributions. India will now look to build on that performance in Colombo. Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal will be keen to find form after modest scores in the first Test. A win would also strengthen India’s push for another World Test Championship final appearance.
India vs Sri Lanka Live, 2nd Test: The second and final Test between Sri Lanka and India moves from Galle to Colombo, where the Sinhalese Sports Club will provide a contrasting backdrop to the series opener. Unlike Galle, SSC has no fort or ocean views. Instead, the ground sits amid Colombo’s modern skyline, with the 350m Lotus Tower standing prominently beyond the stadium.
Despite its urban surroundings, SSC retains plenty of traditional cricketing character. Its two-tier stands, grass banks and manual scoreboard provide a link to an earlier era, while its rich history makes it one of Asia’s most important Test venues. The India-Sri Lanka contest will be the 47th Test at SSC, putting it second only to Galle among Asian venues in terms of Tests hosted.
The venue could produce a very different challenge from Galle. SSC has generally offered good batting conditions, with teams batting first often piling up big totals. The toss could therefore be crucial. At the same time, the forecast suggests rain could interrupt play on each of the five days, while the Colombo heat is expected to make life difficult for the bowlers. Spinners have taken 45 wickets in the last three Tests at the venue, 10 more than pacers.
India arrive with momentum after their 165-run win in Galle. Padikkal, Rahul, Pant and Suthar were the standout performers, but Gill and Jaiswal will be determined to improve after disappointing scores in the opener. India’s batting depth and Suthar’s emergence have given the team plenty of confidence as they look to secure a 2-0 sweep and boost their hopes of reaching the 2027 World Test Championship final.
Sri Lanka, however, will hope home conditions can help them fight back. Kamil Mishara is set to replace the dropped Nishan Madhushka at the top, while Sahan Arachchige is in contention after strong performances for Sri Lanka A. Pasindu Sooriyabandara is expected to retain his place at No. 3.
India also face a selection call over their spin attack. Saransh Jain has bowled extensively in the nets and could make his Test debut, particularly with Sri Lanka expected to field another left-hander. Kuldeep Yadav, meanwhile, was absent from training sessions, adding to speculation over his place.
With both teams facing contrasting objectives, the Colombo Test promises a battle between India’s momentum and Sri Lanka’s desire for a comeback.

title: India face must-win Australia clash, need Netherlands favour to keep World Cup dream alive
content:
âRemember, Red, hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.â
Those famous closing words from âThe Shawshank Redemptionâ could well be the Indian womenâs hockey teamâs mantra as they chase a place in the World Cup semifinals against all odds.
After going down to the Netherlands in their last match following another brave performance, India will have to beat Australia on Sunday in their second game of Pool E and hope that China lose to Netherlands in the other group game.
Considering how Netherlands have played so far, beating China doesnât seem like an improbable task. But China, too, havenât been pushovers. They have remained unbeaten in the tournament so far and gave the Dutch a run for their money at the Olympics final. In their last four Pro League meetings, however, the Dutch have completely dominated them, and India would want that trend to continue on Sunday.
But rather than thinking too much about what may or may not happen in that match, India will have to focus on their own game against the Aussies.
âOur focus has to remain on ourselves because we have one very important match, and we are ready for it,â skipper Salima Tete said. âWe have to give everything we have because itâs our last match, against Australia, and we have to treat it like a final. 
We have a chance, and thatâs what I keep telling the team.â
So far, India have held China to a 2-2 draw, beaten South Africa 6-1, held England to a goalless draw and gone down to Netherlands 0-2. Their unbeaten streak may have come to an end on Friday night, but they put up another impressive showing and, if they can maintain that level against the Aussies, a win is certainly not beyond them.
Interestingly, India played four practice matches against Australia this year and did well against a team in transition. They lost the first match, won the second in a shoot-out after it finished 1-1 in regulation time, beat the hosts 2-0 in the third and then went down 2-3 in the fourth.
Speaking about Sundayâs match, India coach Sjoerd Marijne said, âWe see it as a quarterfinal. Itâs always very close (against Australia), and thatâs how I think the match on Sunday will be. There will not be many secrets because we play many times against each other.â
Having said that, the coach will still hope for one major change â India converting their chances. While they have been disciplined in defence, they havenât been able to maintain the same discipline in front of goal.
âAgainst big teams, if you get three opportunities, you have to convert one or two. Thatâs something we keep working on,â said the Dutchman. âItâs the same with penalty corners. At the moment we are not scoring off a lot of penalty cornersâ¦and we know that. 
But we have the quality, and I have confidence in Navneet (Kaur) and Deepika.â
And perhaps that is where Indiaâs biggest challenge â and their biggest opportunity â lies. They have shown they can stay in the contest against the best in the world. On Sunday, they will need to turn that resilience into goals.
India have done their bit before against the odds. Now, they need one more big performance â and a little help from Netherlands â to keep their World Cup dream alive.

title: Hockey World Cup: India's semifinal hopes end after 1-3 loss to Netherlands
content:
The Indian men's hockey team are out of the FIH World Cup semifinal race after losing 1-3 to reigning Olympic champions Netherlands in their second-round match on Saturday.
India needed a win to keep their last-four hopes alive, but a strong first half was followed by a difficult final quarter. The Netherlands scored twice in the last 10 minutes to seal the match.
Harmanpreet Singh
 scored India's only goal in the 52nd minute from a penalty corner. Duco Telgenkamp (41st), Tjep Hoedemakers (51st) and Thijs van Dam (55th) scored field goals for the Netherlands.
India will now play Argentina in their final second-round match on Monday before entering the fifth-eighth place classification matches.
India out of semifinal race
The defeat leaves India without a point in the second round. India had already lost to England in the first round, and even a victory against Argentina on Monday would take them to only three points.
That will not be enough to reach the semifinals.
India will instead play in the fifth-eighth place classification matches after their final second-round game against Argentina.
The result also means India are still waiting for their first World Cup win over the Netherlands. The Dutch defeated India in the penalty shootout in the 1973 World Cup final.
For India, a match that began with so much promise ended with disappointment as the Netherlands proved too strong in the decisive moments.
India start strongly
India played with control in the opening half and kept the Netherlands from building long periods of possession. The Indian defence was particularly impressive and did not allow the Dutch to create many clear chances.
India entered the Dutch circle from the right in the third minute, but the defenders quickly stopped the move.
Five minutes later, Rajinder Singh received a pass from Hardik Singh and carried the ball into the circle. Once again, India could not find a way through the Dutch defence.
The Netherlands had a chance in the 11th minute when van Dam tried a reverse hit from a pass from the left, but the ball came off the back of his stick.
Netherlands fail to convert penalty corners
The Netherlands earned the first penalty corner of the match in the 13th minute. Jip Janssen took the drag-flick, but Manpreet Singh made an excellent rushing block to keep India safe. The Netherlands then won three penalty corners in the opening minute of the second quarter, but could not convert any of them.
India also continued to look dangerous on the attack.
Meijer denies Dilpreet
India came close in the 24th minute.
Dilpreet Singh received the ball from Manpreet Singh and moved into the circle. He got an opportunity to shoot, but Dutch goalkeeper Meijer Derk made the save. Rajinder Singh was also in a position to make more of the rebound, but India could not take advantage. Neither team could find a goal before half-time as the score remained 0-0.
India miss penalty corner opportunity
India earned their first penalty corner in the 35th minute after taking a referral. Harmanpreet Singh's drag-flick hit the foot of the Netherlands' first rusher. India reviewed the decision and were awarded another penalty corner. But Harmanpreet's second attempt went wide. It was a missed opportunity for India, who had defended well and were also creating chances of their own.
Netherlands break the deadlock
The Netherlands finally found the opening goal in the 41st minute. India's defence, which had been so disciplined until then, switched off for a moment. Tijman Reyanga received the ball inside the circle and went for the shot. The ball took a deflection off Duco Telgenkamp's stick and went into the goal.
Indian goalkeeper Mohit had little chance to stop it.
India immediately looked for a response and earned a penalty corner, but Harmanpreet's drag-flick was saved by the Dutch goalkeeper.
Netherlands double their lead
India had another chance in the 47th minute when Abhishek earned a penalty corner. Harmanpreet was not on the field, so Amit Rohidas took the shot. His slap shot went wide after taking a deflection.
India reviewed the decision after the ball appeared to hit a Dutch defender's foot and were awarded another penalty corner. This time Sanjay took the shot, but the Dutch goalkeeper made another important save. India were being kept out despite their efforts.
The Netherlands then extended their lead in the 51st minute when Hoedemakers scored.
Harmanpreet gives India hope
India responded immediately.
Rajinder Singh won a penalty corner during a counter-attack, giving Harmanpreet another opportunity.
The Indian captain made no mistake this time.
His powerful drag-flick found the back of the net and gave India a lifeline.
India 1-2 Netherlands.
With the goal coming in the 52nd minute, India had a chance to fight their way back into the match.
Van Dam seals India's fate
But the comeback lasted only a few minutes. The Netherlands scored again in the 55th minute to restore their two-goal advantage. India's most experienced player, Manpreet Singh, lost possession and the ball fell to van Dam. The Dutch forward made no mistake and finished the chance.
India 1-3 Netherlands.
The goal effectively ended India's hopes of a comeback.

title: Abinaya Rajarajan breaks U20 national record with stunning 11.34s in Bhubaneswar
content:
Bhubaneswar: Abinaya Rajarajanâs comeback from injury had been a gradual one, with the 19-year-old Tamil Nadu sprinter steadily improving with every competition.
On Saturday, she produced the breakthrough she had been waiting for, clocking a stunning 11.34s to win the womenâs 100m title and break the U20 national record at the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meet at Kalinga Stadium here.
Abinaya bettered the previous mark of 11.53s set by Nipam Chauhan at the U20 Federation Cup earlier this year, capping a steady progression since returning from an injury that kept her out of training for nearly four months.
âIn the Czech Republic, I ran 11.58s. I was hoping to break the national record there, but because of my physical condition, I couldnât do it,â said the 19-year-old, who trains at NCOE Trivandrum under coach R Seenivasan and is currently the third fastest India after Dutee Chand (11.17s) and Rachita Mistry (11.34s).
âBut today I was fully fired up. I really wanted to run and break the under-20 national record. I didnât expect this, though. 11.34 is a crazy, crazy time.â
Abinaya had suffered the injury during the Asian Indoor Championships earlier this year and was forced to withdraw from the final. She then underwent an extended rehabilitation before gradually returning to competition. Her timings improved with every race, but the U20 national record remained elusive.
Her father, however, had spotted her natural speed much earlier.
âWe had a running race when we were out for a walk, and she beat me when she was six years old. Initially, I thought it was a fluke. The next day, I ran with full effort, but she was still faster than me. Thatâs when I realised she was talented,â said Rajarajan.
While the words of her coach and the support of her father helped her through the difficult period, visualization also played a big role in her recovery.
âVisualization was obviously a big part of it. I also kept thinking about the words of my coach during training. And my dad was a huge support. He has always been my hero,â said Abinaya. âEven when I was doing visualization, he would tell me, âDonât take any pressure. Run easily. Just run. Enjoy. I love you.ââ
And after finally producing the run, she had been chasing, Abinaya celebrated with Cristiano Ronaldoâs famous âSiuâ celebration to the delight of the fans. Abinayaâs record-breaking run apart, it was a strong day for Indian athletics.
Rohit Yadav put his Commonwealth Games disappointment behind him to win the menâs javelin title with a huge 87.68m throw in his final attempt, having taken a fall during his second attempt. Yashvir Singh, who won bronze at the CWG, finished second with a best throw of 82.94m.
Among the other big names of Indian athletics, Ancy Sojan won the womenâs long jump with a best leap of 6.71m, while Shaili Singh came second with an effort of 6.56m. Murali Sreeshankar clinched the menâs title with an effort of 8.07m, while Vithya Ramraj won the womenâs 400m with a personal best of 51.96s.
In the menâs 100m, Animesh Kujur and Gurindervir Singh clocked 10.32s and 10.39s respectively.
Among the foreign athletes, Nigeriaâs Commonwealth Games shot put champion Chukwuebuka Enekwechi won the title with a throw of 20.78m. In the womenâs discus throw, Jamaicaâs Commonwealth Games champion Samantha Hall finished second with a throw of 58.43m, while Brazilâs Andressa de Morais won with a penultimate-round throw of 58.66m.
However, it was a disappointing night for Jyothi Yarraji, who finished third in the womenâs 100m hurdles with a time of 13.24s and later pulled out midway into the 100m.

title: From tape-ball to 'dream of Harmanpreet’s wicket', Maryam follows her father’s dream
content:
Hong Kong vice-captain Maryam Bibi is preparing for one of the biggest challenges of her career as her team gets ready to face India in the Womenâs Asia Cup. For Maryam, the encounter is also a reminder of how far she and Hong Kong womenâs cricket have come.
Maryam's cricket journey began far away from the spotlight of international cricket. She started by playing tape-ball cricket with her father and continued playing the format during her primary-school years. It was only when she reached college and discovered hard-ball cricket that she decided to take the sport more seriously.
"I used to play tape-ball cricket with my dad and in primary school. When I went to college, we didn't have tape-ball cricket, we only had hard-ball cricket. For my enjoyment and loving cricket a lot, I wanted to try hard-ball cricket," Maryam told in an exclusive interview with Times of India.
That decision eventually opened the door to a career with Hong Kong. After helping her school team win a championship, Maryam decided to test herself at the national level. She began attending national training sessions alongside club cricket before eventually earning her place in the Hong Kong setup. 
Her early journey also included selection for the 2018 ASEAN Cup tour to Thailand.
âI had to work double hard in studies to play cricketâ
For Maryam, pursuing cricket was never simply about turning up for training. Like many young athletes, she had to balance sport with education, but the demands were particularly challenging.
"In Hong Kong, studies are very important, and managing studies and cricket training was difficult for me, because my mom had a rule that I need to pass my studies to play cricket," she said.
"I have to train early morning and then train evening. So, I need to manage my studies and cricket. Which was one of the biggest obstacles for me," she added.
Fatherâs unfinished dream became her motivation
Maryam credits her father as the biggest influence on her cricket career.
Her father had dreamed of representing the national team but was unable to fulfil that ambition because of personal circumstances. Maryam eventually decided to carry that dream forward herself.
"My dad has the biggest influence on me, because my dad's dream was to play for a national side, and he couldn't play due to some personal reasons, So, I wanted to lift up his dream, and by doing that, I started dreaming to play for Hong Kong team," she said.
'We got smashed' - but India A defeat became a lesson
Maryam has already experienced facing an Indian side, although it was India A, rather than the senior national team. Hong Kong played India A in the 2023 ACC Women's Emerging Teams Asia Cup. India A bowled Hong Kong out for just 34 before chasing the target in 5.2 overs to win by nine wickets. Shreyanka Patil took five wickets for two runs.
Maryam remembers the experience vividly.
"I remember India A coming to Hong Kong and playing Emerging Cup, and we got smashed, for sure. We scored like 36 runs or something, and they chased it down in four overs," she said.
But rather than allowing that defeat to define the team, Maryam believes it became an important learning experience.
"From that game, we had a lot of learnings and lessons we brought back, and in those two years' time, we focused on our fitness, skills and some of the analyst part of the game," she said.
Now, Hong Kong are preparing to face India's senior side, and Maryam believes the approach has to be simple despite the huge difference in experience.
"We know that they are world-class batters and experienced players over there. Our thinking is to play the ball and take them... don't take them lightly, but don't play just because they're an India team. Play it as a game of cricket," she said.
'Harmanpreet is my dream wicket'
There is one Indian wicket Maryam would love to have on her resume. Asked which Indian batter she would most like to dismiss, Maryam immediately picked 
Harmanpreet Kaur
.
"Harmanpreet Kaur, because I think she's my favourite, and she's my dream wicket. She's also a big player, a match-winner player, so I would love to dismiss her," she said.
Maryam's cricketing influences extend beyond India. She named Harmanpreet Kaur and Ellyse Perry as two players she admires for completely different reasons.
"I love the aggression she has, like, the passion for cricket," Maryam said of Harmanpreet.
On Perry, she added: "She's the calmest player I watched... her batting, the way she bats and bowls, and taking every situation very calmly. I just love the way she trains and carries herself on and out of the field."
'Itâs a huge responsibility' - Maryam on vice-captaincy
Maryam now occupies a leadership position within Hong Kong's women's team, serving as vice-captain. She sees the role not as a burden but as an opportunity to influence the next generation.
"I think it's a huge responsibility, and I think it's a privilege to have this responsibility. I never felt it's a burden," she said.
"As a player, I need to lead by example. I need to inspire young girls by setting an example for them, like how I train, how I am on and off the field, and how I can carry myself," she added.
Her ambition extends beyond results. She wants to help create a stronger cricketing culture in Hong Kong.
"I want Hong Kong cricket to be better, not just by result, but also the belief and the culture way," she said.
âSharing the pitch with India will inspire our girlsâ
Maryam believes playing against India can have an impact that goes far beyond the result. For Hong Kong's young players, sharing the stage with established international stars offers an opportunity to learn directly from the best and gain exposure to a much bigger audience.
"Sharing the pitch... and also getting to know them, and if we get a chance to talk, and sharing the experience what they have, and learning from them will really inspire most of the girls who are here," she said.
"It will also give our Hong Kong girls broadcast visibility and everything, so I feel like it will be a good growth for them," Maryam added.
While Maryam insists Hong Kong will give their best against all their opponents, she acknowledged that the clash against fellow associate side Thailand is a particularly important target.
"We should be doing our best in the three teams, but let's be honest about it, we are trying to put our best into the Thailand game," she said.
"My personal target will be to contribute in three departments, whether it's batting, bowling or fielding. I want to contribute... for a win. Any way possible, I'll contribute in all departments," she said.
Although bowling remains her favourite discipline, she has been spending more time with the bat in recent months.
"Honestly speaking, I love bowling, but the past few months I've been batting a lot, so I'm looking forward to bat more," she said.
For Maryam Bibi, therefore, the Women's Asia Cup is about more than simply facing one of the world's strongest teams. It is another chapter in a journey that began with tape-ball cricket alongside her father and has taken her to the Hong Kong national side and into a leadership role.

title: Dhols, chants and belief: How Delhi turned a World Championships semi-final into a homecoming
content:
NEW DELHI: Outside the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium on Saturday, the thermometer read 33 degrees Celsius. It wasn't difficult to break into a sweat. The road that had been largely empty throughout the week was bustling, and the question on most lips was, 'Where is Gate 7?', 'Bhaiya World Championships ke liye kaunsa gate hai?' [Which gate for the 
BWF World Championships
?]
Inside the 15,000-seater facility, half of which was in use for the tournament, the AC had been cranked up. Coincidentally, it matched the intensity and atmosphere of the crowd that had filled the stadium to the brim.
The occasion was the women's doubles semi-final featuring Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Pullela Gopichand. For the 64 minutes that the Indians battled in a three-game contest, winning the first game, the crowd stayed behind them every step of the way.
"Together we rise higher," read a poster from a young fan that was later presented to Jolly. The poster, featuring both players, said, "Two rackets. One Dream. One Nation," and that was the feeling inside the venue.
Treesa Jolly with a poster gifted by a young fan. (Photo Courtesy: Tanuj Lakhina)
"C'mon Pullela!" and "Jolly Jolly" rang out in sections whenever the Indian team earned a point. "Maar! Maar na!" echoed, without rehearsal, whenever the point was there for the taking and a smash looked inevitable. Equally loud were collective moans and "Noooos!" whenever the point went the way of the World No. 
1 and top seeds Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China.
Vadodara native Dr. Harshil was living every moment of it. After buying tickets weeks in advance, he took an overnight train from Gujarat and arrived earlier in the day for the World Championships. The fact that it was for a monumental occasion, India winning a medal for the 12th edition running, was a happy coincidence.
A packed Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium created an unforgettable atmosphere as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand battled China's top seeds in the BWF World Championships semi-finals. (Photo Courtesy:  BAI)
Dr. Harshil doesn't play badminton but stays abreast of the sport and watches every tournament on TV. Also a keen watcher of athletics, he was most enthused about the match featuring Chou Tien Chen and was inspired by the Taiwanese shuttler's battle and recovery from colorectal cancer.
But in that moment, as the vociferous crowd erupted and sat down near simultaneously, he couldn't keep his eyes away from Court 1.
The DJ would ring out at the breaks, celebrating every smash, every drop and every shot landing wide. As far as partisan crowds go, this was a living example. A set of dhols, placed in the second tier of the stadium, would make their presence felt every now and then.
India's Gayatri Gopichand Pullela clicks a selfie with spectators during the match between India and China in the women's doubles semifinal at the BWF Badminton World Championships at Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)
In the second set, as the Chinese pairing started to pick up the lead and took advantage of rising errors from the Indians, the crowd intensity, somehow, only got louder. The defiance of the Indians on the court was being matched by the decibel level of the crowd.
And by the third set, as the Chinese piled on the pressure, with the Indians losing their intensity and coherence, the crowd saw the effort wane. The fans had their voice at the start, but with the World No. 1s plucking points in a row, the spectators started to walk towards the exit doors.
'Focus. Believe. Together. Victory' also read the poster that Treesa carried with her. On the day, the crowd believed in the 23-year-old Indians. It came together, and in massive numbers. The victory, however, eluded them and the fans. But the venue, which had been the butt of jokes during the India Open in January, had just made itself count.

title: US Open leaves Stan Wawrinka out in the cold, denying former champion a wild card for his final Grand Slam
content:
US Open leaves Stan Wawrinka out in the cold, denying former champion a wild card for his final Grand Slam
The US Open has surprisingly denied Stan Wawrinka a wild card for what could be his final appearance at a Grand Slam.
Born into the greatest era in men’s tennis history, Stan Wawrinka spent almost two decades competing alongside the Big Three — Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic — as they dominated the sport.
Yet Wawrinka managed to carve out a legacy of his own. In an era when the Big Three rarely left major titles on the table, the Swiss won three Grand Slam titles, the last of them coming at the 2016 US Open.
A decade later, with Wawrinka in the final year of his professional career, the US Open has surprisingly denied him a wild card for what could be his final appearance at a Grand Slam.
The USTA announced its 2026 US Open wild cards in stages. Wawrinka appeared to be a strong candidate for one of the main-draw spots, having received wild cards at the other three Grand Slams this year. He eventually made the Roland Garros main draw after Lorenzo Musetti withdrew.
Gaël Monfils, who is also in the final year of his career, and Alexei Popyrin were awarded wild cards through the USTA’s reciprocal agreements with the French and Australian federations. Popyrin subsequently entered the main draw directly, meaning his wild card went to fellow Australian Dane Sweeny.
The USTA has reciprocal arrangements that require it to allocate one wild card to a French player and another to an Australian. The remaining places went to American players Michael Zheng, Martin Damm, J.J. Wolf, Sebastian Gorzny and Jack Kennedy, before the final wild card was handed to another American, Patrick Kypson, who is ranked 116th in the world.
Wawrinka’s exclusion is particularly surprising given his record at the US Open and his performances this year. All five of his Grand Slam matches in 2026 have been played in front of packed crowds. He lost in the opening round at Roland Garros and Wimbledon, but reached the third round at the Australian Open before losing to Taylor Fritz in four sets.
The US Open has also been Wawrinka’s most successful Grand Slam by win percentage. He has won 74% of his matches in New York, a record that includes his 2016 triumph over Djokovic in the final. He also reached the semi-finals in 2013 and 2015 and made the quarter-finals in 2010, 2014 and 2019.
Currently ranked outside the top 120, Wawrinka would need a wild card to avoid the qualifying rounds. It remains to be seen whether he will enter qualifying, which begins next week. There has also been no official word from Wawrinka on the decision.
Why did this happen?
There are practical reasons behind the decision. Two of the wild cards were allocated through the USTA’s existing reciprocal agreements with Tennis Australia and the French federation. Others were reserved for American juniors, college players and Next Gen Accelerator entrants.
With only a limited number of spots available, Wawrinka was not the only established name to miss out. Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori were also left without main-draw wild cards, with Nishikori receiving a qualifying wild card instead.
Still, the outcome feels strange.
Wawrinka is a three-time Grand Slam champion, a former US Open winner and a player who has enjoyed some of his finest moments in New York. Yet, in what is his final season, he has been left without a direct route into the main draw of the tournament he conquered a decade ago.

title: Real Madrid snatch late win at Espanyol on Mourinho's return
content:
Real Madrid snatch late win at Espanyol on Mourinho's return
Jose Mourinho's second spell in charge of Real Madrid began with a last-gasp 2-1 victory at Espanyol in La Liga on Saturday, with substitute Carlos Espi pouncing in the 90th minute to grab the winner.
Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in Los Blancos' opening fixture of the season, and new signing Espi secured the points at the death after Alex Calatrava had levelled against Mourinho's star-studded team.
"I think that we deserved to win but that Espanyol didn't deserve to lose," Mourinho told reporters.
"They didn't have any players at the World Cup and have been working together for a long time, and you could see that."
Back in charge of Madrid 13 years after leaving, Portuguese veteran Mourinho must bring the dressing room under control after the chaos of last season, and end Spanish champions Barcelona's domestic dominance.
Mourinho started with superstars Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Bellingham, as well as handing debuts to Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries and Ibrahima Konate.
Bellingham had an excellent first season at Madrid after arriving from Borussia Dortmund but the subsequent two were disappointing, both for him and the club, who failed to win a major trophy in either.
Mourinho installed him in attacking midfield with licence to roam and the former Birmingham man was heavily involved before his goal as Madrid probed.
The England international netted the first of Mourinho's second era at the club, heading home Arda Guler's dangerous crossed free-kick.
Espanyol threatened midway through the first half as Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois beat away Clemens Riedel's drive and Roberto Fernandez hooked over shortly afterwards.
Madrid did not heed the warning and Espanyol levelled in the 30th minute, Calatrava slotting home Javi Hernandez's cut-back after a fine team move.
- Intense battle -
Espanyol stopper Marko Dmitrovic made a good save to stop Mbappe after he got in behind on the right of the area.
The French forward, La Liga's top scorer in both of his two seasons at the club, was not at his lethal best in front of goal.
On the left flank Vinicius had little impact, beyond winning a series of fouls from Espanyol players who were determined to shut him down by any means.
Mourinho sent on two more new arrivals in the form of record signing Yan Diomande and Marc Cucurella as Madrid sought a winner in the final 25 minutes.
Federico Valverde hit the outside of the post with a low effort from the edge of the box as Espanyol dug deep to deny Madrid clear chances.
However in the 90th minute Madrid found the goal they needed when former Levante striker Espi, the lowest profile of Los Blancos' summer purchases, capitalised on a loose ball in the box and fired home.
"We carried out our plan well and then let in that goal at the end," said Calatrava.
"That we conceded was a gut-punch, because we worked hard until the end."
Earlier, Sevilla won 3-1 at Athletic Bilbao and Valencia and Celta Vigo drew 0-0.
On Sunday champions Barcelona play their first game of the season at Elche, while Atletico Madrid host Villarreal.

title: Serena Williams returns to US Open after four years, joins Carlos Alcaraz for mixed doubles
content:
Serena Williams returns to US Open after four years, joins Carlos Alcaraz for mixed doubles
Serena Williams will return to the US Open for the first time since 2022, partnering Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles after receiving a wildcard.
Serena Williams is set for another high-profile return to the US Open after being handed a mixed doubles wildcard alongside defending men's singles champion Carlos Alcaraz, creating one of the most eye-catching partnerships at this year's tournament. Tournament organisers confirmed on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz will compete together at Flushing Meadows, marking the 44-year-old American great's first competitive appearance at the US Open since 2022.
Williams, a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion, returned to competitive tennis earlier this year after nearly four years away from the professional circuit. Her latest appearance came alongside elder sister Venus Williams in the women's doubles at the Cincinnati Open, where the pair were beaten in the opening round by Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns. The Williams sisters had not played doubles together since the 2022 US Open before their Cincinnati comeback.
Serena Williams returns to familiar US Open stage
Flushing Meadows holds a special place in Serena's glittering career. She won six US Open singles titles and also lifted the mixed doubles trophy in New York in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi. Williams and Mirnyi also won the Wimbledon mixed doubles title that year, while she reached mixed doubles finals at Roland Garros in 1998 and the Australian Open in 1999. She later partnered with Andy Murray at Wimbledon in 2019, with the pair reaching the third round.
For Alcaraz, the partnership adds another layer to his own US Open comeback. The Spaniard, who won his first Grand Slam title in New York in 2022, has been sidelined for four months with a wrist injury and confirmed this week that he will return to defend his men's singles crown.
It will be only Alcaraz's second appearance in mixed doubles at a Grand Slam. He teamed up with Emma Raducanu at last year's US Open, but the pair were eliminated in the first round by Jessica Pegula and Jack Draper.
Williams and Alcaraz will enter a star-studded field featuring several blockbuster combinations. Aryna Sabalenka will partner with Novak Djokovic, while Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud return after reaching last year's final. Defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori are also in the draw. Mixed doubles qualifying begins on Monday, August 24, with the main draw starting a day later. The semifinals and final will be played at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday, August 26.

title: Maresca says Man City must fill Rodri void after Barca switch
content:
Maresca says Man City must fill Rodri void after Barca switch
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club must find a "new Rodri" after the departure of the influential midfielder to Barcelona this week.
Rodri, a World Cup winner and Ballon d'Or recipient, ended a seven-year spell at the Etihad Stadium during which he helped City win four Premier League titles and the Champions League.
His exit leaves a major gap in the squad Maresca inherited from Pep Guardiola, but the Italian is confident it can be filled.
"I'll try to find a new Rodri - it is what it is," said Maresca.
"Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things.
"Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.
"When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin arrived. When Sergio Aguero was here, everyone was worried - Erling arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It's just about this.
"When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one."
Rodri's departure is one of several notable exits from City during the close season, with Bernardo Silva, John Stones, Nathan Ake and Tijjani Reijnders also leaving the club.
Savinho is set to join Tottenham, potentially along with Omar Marmoush, and Nico Gonzalez could also depart before the transfer window closes.
City's only major signing so far has been midfielder Elliot Anderson, but Maresca said he expected further additions before the deadline and insisted he was unconcerned by the scale of the squad overhaul.
"Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do," Maresca said ahead of Sunday's Premier League opener against Bournemouth. "It doesn't help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.
"But we need to adapt and we don't want to keep players here that don't want to stay.
"The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.
"It's normal, I'm not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different."

title: Serena Williams teams up with Carlos Alcaraz for US Open mixed doubles comeback
content:
Serena Williams is set to make her return to the US Open in a blockbuster mixed doubles partnership with Carlos Alcaraz. The United States Tennis Association (USTA) announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz have received a wild card into the US Open mixed doubles main draw, with the event set to begin on Tuesday.
The partnership brings together two generations of Grand Slam champions and is expected to be one of the biggest attractions of this year's tournament.
Serena returns to Flushing Meadows
The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion will be back at the US Open for the first time since 2022. Williams returned to competitive tennis this summer after a break from the sport. She played singles at Wimbledon and later teamed up with her older sister Venus Williams in doubles at the Cincinnati Open.
It remains unclear whether Serena will also compete in the women's singles draw. The USTA still has one women's singles wild card available, although Williams has not confirmed whether she intends to use it.
Alcaraz returns after injury
Alcaraz, meanwhile, is set to return to action after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury. The Spaniard recently confirmed that he will defend his US Open singles title, making his mixed doubles partnership with Williams an additional attraction at Flushing Meadows.
The 2026 mixed doubles event will feature a revamped format designed to bring some of tennis' biggest stars into the competition. Matches will be played in a best-of-three format with sets decided at four games, no-ad scoring and a 10-point match tiebreak if required.
The winning team will also share a $1 million prize.
Star-studded mixed doubles field
Williams and Alcaraz are part of an impressive field featuring several high-profile combinations. Former world No. 1s Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic will form another headline pairing, while Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud are also set to compete.
American stars Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz will team up, while reigning champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori will return to defend their title.
For Williams, the US Open holds a special place in her career. She has won the tournament multiple times and previously captured the US Open mixed doubles title in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi.

title: Joe Burrow sends Bengals warning as rumored girlfriend Olivia Ponton’s Hawaii post sparks fan frenzy

While Cincinnati prepared for its Saturday night preseason matchup, Olivia Ponton gave her followers a glimpse of her Hawaii vacation on Instagram.
Olivia Ponton, who has been romantically linked to Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, is making the most of her final break before the 2026 NFL season gets underway.
Speculation surrounding Ponton and Burrow initially emerged in December 2024 after she was reportedly at the quarterback’s home when a burglary was reported. The dating rumors eventually resurfaced in 2026 when the two were seen together at the Kentucky Derby.
Their relationship appeared to become more public in August when Burrow and Ponton were spotted sharing a moment during a Bengals training camp session.
Ponton’s Hawaii post stuns fans
While Cincinnati prepared for its Saturday night preseason matchup, Ponton gave her followers a glimpse of her Hawaii vacation on Instagram.
Her post carried the caption, "Need a second opinion, should I post this?" and quickly attracted plenty of attention from fans. One commenter wrote, "god ur so perfect bro." Another reacted, "You look INSANEE." A third fan added, "Wow gorgeous ."

Sports Illustrated Swimsuit added her to its roster in 2022, and she has since appeared in two separate issues. Whether she will feature in the magazine again next May remains uncertain.

The Bengals have made significant changes to strengthen their roster. Cincinnati traded its No. 10 overall pick to the New York Giants in exchange for All-Pro nose tackle Dexter Lawrence II while also adding Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook, Jonathan Allen and Kyle Dugger in free agency.

title: Treesa-Gayatri lose BWF World Championships semifinal to China, settle for bronze
content:
Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand's remarkable run at the 
BWF World Championships
 came to an end in the semifinals as the Indian pair lost to China's top-seeded duo Tan Ning and Liu Sheng Shu in three games on Saturday. After producing one of the biggest wins of their careers in the quarterfinals, Treesa and Gayatri pushed the Chinese pair hard but eventually went down 21-18, 13-21, 8-21 in a contest that lasted 70 minutes.
Despite the semifinal defeat, the Indian duo will return home with a historic bronze medal, ending India's long wait for a World Championships medal in women's doubles.
Treesa-Gayatri make strong start
The Indians began the semifinal with confidence and held their nerve in a tightly contested opening game. With both pairs trading points, Treesa and Gayatri managed to stay ahead when it mattered most and eventually closed out the first game 21-18, moving within one game of a place in the World Championships final.
The Chinese top seeds, however, responded strongly in the second game.
Tan and Liu raised the intensity and began dictating the rallies, leaving the Indian pair struggling to find the same rhythm they had displayed in the opening game. 
The Chinese duo levelled the contest by taking the second game 21-13.
China dominate the decider
With everything to play for in the deciding game, Tan and Liu quickly established control. Treesa and Gayatri were unable to match the pace and precision of their opponents as the Chinese pair opened up a significant lead. The Indians tried to fight their way back into the contest, but Tan and Liu continued to dominate the crucial rallies.
The top seeds eventually closed out the decider 21-8 to book their place in the World Championships final.
While the defeat ended Treesa and Gayatri's hopes of reaching the final, their campaign has already secured their place in Indian badminton history. The pair became only the second Indian women's doubles combination to win a medal at the BWF World Championships, following Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa, who won bronze in 2011.
Their historic medal came after a stunning quarterfinal victory over world No. 4 Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian. Treesa and Gayatri recovered from losing the opening game to defeat the Chinese pair 16-21, 21-15, 21-13.
The young Indians' run also ended India's wait for a women's doubles Worlds medal spanning 15 years.

title: What led to high school football coach Adam Brubaker's firing? Video shows incident that injured student athlete | WATCH
content:
What led to high school football coach Adam Brubaker's firing? Video shows incident that injured student athlete | WATCH
The footage also appears to show several other adults rushing toward the player and confronting coach Adam Brubaker while the student received attention.
A high school football coach in Simi Valley has been dismissed after a school surveillance video showed him kicking a football that struck a student-athlete in the groin during a recent practice.
Coach fired after video emerges
The Simi Valley Unified School District reviewed the footage and subsequently fired Adam Brubaker as head football coach at Royal High School, according to Eyewitness News. His dismissal came only hours before Royal was scheduled to open its season on Friday.
Video captured by a camera on the school campus appears to show Brubaker visibly frustrated as he approached a player. He then kicked a nearby football, which struck another student in the groin and sent the player to the ground in pain.
Brubaker calls kick an accident
Deep Dive
"I kicked the ball and it hit him in the groin area and instantly I felt like I was going to pass out," Brubaker told Eyewitness News. "I feel obviously a great deal of remorse for what happened. It's a one in a million shot."
Brubaker maintained that the incident was accidental and insisted that he never intended to hit the player.
He explained that he had become angry after watching one player aggressively bring a running back to the ground during a drill, which he said was against the team's practice rules because of the potential injury risk.
The footage also appears to show several other adults rushing toward the player and confronting Brubaker while the student received attention.

Brubaker reiterated that he was not trying to kick the player and said he later approached him after practice to apologize.
"When we finished practice, I went back over to him. I apologized," Brubaker said.
Brubaker accepts district’s decision
Despite believing the kick was accidental, Brubaker said he understood why the district decided to remove him from his coaching position.
"Nothing has been harder in my life than the last three days. It has been an absolute trying time for me, my wife, my kids," said Brubaker.
Following his dismissal, Brubaker’s image was also removed from Royal High School’s football staff page. The position that had previously listed him as the varsity head coach now displays an empty image slot marked "Vacant."
